publicQuestions.question:
Hi there, could you please clarify the questions below:

RFI-01 - Appendix A lists inspection frequencies in addition to cleaning frequencies. Please confirm whether inspections are standalone visits, may be completed during scheduled cleans, and whether their time is included in the 30.75-hour estimate. eg. GSM Admin Bld - if the clean is to be completed twice per day x 4 times per week "0.5hrs per clean however 2 totals hrs allocated per week. means each clean would be only 0.25hrs or the total hours would be 4 per week. these goes for the another twice daily sites.

RFI-02 - Please clarify whether the additional 10 hours per week for supplementary cleans is a guaranteed paid allowance, a not-to-exceed contingent instruction, or an estimate to be priced as an hourly call-out rate. Please also confirm approval and invoicing protocol. Also the BBQ should be priced separetly or would be allocated in the designated hours.

RFI-03 - Please provide or confirm the Council-approved reporting platform, log-sheet template, photo-retention/privacy requirements, and Council CRM process for defects. Or would the contractor use their own internal rerting platform.?

RFI-04 - Please confirm the required sanitary-bin provider/service frequency, whether bins are to be supplied by the contractor, and all waste-disposal requirements/cost inclusions.

RFI-05 - Please clarify Council’s approved chemicals and consumables specifications/brands, dispenser formats and expected stockholding levels, or confirm whether the contractor is to submit a proposed list for approval.

RFI-06 - Please confirm service windows, key/access arrangements, alarms, water/power availability, parking, and any event/holiday uplift requirements for each facility.

RFI-07 - Please define “deep cleaning as required”, identify expected triggers/frequency, and confirm whether it is included in routine price, supplementary hours, or a separately instructed rate. Eg. Graffiti removal would be under deep cleaning or adhoc?

RFI-08 - Please confirm whether Council expects one contractor to cover all facilities or may award multiple contracts, and state the anticipated commencement date/mobilisation period.
publicQuestions.answer:
Hi, thankyou for your questions. Please see answers below.

RFI-01: Inspections would be required at least daily at the sites noted. These may be conducted stand-alone or as part of a scheduled clean. Contractor will be required to return to site to clean outside of scheduled cleans if requested due to high usage or incident or verified community complaint. Negotiation over inspections to account for travel time and to ensure efficiencies can take place at contracting stage.

RFI-02: Supplementary cleans have been included as a contingency to be used as required. BBQ cleaning included in site designated hours. Invoices to be submitted with Monthly Performance Report by 5th business day of each calendar month.

RFI-03: Council uses the Civica Authority and Reflect platforms for CRMs and task verification. Access details to these platforms along with log sheet templates, etc will be provided to successful contractor.

RFI-04: Sanitary bin provision and servicing to be determined/subject to negotiation. Can be included in quote if you wish.

RFI-05: Contractor to supply a proposed list of chemicals for approval.

RFI-06: Service windows would generally be 6am-5pm daily. All sites have parking, water and power. Event/holiday/high-demand requirements subject to negotiation with successful contractor.

RFI-07: Deep cleaning may be required periodically. This can be negotiated with contractor. Indicative rates may be provided. Graffiti and maintenance issues are reporting only – see 3.3 in the RFQ.

RFI-08: Anticipated commencement date is 4Q 2026, subject to successful contracting. Multiple contracting may be considered, although preference is for a single contractor.

** ABOUT THE BEGA VALLEY **

The Bega Valley Shire is located at the south-eastern corner of New South Wales, halfway between Australia’s two largest cities, Sydney and Melbourne and three hours’ drive from the nation’s capital, Canberra.

Our coastal fringe extends from Wallaga Lake in the north to Cape Howe and the Victorian border in the south. Collectively this 225-kilometre section forms the beautiful Sapphire Coast, the heart of Australia’s Coastal Wilderness.

Our community vision explains our collective aspiration that we are an inclusive and welcoming community that integrates quality of life, prosperity, sustainable development and conservation of the environment. Our connection to Country is guided by the culture and heritage of our Traditional Owners.

** ABOUT COUNCIL **

Bega Valley Shire Council is responsible for providing all of the typical local government services across the Bega Valley Shire including maintaining a broad range of assets valued at over $1.7 billion that allow our visitors and community alike to live, work and play.

The Bega Valley Shire is governed by an elected Council comprising nine Councillors. Councillors provide leadership and establish policy and strategic direction for the organisation and the future of the shire.

Delivering the day to day services for council is a professional and dynamic staff cohort of over 560 people including full time, contract and casual positions.

Contractors to council play an important and valued role, assisting us delivering services and projects to the highest of standards and value for money.

** WHAT COUNCIL DOES **

Provide and maintain community facilities such as:
•	Parks and sportsgrounds
•	Playgrounds and skate parks
•	Sapphire Aquatic centre Pambula and swimming pools throughout the shire
•	Sports and recreation facilities throughout the Shire
•	Local libraries in Bega, Bermagui, Eden and Merimbula
•	Preschools and Childcare centres in Bega and Eden, and our Mobile service for Candelo and Bemboka
•	Merimbula Airport, Bega Saleyards and Cemeteries throughout the Shire

We care for the environment by:
•	Managing and enhancing bushland areas
•	Providing environmental and waste education and recycling services
•	Responding to pollution incidents and prosecuting polluters
•	Monitoring the water quality of the Shire’s estuaries
•	Planting trees and controlling noxious weeds
•	Beneficially recycling and reusing treated effluent

We create a safer place to live by:
•	Maintaining and improving roads, footpaths and stormwater drains
•	Working with emergency organisations such as the Rural Fire Service, State Emergency Service, NSW Police and NSW Surf Life Saving
•	Managing the keeping of companion animals
•	Inspecting food premises
•	Treating and supplying drinking water to our community
•	Treating sewage to a high standard to protect human health

We enhance our community by:
•	Listening to community views
•	Holding citizenship ceremonies, Australia Day Celebrations and the Seniors week luncheon known as the Golden Gig
•	Offering services for seniors, young people, new migrants and people with a disability
•	Providing grants to community organisations
•	Supporting local community groups such as sporting clubs, arts, migrant groups and charities
•	Encouraging and promoting volunteering in our communities

We plan for the future by:
•	Planning and managing the urban environment
•	Preserving heritage sites
•	Consulting with the community about its needs
•	Developing long term strategic plans for Council and the Shire

publicQuestions.question:
Thank you for the opportunity to quote. The following clarifications are sought, and it is requested that responses be circulated to all Respondents.

Information to be provided

Schedule 1 provides the Rosny to Otago Stormwater System Management Plan as Attachment No. 1 for information only, while scope item (c) requires the provision of updated flood models. We have assumed the updated models are to be prepared in TUFLOW to align with the existing modelling, and that the GHD TUFLOW model will be made available at award in re-runnable form, including geometry, boundaries, roughness, virtual pipes, DEM and log files. Could Council confirm this, and confirm that Council holds the intellectual property in the model or a licence from GHD permitting its reuse and adaptation?

Pricing Schedule

The geotechnical investigation program is prepared by the Consultant and tabled at the Inception Meeting under Schedule 1 item (d). Would Council consider making Pricing Schedule Item 3 a provisional item, so that the sum is adjusted to the agreed program and the actual investigation cost?

Schedule 1 item (h) requires documenting and gaining approval from the relevant service providers for any service relocations required by the works. Whether relocations are required, and the extent of any relocation, cannot be determined until the detailed survey and potholing are complete. title: REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL 20.26 AIRPORT ADVERTISING LICENSE
description:
The Shire of Ashburton (Shire) invites proposals from suitably qualified and experienced advertising organisations for the provision, management, marketing, sale and ongoing maintenance of advertising opportunities at Onslow Airport and within the surrounding airport precinct.

1.1	Summary of Opportunity

The Shire intends to identify a single advertising organisation (with whom to progress negotiations) at the conclusion of this Request for Proposal process.

The successful Respondent will enter into an exclusivity period of 2 months to endeavour to negotiate a potential licence agreement for advertising space at the Onslow Airport for a 5 year term with an option to extend the term for two (2) x 2 year option periods at the sole discretion of the Shire of Ashburton. It is intended that under this licence agreement (if granted) the successful Respondent will be responsible for developing, installing, managing and commercialising advertising assets across approved locations within the airport environment.

Subject to the terms of the licence agreement and also subject to the Local Government Act 1995 (WA) (LGA) (including s3.58 of the LGA), the successful Respondent will be granted advertising rights to market, sell, manage and maintain approved advertising opportunities within specific agreed locations in the Onslow Airport and the surrounding airport precinct, excluding those areas specifically identified within this RFP (see section 4.2).

The Shire is seeking an innovative and commercially focused partner capable of maximising the value of the airport's advertising opportunities while enhancing the passenger experience and maintaining the high presentation standards of the airport precinct. Respondents are encouraged to present creative and contemporary advertising solutions, including both traditional and digital advertising formats, that are appropriate for a regional airport environment.

The successful operator will demonstrate the ability to attract and retain advertisers, generate sustainable revenue streams, and deliver high-quality advertising infrastructure that complements the airport's role as a key gateway to the Ashburton region. The Shire may, following evaluation of submissions, select a preferred Respondent and enter into an exclusivity period during which time the Shire and preferred Respondent will seek to finalise an in-principle licence agreement without undertaking any further request for tender or quotation process.

One of the first standalone mountain bike clubs in Australia we formed in 1984 and has been a staple part of the Australian mountain bike scene ever since.

CTMBC is in charge of grant funding to build the Lithgow Mountain Bike Transformation Project, funded by the Department of Regional NSW.
vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Tuesday 08 September 2026 05:00 PM (AUS Eastern Standard Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background:
In mid-2022 CTMBC was awarded grant funding by the NSW Department of Regional NSW to develop approximately 25 km of purpose-built single-track and establish a mountain bike park adjacent to Lithgow at State Mine Gully. The project is co-funded, with National Parks and Wildlife Service (NPWS) providing a co-contribution directed to adjacent car parks, walking and bike tracks on the National Park estate, and additional Australian Government funding contributing to the broader program in 2025. Grant funds are held in trust by Keystone Lawyers as escrow agent and disbursed to suppliers as approved and as required.

Development consent for the mountain bike park was granted on 10 August 2026 under DA170/25 (Western Regional Planning Panel reference PPSWES-324). The trail alignments have been designed by World Trail Pty Ltd and are an approved plan under the consent.

Activities to obtain the Construction Certificate are underway and are expected to be completed by November 2026. While the Construction Certificate is a prerequisite to construction commencing, the development application was by far the most difficult activity and is now approved. Subject to those remaining conditions, the project is free to proceed.

This EOI relates to Package 1 — the State Mine Gully (excluding National Park) trail network, being approximately 24.5 km of the 37.6 km total network. The remaining approximately 13.1 km sits within the Gardens of Stone State Conservation Area and is a separate NPWS-funded and NPWS-delivered workstream that is not part of this procurement.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
After four years of planning, assessment and collaboration, the Club is celebrating an approval that marks a major milestone for a project that has navigated a complex planning and environmental assessment process involving multiple agencies, extensive technical studies and broad stakeholder engagement.

The consent unlocks approximately 25 kilometres of purpose built bike and walking trails, within the State Mine Gully precinct commencing from the State Mine Heritage Park and reachable in two hours from Sydney by road, and served directly by passenger rail. It is the link the whole vision depended on, connecting the Lithgow town centre directly to the trail network, so that riders arrive in town, stay in town, and spend in town.

The trail network will play a key role in connecting Lithgow to some of Australia’s most spectacular natural landscapes, helping establish the city as a gateway to both the Gardens of Stone and Wollemi National Parks.

The trails are designed for everyone from first time riders to experienced descenders, with network design by leading international mountain bike trail designers World Trail. Designed for riders and visitors of all abilities, the network will provide new opportunities for outdoor recreation, nature based tourism and community wellbeing while showcasing the region’s unique landscapes and heritage. For a town built on coal and steel, it is a genuinely new chapter: a former industrial landscape becoming a destination in its own right

title: Design & Construction - Two (2) Bedroom Modular Dwellings - Yarrabah ASC
description:
The Scope is described in the document(s) attached to or provided with this Request for Quotation and identified as:

Scope of Works (Design & Construct)

The Contractor shall undertake the complete design of new residential Modular dwellings at 13 Smith Street and Bulguru Park, Yarrabah with the following design required for council approval –

Tenderers are required to provide separate lump-sum pricing for the following options and Locations:

13 Smith Street, Yarrabah

•	Option 1 – Two (2) Modular Homes: Total lump-sum price for the supply and delivery of two (2) modular homes.

•	Option 2 – Three (3) Modular Homes: Total lump-sum price for the supply and delivery of three (3) modular homes.

Pricing for each option is to represent the complete cost applicable to that quantity, including any applicable economies of scale, bulk purchasing discounts, shared mobilisation, transport, preliminaries or other cost efficiencies.

However, Council reserves the right, at its sole discretion and subject to available funding, to proceed with either Option 1 or Option 2.

Bulguru Park, Yarrabah

•	Two (2) Modular Homes: Total lump-sum price for the supply and delivery of two (2) modular homes.

Design Requirements / Preferred Layout Outcomes

Tenderers are to incorporate the following design considerations within the proposed dwelling layouts, noting these items are preferred outcomes and not limited to the below:

•	Modular Dwellings to include Two (2) bedrooms, with Kitchen, bathroom, WC toilet, and Laundry and any other requirements to ensure they are Platinum level minimum as per Remote Housing Standards

•	Individual Driveways to the dwellings

•	Vehicle parking areas to include colour matched fencing, screening or similar treatments to improve privacy, security and streetscape presentation.

•	Kitchen and/or lounge room preferred toward the street facing side of the dwelling to improve outlook, passive surveillance and natural light.

•	Dining area to provide practical connection between kitchen and living areas with efficient internal flow.

•	Laundry to be located towards the rear of the dwelling with direct access to patio / outdoor area for functionality.

•	Adequate internal linen storage to be provided, centrally located and practical for day to day household use.

•	Overall design to prioritise privacy, functional living, efficient use of site area, and a high quality residential presentation suited to the local environment.

•	The design must conform with Remote Housing Standards and be minimum of Platinum Level in all aspects.

•	Design and Construction to incorporate the Yarrabah Aboriginal Shire Council House Fencing Standards 2024 – which is attached as part of this RFT.

The Works include, but are not limited to, all labour, materials, plant, equipment, design, approvals and activities necessary to deliver a fully operational, compliant and complete housing development fit for purpose and ready for handover and occupation.

Payment Terms

Payment terms are done via progress claims every 21 Days or at agreed payment intervals.

Key Requirements

•	The Contractor is responsible for the complete design development, coordination and certification of the Works.

•	The Contractor shall ensure the Works comply with all applicable legislation, codes, standards and authority requirements.

•	The Works shall be delivered as a complete and functional development, notwithstanding any omissions or discrepancies in the reference documentation.

•	A mandatory Indigenous Employment and Business Participation (IEBP) Plan shall be submitted with the Tender. Failure to submit an IEBP may result in the Tender being deemed non-conforming.

•	Design and Construction must be minimum of Platinum Level as per the Design and Construction standards for Remote Housing.

•	Dwelling must be able to be moved from the property at a later date(10 Years plus) if needed.

•	Property to be raised to acceptable FFL requirements as per Yarrabah Aboriginal Shire Council.

Scope of Works

Without limiting the Contractor’s obligations, the Works include but are not limited to:

Design & Approvals

•	Detailed building designs of all dwellings and associated infrastructure

•	Modular Style homes must be Platinum Level Minimum as per the Design & Construction Standards for Remote Housing.

•	Design coordination across all disciplines

•	Preparation of all documentation required for construction, approvals and certification

o	The Contractor must submit SD stage drawings to Council for feedback and approval prior to progressing to CD.

•	Obtaining all approvals, permits and authority clearances

Site Establishment & Civil Works

•	Site establishment, access, temporary services and controls

•	Clearing, grubbing, demolition if required and site preparation (demolition of existing dwellings is excluded from this tender)

•	Bulk earthworks, cut and fill, trimming and compaction incl. testing if applicable

•	Set-out of all works in accordance with approved design and issued FFLs

•	Stormwater drainage, overland flow management and lawful discharge

•	Geotechnical woks will be undertaken by the successful tender.

Residential Construction

•	Construction of Modular dwellings in accordance with nominated house types

•	Modular Home Style. Must be able to be detached and moved if needed.

•	Complete construction of each dwelling including all structural, architectural and building elements necessary to achieve a fully functional and compliant dwelling

•	Supply and installation of all fixtures, fittings and appliances

•	Kitchens, bathrooms and laundries including joinery

Services & Utilities

•	All hydraulic services including water, sewer and drainage

•	Electrical reticulation, metering, switchboards and internal installations

•	Communications and data provisions as typically required

•	Coordination and connection to mains

External & Ancillary Works

•	Driveways, pathways, hardstand areas and access ways

•	Fencing, gates and boundary treatments

•	Reinstatement and making good of all disturbed areas

•	Installation of external fixtures including T-Bar clotheslines, external sink and bins

Testing, Commissioning & Handover

•	Testing and commissioning of all services and systems

•	Rectification of defects and completion of outstanding works

•	Provision of as-constructed documentation, manuals and warranties

•	Final certification and approvals for occupancy

•	Handover of a complete, operational and compliant development

Contractor Obligations

•	The Contractor shall verify all site conditions, dimensions, levels and service locations prior to commencing Works.

•	The Contractor shall be deemed to have allowed for all conditions that may reasonably be anticipated from available information and site inspection.

•	No claim will be accepted for matters arising from failure to adequately investigate site conditions or coordinate the Works.

•	The Contractor is responsible for all coordination, interfaces and integration of the Works, whether expressly stated or reasonably inferred.

Project Specification

•	National Construction Code (NCC)

•	Design & Construction Standards for Remote Housing

Documents Provided

•	Geotechnical Data – 13 Smith Street

•	386262-4 L147 Smith Survey Data

•	13 Smith St_DFL_Topography

•	13 Smith St_Unit 1_DFL_Topography

•	13 Smith St_Unit 3_DFL_Topography

•	YASC_2026_021 – YASC Housing Fence Standards

The Contractor shall comply with the current edition of the National Construction Code (NCC), all applicable Australian Standards (AS/NZS), and all relevant statutory and regulatory requirements.

It shall be the Contractor’s responsibility to identify and comply with all standards applicable to the Works, whether they are specifically listed in this document.

Tenders are invited for the Statutory Planning Public Notice Installation Service.

Council is seeking submissions from suitably qualified and experienced contractors for the provision of public notification signage services associated with statutory planning applications. The services include the production, installation, maintenance, inspection and removal of public notice signs at locations throughout the municipality, in accordance with Council requirements and relevant legislative obligations.

The successful contractor will be required to provide a reliable, responsive and customer-focused service that supports Council’s statutory planning processes. Tenderers will be expected to demonstrate their experience in delivering similar services, their capacity to meet service timeframes, quality assurance processes, reporting capabilities, and commitment to workplace health and safety. The City of Stonnington is a local government area located within the metropolitan area of Melbourne, Australia. It comprises the inner south-eastern suburbs, between 3 and 13 km (2 and 8 mi), from the Melbourne CBD. The city covers an area of 25.7 km2 (9.9 sq mi).

Within twenty years of the settlement of Melbourne in 1835, the Prahran Municipality (later City of Prahran) was formed in 1855, followed by the Gardiner Road Board (later City of Malvern) in 1856.

The late 19th century saw substantial residential and commercial development such that by 1891 Prahran had a population of almost 40,000 and Malvern 11,000. Following the election of the Kennett government in the Spring of 1992, as part of a comprehensive reorganisation of local government in Victoria, the Cities of Malvern and Prahran were amalgamated to form the City of Stonnington.

publicQuestions.question: Can you please explain the journey and processes the jockey takes on race day through the jockey administration building from start to finish? Including where they enter and exit, and if the jockey needs to sign-in and sign-out at Reception upon entrance and leaving?
publicQuestions.answer:
Please see the information provided below for information:

With regards to the Stewards’ Room, the media truck currently hooks up in the Stewards’ Room a couple of hours prior to the start of each Raceday. PRC is checking whether there are any requested changes from the media truck to see if there are any suggestions on how this process can be streamlined. Tenderers are requested to take this into consideration.

 Jockey Processes and Movements

1. Jockey Arrival and Movement

Upon arrival at the racecourse, jockeys report to the Clerk of Scales, who is employed by RWWA, to advise that they have arrived and surrender their mobile phone for the day.

They then proceed to the jockey locker/change rooms. There are separate male and female locker rooms, with associated showers.

Once changed, jockeys generally remain in the Jockeys’ Lounge until they are called for their race.

A doorbell/alert system is currently located in each locker room to notify jockeys when they are required to come out for race preparation.

When called, jockeys leave the locker/lounge area and report to the Clerk of Scales, where those riding in the upcoming race are weighed before proceeding to the mounting yard.

The layout should allow this movement to occur efficiently without trainers, barrier staff, presenters or other personnel needing to move through the jockeys’ private areas.

2. Jockeys’ Lounge & Kitchenette

Required kitchenette facilities:

-Sink

-Bench space for a slow cooker and microwave

-Full-size refrigerator

-Under-bench storage for crockery and cutlery

-Room for: Toaster, Toasted sandwich maker, Kettle, Microwave, Slow cooker

Jockeys will need room for lounge chairs & dining table in this area. Usually 30-36 Jockeys each raceday (Some will only have one race). There will also be a notice Board to pin up raceday information sheets here.

3. Jockey Massage Area

There is currently a small massage area adjacent to the jockey locker rooms.

This should be retained in the new design, with appropriate privacy and convenient access from the jockey facilities.

4. Clerk of Scales

The Clerk of Scales room should remain the central operational point for the jockey facilities.

The Clerk of Scales is the first point of contact for jockeys arriving at the racecourse and is responsible for the weighing process.

The area needs to accommodate:

- Clerk of Scales workstation with notice Board to pin up raceday information sheets

- Jockey arrival/check-in

-Phone collection and secure storage

-Jockey weighing process

-Interaction with jockeys immediately before they proceed to the mounting yard

-Access to the Scales Assistant and saddle/saddle cloth storage

5. Saddles and Saddle Cloths

Trainers need to collect saddle cloths before each race.

Saddle cloths are distributed by the Scales Assistant and are currently stored in large pigeonholes adjacent to the Clerk of Scales.

There is normally a divider/barrier between the trainers and the saddle cloth storage, preventing trainers from simply helping themselves to saddle cloths.

The new design should retain this controlled distribution arrangement, allowing:

Scales Assistant ? Saddle Cloth Storage ? Trainer Collection without trainers having unrestricted access to the storage area.

6. Trainer and Barrier Staff Waiting Area

A waiting area is required for trainers and barrier staff who are waiting prior to each race.

This area could be positioned adjacent to the Clerk of Scales but should not interfere with jockey circulation or the weighing process.

The external side of the building should also provide a gated common area leading towards the mounting yard. Jockeys will go through this area to access the mounting yard.

This area will function as a common waiting/holding area for:

Trainers

Barrier staff

Television presenters

Other race-day personnel requiring access to the mounting yard

7. Stewards’ Area

A dedicated Stewards’ area is required immediately adjacent to the Clerk of Scales.

The room should be approximately boardroom-sized, allowing for up to six RWWA Stewards on a Raceday.

The room will be used for:

-Steward meetings

-Race-day operations

-Reviewing race footage

-Conducting steward enquiries

-Discussions with jockeys, trainers and other participants when required

The room should therefore have sufficient space and privacy to conduct formal enquiries without disrupting the general race-day operation.

Stewards’ technology and equipment requirements

The room will require:

-Up to four large television screens

-Numerous electrical power outlets

-Numerous Ethernet/data outlets

-Suitable locations for screens and associated equipment

-Adequate desk/boardroom table space for up to six Stewards

-A refrigerator for food and drinks supplied by the Race Club

The power and Ethernet requirements should be considered at the design stage rather than relying on extension leads or temporary cabling on Racedays.

The key consideration is that the Clerk of Scales should sit centrally between the jockey facilities, saddle/saddle cloth distribution, Stewards’ area and access towards the mounting yard.

publicQuestions.answer:
RFI 1 – Approval of Nominated Subconsultants

Response:

Tenderers are referred to Clause 3.4.1 of the Tenderer’s Offer Form, together with the subconsultant requirements of the RFT and the relevant provisions of the Consultancy Agreement.

The Principal intends to review the Tenderer’s nominated subconsultants as part of the tender evaluation process, having regard to the information provided in the Tender. The Principal nevertheless reserves its rights under the RFT and Consultancy Agreement in relation to the approval of subconsultants. The RFT requires Tenderers to identify proposed subconsultants and provides that the Consultant remains responsible for their performance.

Where the Principal does not accept a nominated subconsultant, the Tenderer/Consultant will be required to promptly nominate a suitably qualified and experienced alternative for the Principal’s approval. No fixed timeframe applies; however, this is to occur without unreasonable delay and so as not to adversely affect the Project programme.

Consistent with Clause 3.4.1 of the Tenderer’s Offer Form, Tenderers should allow for any replacement of a nominated subconsultant required through this approval process without adjustment to the tendered fee.

If, following appointment, the Principal requires a change that materially alters the agreed scope of Services or gives rise to circumstances outside the requirements contemplated by the RFT, any associated cost or programme implications will be considered in accordance with the variation provisions of the Consultancy Agreement. No adjustment to the Contract Price or programme will apply unless approved in writing by the Principal.

Except as clarified above, the requirements of the RFT, Scope of Works, Tenderer’s Offer Form, Consultancy Agreement and issued Addenda remain unchanged.

________

RFI 2 – Development Approval Pathway

Tenderers are referred to Clause 4.3 – Planning and Statutory Approvals, Clause 7 – Programme and Milestones, Clause 9 – Principal’s Responsibilities and Clause 10 – Exclusions and Additional Services of the Scope of Works, together with Addendum No. 1.

The Principal is not prescribing at tender stage whether the Project will proceed by way of a new Development Application, an amendment to Development Approval P140/2022, or continued reliance on the existing approval where legally available.

As set out in Clause 4.3 of the Scope of Works, the successful Consultant is required to review the existing Development Approval and current project information, determine the applicable statutory approval pathway and advise the Principal whether a new Development Application, amendment to an existing approval or other statutory approvals are required.

Addendum No. 1 also confirms that the Development Approval documentation previously provided remains available for reference and consideration in relation to the previous approval and statutory approval pathway. The concept drawings subsequently issued with Addendum No. 1 represent the current concept information for the purposes of the RFT.

For tender pricing purposes, Tenderers are to allow within their lump sum for the professional services necessary to determine and progress the applicable planning approval pathway, including preparation and coordination of a new Development Application or amendment to the existing Development Approval if required.

Any Development Application or amendment is to address the Project works requiring planning approval and have regard to both Separable Portion 1 and Separable Portion 2. The documentation is to preserve the Principal’s ability to proceed with Separable Portion 1 only or both separable portions in accordance with the RFT.

The Project programme contemplates the planning and statutory approval process occurring prior to construction. Tenderers are required to develop their proposed programme having regard to the applicable approval pathway and anticipated authority assessment periods, with the objective of supporting construction commencement following completion of the major race meetings at the end of March 2027. Tenderers should identify any approval-related programme risks or constraints in their submission. The Scope expressly requires the Consultant to prepare the consultancy programme, identify critical path activities and integrate statutory approvals with the required Project programme.

Tenderers are to include within their lump sum the consultant services, documentation and supporting specialist inputs reasonably identifiable from the RFT documentation as necessary to progress the applicable Development Application or amendment. If, following appointment and confirmation of the statutory pathway, additional investigations or specialist services are required that were not reasonably identifiable at the time of appointment, these will be dealt with in accordance with the Additional Services provisions of the Scope of Works.

Statutory application fees, authority fees and other third-party statutory fees will be paid by the Principal in accordance with Clause 9 of the Scope of Works.

Except as clarified above, the requirements of the RFT, Scope of Works, Tenderer’s Offer Form, Consultancy Agreement and issued Addenda remain unchanged.

publicQuestions.question:
Will the Principle consider or allow the following:

1.The submission of an alternate or accompanying format price file, for the following reasons:

 a) The Items requested in the price file are quite generalised and will potentially limit the principles’ ability to choose the most appropriate product available, or limit the supplier’s

ability to recommend the most suitable product

b) By allowing alternate or accompanying price/product files, more options will be available to the principle, increasing the ability to achieve a desired result

c) By allowing an alternate format, suppliers will likely be able to update the principle on price variations in a more detailed manner

2. Quarterly updates to product/price files, for the following reasons:

a) Many specified products will fall under agency platforms, meaning price changes and timings will be dictated to by the product suppliers and not the tender suppliers

b) Volatility in fertiliser pricing on the back of the middle east conflict

publicQuestions.answer:
Dear Tenderer,

Thank you for your enquiry regarding SSROC T2026-02 Supply and Delivery of Agricultural Products Services Tender.

In response to your specific questions:

1.	The RFT already contemplates this scenario. Tenderers are reminded of the following provisions that remain in effect:

The Pricing Schedule (Form 7) contained within Part 3-2 Mandatory Returnable Schedules must be completed in full using the prescribed Excel format. The RFT expressly states that “Tenderers must not alter the contents or formatting of the Pricing Schedule, other than to include additional line items where relevant or referred to in the pricing table.” Accordingly, the prescribed Form 7 remains a mandatory conforming requirement and cannot be omitted or replaced.

At the same time, the RFT expressly encourages innovation, stating that “Tenderers are encouraged to submit innovative or alternative ways of servicing this contract.” An alternate or supplementary product/price file may be submitted, provided that:

a.	A fully compliant and conforming Tender, including a completed Form 7, is submitted in the first instance.

b.	The alternate or supplementary file is submitted through Form 22 (Summary of Alternative Tenders) as an alternative or supplementary submission and is clearly identified as such.

c.	The supplementary file is cross-referenced to the relevant line items contained in Form 7.

d.	The alternate file does not replace or contradict the conforming schedule and may only be submitted as a supplement to it.

Tenderers are also reminded that the basket of goods contained in Form 7 is recognised within the RFT as a generic and representative basket only and is not intended to encompass all products that may be procured under the Agreement. Councils may engage Preferred Suppliers for items outside the basket through the SSROC Vendor Panel at the rates and conditions agreed under the PSMA.

2. This matter is governed by the Preferred Supplier Master Agreement (PSMA).

The RFT states that "the Agreement Terms and conditions of pricing, price variations and replacement costs are stipulated in the Preferred Supplier Master Agreement (PSMA)" (Part 4 of the RFT). Tenderers are directed to review the draft PSMA in full.

The formal contract review mechanism includes an Annual Contract Review Report, which encompasses pricing review and market benchmarking as standard components. This represents the primary structured mechanism for price file updates under the Agreement.

Tenderers wishing to propose departures from the pricing variation provisions of the draft PSMA — including any proposal for more frequent (e.g. quarterly) price reviews — are invited to do so via Form 6 (Proposed Contract Departures) in the Part 3-1 Returnable Schedules. Any such departure will be considered by SSROC on its merits and may be subject to negotiation following evaluation. Proposed departures will not render a tender non-conforming, but the Principal reserves the right to accept, reject, or negotiate any proposed departure.

Tenderers proposing a quarterly mechanism are encouraged to include in their Form 6 submission the specific categories or product lines for which the departure is sought, the proposed triggering criteria, and any suggested guardrails (e.g. CPI or index caps, notice periods), to facilitate the Principal's assessment.

Should you require any further clarification, please submit your questions through the tender portal in accordance with the tender process and timelines outlined in the tender documentation.

We thank you for your interest in this opportunity and look forward to receiving your submission.

The proposal is to complete all external refurbishment works to meet current compliance and avoid expensive maintenance issues in the future. The proposed works will align with the extensive engineering reports, and Heritage approved Architectural design completed in 2024.

Works will include, but are not limited to:

•	Veranda and Balustrade Upgrades

•	Asbestos Removal

•	New Waterproof Protection (Level 1 - Veranda Deck)

•	External Lighting Upgrades

•	Replacement of Fire Stairs

•	New Covered Walkway (Block F to Block V)

•	DDA Front Ramp

•	Various Building Works

•	External Painting

The Works will take approximately 10 to 12 months to complete (from award date) and will need to be staged to suit the scope of works and the operations of Oral Health, Supportive Therapy, Hospital in the Home and Staff Accommodation.

publicQuestions.question:
Q1 - Can you provide more detailed usage information for each site so transport and volumes can be better understood and considered in our offer.

Q2 - With delivery to a campus where multiple areas are using the linen service is it expected that the provider deliver to each user area or will delivery be to one central point at the campus and collected from this staging area by users

Q3 - Can you clarify what contract term you are seeking to implement with successful provider eg 1 2 or 3 years
publicQuestions.answer:
Q1. Can you provide more detailed usage information for each site so transport and volumes can be better understood and considered in our offer?

Response:

TAFE Queensland has provided the best available information to support suppliers in preparing their offers. The volumes included within the procurement documentation are indicative only and have been developed for evaluation purposes.

Please refer to Attachment A – Specification and Attachment C – Linen Hire & Laundry Pricing List (Pricing Scenario tab) for indicative demand information.

As outlined in the Specification, service demand varies by campus and is influenced by factors such as student enrolments, training schedules, practical class delivery, events, facility utilisation, and seasonal activity. Accordingly, TAFE Queensland is unable to provide guaranteed site-specific usage volumes. Suppliers should base their offers on their capacity to service nominated locations and accommodate fluctuations in demand throughout the contract term.

The current estimated demand across the TAFE Queensland network is approximately 2,750 to 4,300 items per week; however, actual volumes may be higher or lower depending on operational requirements.

Q2. With delivery to a campus where multiple areas are using the linen service, is it expected that the provider deliver to each user area or will delivery be to one central point at the campus and collected from this staging area by users?

Response:

For the purposes of tender evaluation, suppliers should assume that delivery and collection will occur at a single nominated delivery point within each campus.

Specific delivery arrangements may vary between campuses and service areas and will be confirmed during implementation with the successful supplier(s). Suppliers may identify any assumptions, site requirements, or alternative service delivery approaches within their offer submission.

Q3. Can you clarify what contract term you are seeking to implement with the successful provider, e.g. 1, 2 or 3 years?

Response:

The contract term is stated in both the Invitation to Offer and Attachment A – Specification. The proposed Standing Offer Arrangement term is three (3) years, with an option for TAFE Queensland to extend the arrangement by up to two (2) additional periods of twelve (12) months each, at TAFE Queensland's discretion. The maximum potential term is therefore five (5) years.

publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your clarification question.

We request that the maintenance schedule is priced so that the bespoke rooms are serviced biannually and the 96 standard meeting rooms annually.

title: RFT260087 Construction of Blackwater Recycled Water Pipeline Stage 2 Valve Station
description:
Background Information

Central Highlands Regional Council is seeking a suitably qualified and experienced contractor to undertake the construction of the Blackwater Recycle Water Pipeline Stage 2 Valve Station at Hunter Street, Blackwater.

The works form part of Council’s recycled water infrastructure and involve the fabrication, supply and installation of new valve station pipework and associated equipment and protective structural cover, together with connections to existing pipeline infrastructure. The works include integration with the existing DN300 HDPE Stage 3 pipeline and DN200 HDPE rising main, installation of Principal-supplied and Contractor-supplied equipment, and associated civil, excavation, backfilling, testing, commissioning and reinstatement works.

The existing DN100 effluent pipeline is required to remain operational during construction until the new work is complete, and the final connections can be undertaken.

The successful Contractor will be required to carefully plan and coordinate the works with Council to maintain continuity of service, minimize operational disruption, and deliver a complete, tested and commissioned installation in accordance with the detailed design drawings and Contract requirements.

Key Deliverables include:

•	Site establishment, management plans, site preparation and disestablishment.

•	Supply and fabrication of stainless-steel pipework and fittings in accordance with the detailed design drawings.

•	Excavation, trenching, backfilling and associated civil works required for the valve station and pipeline connections.

•	Construction of the reinforced concrete valve station slab, plinths and associated civil works in accordance with the detailed design drawings.

•	Supply, fabrication, delivery and erection of the structural steel valve station cover over the above-ground pipework, including roof sheeting and associated structural components, in accordance with the detailed design drawings.

•	Construction and installation of the new valve station pipework and associated equipment.

•	Connection of the new works to the existing DN300 HDPE Stage 3 pipeline and existing DN200 HDPE rising main.

publicQuestions.question:
Dear Council Tender Team,

We are currently preparing our tender submission for TEN16777 – Rehabilitation of Sewer Mains, Cleaning, CCTV Inspections, Condition Assessment, Lining & Associated Works.

Having reviewed the tender documentation and the clarifications already published on VendorPanel, we request clarification on the following items to ensure our Schedule of Rates is prepared in accordance with Council’s intended delivery and payment arrangements.

1. Indicative quantities and sewer segment lengths

Council has advised that the works will be issued as a single-block work package each financial year and that the current financial year budget is approximately $500,000.

Can Council please provide, if available, indicative quantities for the anticipated 2026/27 works, including approximate sewer main lengths by diameter, number of sewer segments, anticipated number of house service connections/junctions, and approximate quantities of cleaning/CCTV works?

If these quantities are not yet available, can Council provide historical annual quantities or a representative previous work package to assist tenderers in establishing appropriate Schedule of Rates pricing?

2. Minimum work package quantities / mobilisation

Schedule 3 requires unit rates that incorporate mobilisation/demobilisation, equipment setup and associated activities.

Within the annual work package, will Council establish minimum work package quantities, minimum chargeable liner lengths, mobilisation/demobilisation items or minimum call-out values?

If not, can Council please advise whether tendered per-metre rates are expected to cover mobilisation and setup costs irrespective of the length or quantity of individual sewer segments instructed?

3. Traffic management

The tender documentation requires traffic control to be incorporated into various cleaning, assessment and lining activities while also providing separate Traffic Management items within the Schedule of Rates.

Can Council please clarify the intended application of the separate Traffic Management Schedule items and provide an indication, if available, of the anticipated proportion of works likely to require additional traffic management, particularly works on higher-volume roads, controlled arterial roads, lane closures or other complex traffic environments?

4. Abnormal cleaning and obstruction removal

Where sewer cleaning encounters conditions materially beyond normal pressure cleaning and root cutting, such as significant deposits, concrete, major obstructions or other conditions requiring specialist or extended removal methods, will these additional works be separately authorised and paid under an applicable Schedule of Rates item or treated as a variation?

5. Major bypass pumping

Where sewer flows cannot be adequately controlled using normal bunging or flow-control methods and substantial temporary bypass pumping is required to undertake cleaning, CCTV or lining works, can Council please confirm whether major bypass pumping is deemed included within the applicable scheduled rates or will be separately authorised and payable based on the site-specific requirements?

6. Schedule of Rates – basis of payment

The tender documentation describes TEN16777 as a Schedule of Rates contract, and the Technical Specification provides for payment based on the unit rate for quantities ordered and accepted.

Can Council please confirm that the Contract is intended to operate on a remeasurable Schedule of Rates basis, with payment based on the actual quantities of work ordered and completed at the applicable tendered unit rates, notwithstanding the fixed lump sum wording contained within the amended Clause 3 of the General Conditions of Contract?

Thank you for your assistance. We look forward to Council’s clarification.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Council does not have confirmed quantities for the 2026/27 works package at this stage. As a guide only, a typical annual package may include Cleaning, CCTV and Relining of the following assets:

•	80-100 sewer segments of 150mm diameter (approximately 2,500m to 3000m)

•	4-8 sewer segments of 225mm diameter (approximately 200m to 400m)

•	3-6 sewer segments of 300mm diameter (approximately 150m to 300m)

These quantities are indicative only and may vary based on condition assessments, priorities and available budget. Council does not guarantee any minimum quantity, value or distribution of work under the contract.

2. Council intends to issue the annual rehabilitation works as a single work package. Tenderers should include mobilisation, demobilisation, setup and associated costs within their tendered rates. No minimum quantities, minimum liner lengths or minimum call-out values are guaranteed.

3. Traffic management requirements will vary depending on the location and nature of the works. Where external traffic control services are required, the separate Traffic Management items within the Schedule of Rates will apply.

4. Where abnormal cleaning or specialist obstruction removal is required, the work will be subject to Council approval and paid under an applicable Schedule of Rates item or treated as a variation.

5. Major bypass pumping will be assessed on a site-specific basis and, where approved by Council, will be separately authorised and paid under the relevant Schedule of Rates item or as a variation.

6. The contract is intended to operate as a Schedule of Rates contract, with payment based on the actual quantities of work completed and accepted at the tendered unit rates.

publicQuestions.question:
-	It would be appreciated if Council could please advise of your target timeframe for the project.

-	It would be appreciated if Council could please provide an indication of budget or budget range for the project as we suggest this will allow submissions to be more tailored and aligned with Council’s expectation?

-	In relation to the Scope of works item:

“A fit for purpose risk assessment will be required to inform the provisions of the Planning Scheme relating to natural hazard risk (flood, bushfire, landslide and coastal hazards). The Integrating State Interests in a Planning Scheme guidance material includes information on the steps involved in undertaking a fit for purpose risk assessment”,

we seek Council's confirmation that whilst the planning risk assessment is part of the Scope of Works, the risk assessments based on the technical studies for flood, bushfire, landslide and coastal hazards, have been completed by the relevant technical expert and will be provided to the successful consultant as background material?'
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for the questions. Council provides the following clarification:

1. Project timeframe

Council requires the draft Planning Scheme Amendment to be completed and submitted for State Interest Review by June 2027. Tenderers should provide a project program demonstrating how this milestone will be achieved, including sufficient time for technical studies, drafting, Council review and Councilor workshops.

2. Project budget

Council has not prescribed a fixed budget or budget range. Tenderers are requested to provide a competitive fee proposal based on the Scope of Works, clearly identifying key project stages, assumptions, exclusions and any additional or optional services.

3. Natural hazard risk assessment

Council confirms that the requirements differ across the four natural hazards:

Flood – the technical study has been completed and will be provided to the successful consultant.

Coastal hazards – the technical study has been completed and will be provided to the successful consultant.

Bushfire – a technical study and associated risk assessment are required to be completed as part of this commission.

Landslide – a technical study and associated risk assessment are required to be completed as part of this commission.

The successful consultant will be responsible for undertaking the overall fit-for-purpose planning risk assessment and integrating the outcomes of all four hazard assessments into the Planning Scheme in accordance with the relevant State interests and guidance material.

Previous housing engagement: Council has undertaken previous community and stakeholder engagement through strategic planning, housing and community planning activities. Relevant available reports and consultation outcomes will be provided to the successful consultant. Project-specific housing engagement will still be required.

Existing stakeholder relationships: Council has established relationships with relevant community, industry, service providers, major employers and State Government agencies. Council will assist with stakeholder identification and introductions where appropriate. The Study Team will be responsible for maintaining the project stakeholder register and managing engagement.

First Nations engagement protocols: Council has existing relationships with Traditional Owners and First Nations organisations. Council will assist the Study Team in identifying appropriate representatives and engagement protocols to ensure consultation is culturally appropriate.

First Nations engagement responsibilities: This will be a shared responsibility. Council will facilitate introductions and provide guidance on existing relationships and protocols. The Study Team will be responsible for preparing, facilitating, documenting and reporting on the engagement and incorporating outcomes into the project.

Consultation responsibilities: Council will assist with stakeholder identification, introductions, Council communication channels, elected-member engagement and State agency coordination. The Study Team will be responsible for engagement planning, materials, logistics, facilitation, surveys, recording outcomes, analysis and consultation reporting.

Stakeholder contact information: Council will provide or facilitate appropriate stakeholder contacts where permitted, subject to privacy requirements. The Study Team will manage the project-specific contact database.

Venues and logistics: Council can assist with access to suitable Council facilities where available. The Study Team should allow for coordination and delivery of consultation activities within its proposal.

Engagement materials: The Study Team will prepare consultation and engagement materials, subject to Council review and approval before release.

Workshops and community sessions: The Study Team should allow for professional facilitation of workshops, meetings and community sessions. Council officers will participate where appropriate.

Online engagement: The Study Team will be responsible for preparation and administration of online engagement and surveys. Council can assist with promotion through its existing communication channels.

Elected representatives: Council will coordinate access to elected representatives. The Study Team should allow for preparation and facilitation of relevant Councillor workshops and briefings.

State Government agencies: Council will assist with formal agency coordination. The Study Team will be responsible for technical input, participation, follow-up and incorporation of State agency feedback.

Consultation outcomes: The Study Team will be responsible for recording and analysing consultation outcomes and demonstrating how findings have informed the Housing Needs Assessment, Housing Strategy and Planning Scheme amendment.

Preliminary consultation: Tenderers should assume that project-specific preliminary consultation remains within the scope of the successful Study Team. Council will provide relevant previous consultation material where available as background information.

Council participation: Council officers will participate in key workshops, Councillor briefings and major engagement activities where appropriate. Tenderers should nevertheless allow for the Study Team to independently facilitate engagement activities.

Fee proposal: Tenderers should include sufficient allowance for the consultation and engagement required to deliver the project. The final engagement program and methodology will be agreed with Council during project inception.

title: TRC000584 Southern Cross Oval Light Upgrade
description:
Southern Cross Reserve Oval is a Council-managed, multi-use sporting facility comprising a single irrigated oval with a turf wicket block and supporting amenities. The oval is classified as a Class 1 sports field within Toowoomba Regional Council’s sports field hierarchy due to the quality of the playing surface, the level of supporting amenities and the availability of oval lighting.

The facility supports a high level of seasonal community sport. During summer, it is used for Toowoomba A Grade Cricket competition, including limited-over, night fixtures and T20 night games. During winter, the oval supports Downs Rugby competition and AFL Darling Downs competition. Key user groups operating from Southern Cross Reserve Oval include Toowoomba Cricket Incorporated, Bears Rugby Union and South Toowoomba Bombers AFL.

The current oval lighting configuration includes three 30 metre TP EK30M GM poles, and three 25 metre TP EK25M GM poles, fitted with a combination of Philips MVP507 luminaires and Philips MVF403 ArenaVision luminaires.

Council has approved a capital budget allocation for the replacement of luminaires at Southern Cross Reserve Oval as part of the Sports Lighting Replacement Program. The upgrade is scheduled for delivery during the 2026–2027 financial year and is intended to improve lighting performance, reliability, energy efficiency and ongoing serviceability while supporting continued community sport use of the facility.

Toowoomba Regional Council (TRC) invites submissions from suitably qualified and experienced Principal Contractors for the design, supply, installation, management and coordination of the replacement of sports oval luminaries at Southern Cross Reserve.

regards

Kathy

publicQuestions.question: Hi Eddie, addendum 3 mentions conflicting dates for the second site inspection (26/08 in the text & 28/08 in the table) Can you please confirm? Many thanks
publicQuestions.answer: The second site visit is scheduled for next Wednesday 26 August at 1pm.

publicQuestions.question: Hello can you confirm the alternative time for the Site inspection - is it the Wednesday 26th? I note on the addendum notice it indicates the 26th and 28th at 1pm in the table.
publicQuestions.answer: Sorry for any confusion. Second site inspection will be Wednesday 26 August 1-3pm.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI Question 1: Flood risk and integrated water management

The site is subject to the Land Subject to Inundation Overlay and adjoins Bendigo Creek. Will respondents be expected to address flood risk as part of the scope?

RFI Question 2: Access and movement

Could the City clarify the expected scope of access, movement and car parking component within the Master Plan? Will specialist transport expertise be required, or is this expected to be addressed at a high level within the urban design response?
publicQuestions.answer:
Question 1: Yes, the constraints of the LSIO should be taken into account.

Question 2: Indicative pedestrian/cycling access through the site linking into public spaces and broader networks should form part of the master plan. Vehicle access (most likely through the existing gate entry/ies) including for emergency vehicles is required. It is anticipated that parking will need to be provided to some extent but given there is a large public car park to the east and some on street parking, hopefully on-site parking can be discreet and minimised. We do not think the scrutiny of the project by traffic expertise is warranted at master plan stage and would expect that those issues are dealt with later.

publicQuestions.question:
From a review of the brief, it is our assessment that the scope of works is misaligned with the budget of $150-190k.

Can you please confirm if the price is fixed or the scope? Would you be open to a non-conforming bid with a greater fee or a more confined scope?
publicQuestions.answer: Thanks for this question and an important one to clarify. The budget is indicative only. The scope is fixed and a submission needs to be received that conforms with the scope at whatever price/costing you consider is necessary to meet the scope. A greater fee outside of the indicative budget will certainly be considered. You may also choose to put in a non-conforming submission that doesn't meet the full scope but meets the indicative budget. The non-conforming submission is additional to a conforming submission and won't be considered if it is a stand along submission.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Kathy,

Regarding Q1 in my previous RFI. On Page 16 of the RFQ under Key Stakeholders:

Council’s Project Manager is the primary contact and is responsible for the day-to-day requirements of the project, including, but not limited to:

• Confirm the project brief, scope of the project and methodology

• Following procurement, engage organisations to complete technical investigations

• Assist with onsite community consultations

• Engagement of Councillors and Council.

Cheers,

James
publicQuestions.answer:
Hi James

That would be if we felt there was something that might need further investigation such as some contamination advice if a proposal was to breach the capping of the ground surface or perhaps some engineering advice on the structural integrity of one of the buildings. I think at master plan stage this scenario is not likely but just in case something arose.

In regard to your other questions, they have disappeared off Vendor Panel after I responded to Q1 privately. Could you repost the rest of the questions as I will respond publicly to those?

many thanks

Kathy

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Kathy,

1. The RFQ notes that Council will engage organisations to undertake technical investigations. Can Council confirm which investigations are anticipated and whether the consultant is expected to coordinate and incorporate these findings rather than undertake the investigations?

2.Can Council confirm the anticipated number and format of consultation activities for Stages 1 and 2? Can the listed stakeholders be engaged through a combination of grouped sessions, individual meetings and online engagement?

3. Section 13 identifies an estimated project duration of 10–12 months and lists Milestones 1–4 against Weeks 1, 9, 20 and 35 under a column headed ‘Start date’. Could Council please confirm whether these weeks represent the commencement of each subsequent stage, or the required completion dates for the stated milestone outputs?

4. Can Council confirm the expected Heritage Victoria review process for the Options Analysis and Heritage Interpretation Plan, including the anticipated number of review rounds and whether Council will facilitate the referral?
publicQuestions.answer:
1. If there were additional investigations necessary to enable a fulsome design response then Council would engage relevant expertise to deliver this. It is anticipated that for master planning we have sufficient information but perhaps we may need to investigate some structural integrity of something or seek some further clarity around contamination such as breaking through the capping. Council will coordinate this work if it is required and it would be at the discretion of Council and funded by Council.

2. Consultation Stage 1 - one group session would suffice and if they are unable to make that then online engagement. Council can assist with this. Consultation Stage 2 - up to the consultancy as to how they can effectively reach the public such as drop-in sessions which Council can assist with any format. We also have several media avenues to reach out such as Facebook page and website, local paper. Group session with key stakeholder groups as per Stage 1.

3. This is the anticipated start dates but acknowledge that there will be some crossover with dates. They are not hard and fast but indictive so that we all have some understanding of the possible length of the project. This can be further discussed at an inception meeting and negotiated, with the understanding that there is flexibility given the unknowns of the project.

4. Council will facilitate the referral to HV. I am seeking some clarity from them as to the scope of this work given the permit conditions are theirs and I will post that advice as soon as I get it. If you have a heritage consultant already on board, they should have an idea of this. I would refer to your heritage consultant as to how may rounds this would normally entail with HV. I understand they are very particular and accounting for the heritage significance of the site.

publicQuestions.question: For Evaluation Criteria Response 1.2, can you please confirm if you would like this information for all key personell listed on the project or just the leadership team? Can you also confirm if this extends to the subconsultants.
publicQuestions.answer: We would like to know what experience the team can bring to the project whether that is key personnel and/or leadership team and this extends to sub-consultants. If the leadership team has good experience on similar projects but the key personnel on the project don't then we would want to know how involved and what oversight the leadership team will have. This is a high-profile project for the City and will have a lot of scrutiny by the Councillors and community and we would like that there is an experienced and strong leadership team involved and leading that public/Council interface when required.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Kathy,

Can you please confirm if there is an existing feature & level survey for the subject site?

Also, can you confirm if Council has undertaken any economics assessments related to retail demand in the area?

Thanks!
publicQuestions.answer:
There is an existing feature survey that was undertaken as part of the Environmental Audit as part of the remediation works. I am endeavouring to get access from the Auditor to the document so it can be shared on Vendor Panel hopefully tomorrow. I will keep you posted. This will be sufficient as an interim document, however, I will get an updated feature survey with revised levels done as soon as possible.

There are no economic assessments related to retail demand in the immediate area, however, I can tell you that there are vacant shops in the city centre. The Gasworks site does however, have a different context and possibly more nuanced potential than that of a site within the city.

publicQuestions.question: For Evaluation Criteria Response 1.1, can you confirm if you would accept 3 project examples that are Non-City of Greater Bendigo
publicQuestions.answer: Yes of course. That wording is a bit confusing. Three non-Bendigo projects are absolutely acceptable. We accept that not all consultancies will have done work in Bendigo and it is not necessary to have done so. It's about capability and not whether past projects are local.

publicQuestions.question:
Hello,

Please confirm whether Council will arrange and fund DJAARA participation and cultural advisory services, or whether the consultant is expected to engage DJAARA directly.
publicQuestions.answer: Council will initiate contact with DJAARA for their involvement. Costs associated with DJAARA will be the responsibility of Council. There is no formal protocol for engaging with DJAARA. It has been and continues to be a very collaborative relationship on design projects.

publicQuestions.question:
1. The Assumptions (Item 11) state that consultants' attendance at engagement activities is "to be confirmed" and that "an hourly rate to be provided to participate in engagement." Can you please confirm whether attendance at consultation and workshops is to be included in the fixed milestone fees, or reimbursed separately at the hourly rates provided in the Schedule of Rates.

2. The brief treats economic viability as a "foundational requirement," referring to revenue streams, tenant and activation mix, and a sustainable operating model. Can you please confirm whether the project requires a full business case or financial model, or a strategic economic and activation framework to guide the Options Analysis and Master Plan.

3. The Options Analysis and Master Plan ask for "approximate costs" and "indicative capital implications." Can you please confirm whether a quantity surveyor cost plan is anticipated within the fee, and if so, to what level of detail.

5. Early engagement with DJAARA is a required part of the scope. Can you please confirm whether Council has an existing engagement agreement or protocol, and whether any DJAARA participation fees are to be borne by Council.

6. In the Schedule of Rates and Basis of Payment, "Consultation Stage 1 completed" appears under both Milestone 1 and Milestone 2. Can you please confirm which milestone this deliverable sits under for payment.

7. A Heritage Impact Assessment is listed as a Stage 3 deliverable. Please confirm whether it must be prepared to permit-grade standard (to Heritage Victoria requirements), or as a high-level assessment to inform the concept options.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. I think you should include a fee for consultant attendance at the engagement activities. Also provide an hourly rate in case there will be additional attendance required.

2. The City is not after a business case at this stage. A framework to guide potential options is sufficient which could be tested at the next stage through a business case.

3. A quantity surveyor is not required. Indicative costs based on previous experience is sufficient at this stage.

5. Costs with DJAARA involvement will be the responsibility of Council. There is no agreement of protocol in place. Council will facilitate the initial engagement with DJAARA.

6. Apologies, that Consultation Stage 1 sits within Milestone 1 and will be scheduled for payment accordingly.

7. The Heritage Impact Assessment should be high level and consider the impacts on heritage within the concept options.

publicQuestions.question:

Is Council considering private investment as part of the site's future, or is the expectation that development will be government-funded? 3. Would Council consider selling or leasing parts of the site to facilitate redevelopment?

publicQuestions.question:
Clarification on Question 2.1 (Capacity)

We note a similar question has been raised on this item, but are seeking further clarification on the following:

1.	Question 2.1 states "capacity to provide resources to deliver similar projects over the last 5 years," while the accompanying instruction asks tenderers to "provide a list of current projects, their value and expected completion dates." Could Council please confirm whether this question is seeking evidence of past project experience (similar to Question 1.1) or the tenderer's current workload/capacity to take on this contract?

2.	Where a tender is being submitted by a multi-disciplinary team (e.g. a lead consultant supported by sub-consultants or partner practices), could Council please confirm whether Question 2.1 should be answered by the lead consultant only, or whether each practice/sub-consultant in the team is required to provide their own capacity details?
publicQuestions.answer:
1. The aim of this questioning is to ascertain whether the tenderer has delivered similar projects (although accepting that this project has some unique aspects) and there is the capacity to deliver projects of a similar nature in the past ie. there is a capacity of expertise/resources to deliver something similar. Not asking about your current workload capacity.

2. This should be answered by the lead consultant. If sub-consultants have experience/capability then this could be added in the attachments to support that.

publicQuestions.question:
Question 1.5 asks for our Past performance for the last 3 years. Can you please clarify what kind of response you are expecting for this question? E.g are you asking about our project performance?

How does this question differ from 2.1?

Thank you
publicQuestions.answer:
There have been a few questions around Part 4, Section 1 Capability and Section 2 Capacity. Procurement have provided some clarity on this as follows:

1. Capability is requesting examples of past work that shows your capability to complete this work. These examples are selective and should represent work you have completed of a similar nature and may be used as reference checks for short listed organisations. (these don't need to be current projects and should be of a similar nature to the works requested in the RFQ)

2. Capacity is requesting details of your current workload with completion dates and how much each project would represent as a percentage of your workload capacity. This is to demonstrate that you have the capacity to take on this project within the agreed timeframe.

If you need any further clarity, please send through a query.

thanks

Kathy
