regards

Kathy

publicQuestions.question:
Hello. Noting there has already been a number of questions relating to the Part 4 Response Schedule, can you please provide further clarifications on the following:

Criterion 1.2 Could you confirm whether this criterion asks tenderers to nominate a single key person and provide three examples of their relevant experience, or whether it should cover multiple key personnel across the proposed team?

Criterion 1.5 The criterion notes that "past performance for the last 3 years may be included when evaluating this criterion." Could you clarify what type of response Council expects here, and how it is intended to differ from the project examples provided under Criterion 1.1?

Criterion 2.1 Could you confirm whether this criterion asks for all current projects of the tendering entity, or a representative selection? Could you also confirm what "capacity" refers to — for example, the proportion of the practice's overall resource each project currently consumes?

Criterion 2.2 Could you confirm what "capacity" refers to in relation to individual personnel? For example, the proportion of that person's available time allocated to this commission, or their availability more generally. Could you also confirm whether sub-consultant personnel should be included in this table alongside the tendering entity's own staff.

Schedule of Rates The schedule lists rates for Principal, Senior staff and Junior staff. Could you confirm whether tenderers can add rows reflecting their actual staffing structure. Could you also confirm whether sub-consultant rates should be included in this schedule.

Many thanks.
publicQuestions.answer:
Criterion 1.2 - For any key personnel nominated in criterion 2.2, list all of those that were involved in any of the projects listed in 1.2.

Criterion 1.5 - No response required here. Council reserves the right to use previous projects not listed by the Tenderer as examples of previous capability.

Criterion 2.1 - Preference is to list all current workloads to allow the City to understand the Tenderers capacity to undertake this project in a timely manner. We would prefer all projects to be listed or alternatively if this exceeds 10, a representative selection of key projects the key personnel will be working on. Under capacity for this item please note the practice's overall resources as a percentage of commitment to each contract.

Criterion 2.2 - Capacity here should represent the individual's commitment to this project as a percentage of their overall workload (eg 1 out of 4 projects on the go 25%). You can list subcontractors however don't assign a percentage to them as you possibly can't keep them to that value.

Schedule of Rates - Yes, you can add as many new lines as you see fit. This should include all sub consultancies as well.

publicQuestions.question: Are the cover pages, contents page and cover letter included in the 15 page count? Thanks
publicQuestions.answer: The 15 page limit does not include the cover pages, contents page or cover letter although it is preferred that the cover letter is no more than two pages.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi,

can you please elaborate on the following response? Would you like us to nominate an additional 3 projects and outline who from our proposed key personnel have worked on those projects or would you like us to submit 3 projects per key personnel?

Criterion 1.2 - For any key personnel nominated in criterion 2.2, list all of those that were involved in any of the projects listed in 1.2.
publicQuestions.answer:
2.2 This should list the key personnel that will be working on the Gasworks project and their capacity to be involved in the project. These personnel may not have worked on the projects listed in 2.1 as this is organisational wide. We want to know who will be the key personnel for this project. For example if a Principal Architect or Director is to have 10% involvement in the project and the graduate architect is to have 90% involvement. This is to give us an idea of the level of oversight by senior personnel, input of experienced and less experienced so we can get an understanding of the level of expertise across the life of the project.

1.2 List three projects of the organisation and the key personnel that worked on these projects. They may not align with the projects you have put forward for the organisation's capability or capacity at 1.2 or 2.1. It may be that some key personnel were involved in these projects or none of them had involvement with any of the projects listed. It gives us an idea of the experience of the key personnel you are putting forward to do the Gasworks project.

publicQuestions.question: Can suppliers submit for the facade-cleaning component only? If a single response must cover both components, may the access-system inspection and testing be delivered by an approved specialist subcontractor or consortium member? Please confirm the mandatory licences or accreditations and minimum insurance limits for the head contractor and specialist subcontractor, and whether any mandatory briefing or site inspection applies.
publicQuestions.answer:
Tenderers may submit a response for the full scope of services or for an individual service component as follows:

•	Façade and Window Cleaning Services Only and/or

•	Anchor Point Inspection, Testing and Certification Services Only or

•	Both Service Components as a Single Submission.

Where a Tenderer elects to submit for both service components but does not directly perform anchor point inspection and testing services, the Tenderer may engage a suitably qualified specialist subcontractor or consortium partner to undertake these works. Any proposed subcontractor or consortium member must be clearly identified within the tender submission, including their qualifications, experience, certifications and relevant licences.

For facade and window cleaning works via rope access:

•	Current Queensland Work Health and Safety compliance.

•	Personnel holding a current General Construction Induction (White Card).

•	Rope access technicians certified through an internationally recognised rope access scheme, such as:

o	IRATA (Industrial Rope Access Trade Association) or

o	SPRAT (Society of Professional Rope Access Technicians).

•	Demonstrated competency in working at heights and rescue procedures.

For anchor point inspection, testing and certification services:

•	Demonstrated competency to inspect and certify fall-arrest anchor systems in accordance with the relevant Australian Standards.

•	Inspection and testing personnel suitably qualified and experienced in:

o AS/NZS 1891 series.

o AS/NZS 5532

o	AS/NZS 4488 (where rope access systems are utilised).

•	Use of calibrated testing equipment and provision of certification documentation upon completion.

Minimum insurance limits are noted in the ITO documentation, and a non-mandatory site inspection has already been held.

title: 2026.31 - Barmaryee Sports Precinct Master Plan
description:
Livingstone Shire Council (Council) invites suitably qualified and experienced consultancy firms to submit a Tender for the preparation of the Barmaryee Multi Sports Precinct Master Plan.

The objective of this engagement is to develop a comprehensive, evidence-based and implementable Master Plan that will guide the future planning, development and staged expansion of the Barmaryee Multi Sports Precinct as a regionally significant sporting and recreation hub.

The Master Plan will establish a long-term vision for the precinct, incorporating the planning and integration of sporting infrastructure, supporting facilities, transport networks, access, parking, open space, landscaping and associated infrastructure to meet current and future community needs.

The Barmaryee Multi Sports Precinct is a strategically important Council-owned facility that currently accommodates a range of sporting and community activities, including Junior Rugby League, Touch Football, Netball, OzTag, Keppel Coast District events and school sporting carnivals.

The precinct has been identified as the preferred location for the future expansion of rectangular sports, including Rugby Union, Outriggers, Volleyball and other compatible sporting and recreation activities. Continued population growth, increasing participation rates and demand for regional sporting infrastructure have created the need for a coordinated and sustainable master planning approach to maximise the precinct's capacity, functionality and long-term value to the community.

The successful Tenderer will be responsible for providing all professional services necessary to deliver the Master Plan in accordance with the Contract, Technical Specification and associated Tender Documents, including project management, stakeholder engagement, site investigations, technical assessments, concept development, implementation planning and final reporting.

The Contract will be administered under AS 4122 – General Conditions of Contract for Consultants, with services delivered in accordance with the staged deliverables specified in the Tender Documents.

publicQuestions.question:
CAD Deliverables Clarification

The tender documentation identifies both the Draft Master Plan and Final Master Plan as requiring submission in CAD format. Could Council please clarify its expectations regarding the CAD deliverable and the intended use of the files?

Our standard approach for strategic master planning is to prepare plans using industry-standard graphic design and publishing software, including Adobe Illustrator and Adobe InDesign. This workflow produces high-quality presentation plans suitable for stakeholder engagement, Council reporting, funding submissions and grant applications, while still allowing accurate spatial planning and design outcomes.

We note that plans prepared directly in CAD software can result in a more technical drawing style and may require additional drafting and graphic production processes to achieve the presentation quality typically expected of master planning documents.

Importantly, Illustrator-based plans can be exported to DWG format, with model space linework and layer information retained and accessible within AutoCAD. As such, it may be possible to satisfy Council's CAD requirements without preparing the master plan entirely within a CAD platform.

Could Council please clarify:

- Whether the requirement for CAD is intended to provide Council with an editable digital file of the final master plan;

- Whether CAD files derived from Illustrator exports would be acceptable;

- Whether Council has a preferred CAD platform or file format (e.g. DWG, DXF); and

- Whether there is a specific operational or asset management purpose for requiring CAD deliverables.

Understanding Council's intended use of the CAD files will assist tenderers in proposing the most appropriate and cost-effective approach to delivering the master plan. Thank you in advance.
publicQuestions.answer:
Council requires the Draft Master Plan and Final Master Plan to be submitted in editable CAD format (DWG) in accordance with the RFQ requirements.

In response to your specific questions:

1. Whether the requirement for CAD is intended to provide Council with an editable digital file of the final master plan

Yes. Council requires editable CAD files of both the Draft and Final Master Plan to support future planning, concept development, staging reviews, grant funding applications and subsequent design activities.

2. Whether CAD files derived from Illustrator exports would be acceptable

Tenderers may utilise their preferred software and workflows during development of the master plan. However, the submitted deliverable must be an editable DWG file that accurately represents the adopted master plan and is suitable for future use and modification by Council and future consultants.

3. Whether Council has a preferred CAD platform or file format

Council requires submission of the Draft and Final Master Plan in DWG format.

4. Whether there is a specific operational or asset management purpose for requiring CAD deliverables

The purpose of the CAD deliverables is to ensure Council retains an editable spatial representation of the adopted master plan that can be utilised for future planning, concept refinement, staging assessments, funding applications and subsequent project development.

Council acknowledges that presentation-quality master plans are often produced using a range of software platforms. However, regardless of the software used during plan development, the Draft and Final Master Plan must be provided as editable DWG files in accordance with the RFQ requirements.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI 1 – Status of Concept Plan Review and Future Facility Provision

Council has provided the Barmaryee Multisport Precinct Concept Plan Review 2024 which identifies preferred future infrastructure including rugby union, AFL, cricket, running track and beach volleyball facilities.

Can Council confirm whether the findings, priorities, facility allocations and future development opportunities identified within the Concept Plan Review represent Council's endorsed strategic position and preferred development direction for the precinct, such that the consultant's role is primarily to validate, refine and spatially accommodate these facilities?

Alternatively, is Council seeking the successful consultant to independently reassess facility requirements, undertake option analysis and prioritisation, and potentially recommend materially different outcomes based on technical investigations, stakeholder consultation, servicing constraints and affordability considerations?

RFI 2 – Sporting Needs Analysis

The Concept Plan Review 2024 references an existing Sporting Needs Analysis used to inform engagement outcomes and future planning for the precinct.

Can Council provide this document to tenderers?

Further, can Council confirm whether the successful consultant is expected to include a specialist sport and recreation consultant to undertake additional participation forecasting, demand modelling or needs assessment activities beyond review of existing Council studies and stakeholder engagement outcomes?

RFI 3 – Stakeholder Engagement Expectations

The Concept Plan Review 2024 identifies previous community surveys, stakeholder engagement activities and direct discussions with sporting clubs and user groups.

Can Council clarify whether the consultant is expected to:

a) validate and refine existing stakeholder requirements; or

b) undertake a new consultation process and re-establish stakeholder requirements from first principles?

Please also clarify the minimum stakeholder engagement activities expected as part of this commission to ensure consistency across tender submissions.

RFI 4 – Cost Planning Scope

The Scope requires preparation of planning-level cost estimates and staging strategies.

Can Council confirm whether cost estimates are required only for the preferred Master Plan outcome, or whether alternative layouts, facility configurations and staging options are also expected to be developed, costed and comparatively assessed?

RFI 5 – Traffic Assessment Scope

Can Council clarify whether the traffic assessment is intended to comprise:

a) a strategic review of site access, circulation and parking requirements to support the Master Plan; or

b) a detailed traffic engineering assessment including traffic generation analysis, intersection performance and future event capacity modelling?

RFI 6 – Flooding and Environmental Assessment Scope

We acknowledge Council's previous responses regarding flood and environmental investigations.

Given the supporting information is not available during the tender period and the extent of any further investigations cannot presently be determined, can Council confirm that:

a) tenderers may assume review of existing information and provision of strategic master planning advice only;

b) any additional flood modelling, hydraulic investigations, ecological field surveys, EPBC Act assessments or specialist studies identified as necessary following review of existing information may be treated as provisional sums or variations?

RFI 7 – Site Servicing Capacity

Has Council undertaken any previous investigations into utility servicing capacity for future expansion of the precinct, including potable water, irrigation water, sewer, electrical and communications infrastructure?

If so, can relevant studies and available servicing information be provided to tenderers?

Further, can Council clarify whether the successful consultant is expected to:

a) undertake a high-level servicing review only; or

b) engage utility authorities and identify network constraints, augmentation requirements and upgrade implications necessary to support the ultimate Master Plan development scenario?
publicQuestions.answer:
RFI 1 – Status of Concept Plan Review and Future Facility Provision

Council confirms that the Barmaryee Multisport Precinct Concept Plan Review 2024 forms the primary basis for preparation of the Master Plan and represents the most recent planning undertaken for the precinct.

The Concept Plan Review 2024 has not been formally endorsed by Council. The consultant is expected to review, validate, refine and optimise the recommendations contained within the Concept Plan Review in accordance with the Scope of Works.

Council is not seeking a new strategic planning exercise or a reassessment of facility requirements from first principles.

RFI2 – Sporting needs analysis

Council will make available relevant background information and previous studies held by Council that are considered applicable to the project. If available, the Sporting Needs Analysis referenced within the Concept Plan Review 2024 will be provided.

Council is not specifically seeking a standalone sporting needs analysis, participation forecasting exercise or demand modelling study. Tenderers should allow within their fee for review of available information, stakeholder engagement and investigations reasonably necessary to satisfy the Scope of Works.

RFI3 – Stakeholder engagement expectations

Council expects the consultant to review previous engagement outcomes and undertake stakeholder engagement activities necessary to validate and refine stakeholder requirements for the Master Plan. Existing consultation outcomes should be considered as key inputs into the process.

The consultant shall engage with the stakeholders identified in the Scope of Works and any additional stakeholders nominated by Council. Tenderers should allow within their fee for all stakeholder engagement activities reasonably necessary to satisfy the Scope of Works.

RFI 4 – Cost Planning Scope

Planning-level cost estimates are required for the preferred Master Plan outcome and associated staging framework. Cost estimates shall be prepared in accordance with the requirements of the Scope of Works and be suitable for strategic planning purposes

RFI 5 – Traffic Assessment Scope

The consultant shall undertake a traffic assessment in accordance with the Scope of Works to inform development of the Master Plan, including consideration of site access, circulation, parking and future precinct requirements. Tenderers should allow within their fee for investigations reasonably necessary to satisfy the Scope of Works.

RFI 6 – Flooding and Environmental Assessment Scope

Existing flood and environmental information held by Council, including the Flood Assessment Report, will be provided where available.

The consultant shall review the information provided and undertake the assessments required by the Scope of Works, allowing within their fee for investigations reasonably necessary to inform development of the Master Plan

RFI 7 – Site Servicing Capacity

Relevant servicing information held by Council will be provided where available.

The consultant shall undertake the servicing assessment required by the Scope of Works and allow within their fee for investigations reasonably necessary to inform development of the Master Plan

Dear Procurement Team,

We note that under the Specification, Hard Waste and (Bundled) Green Waste Collection are required to be delivered concurrently under Options A, B and C (Clause 6.1.2(a)), with Option D (User Pays Hard Waste Collection) being the only option that excludes Green Waste.

We would appreciate Council's clarification on the following:

If this is possible, please advise how it should be addressed in our submission (e.g. declared as a Non-Conformance under Schedule 3 with a valued cost impact, delivered via a subcontracted/partnership arrangement for the Green Waste component, or another mechanism Council would accept).

2. If a Hard Waste-only submission is not permissible under Options A, B or C, can Council confirm whether Option D (User Pays Hard Waste Collection) may be tendered for, and potentially awarded, on a standalone basis, independent of the outcome for Options A, B or C?

Thanks for your time in advance.

title: RFT CT2027006 Livestock Marketing Centre: Sheep Loading Ramp Renewal D&C
description:
Wagga Wagga City Council (Council) are improving the loading ramps of the Livestock Marketing Centre (LMC) sheep delivery yards. The ramps, located in the northeast corner of the site, were constructed with the original facility and have reached the end of their useful life. This increases the risk of slips, injuries and creates potential workplace safety and animal welfare concerns.

The project aims to replace the original ramps with modern equipment to ensure safe operating conditions for animals, staff, and operators. Pavement renewal at the base of the ramps will also be undertaken.

The desired outcome of this RFT is to enter into a Lump Sum Contract with an appropriately experienced Contractor for the Design & Construction of new ramps and pavement renewal in accordance with the tender documentation.

The Scope of Works under this RFT is to design new loading ramps, remove the existing ramps, remediating the pavement, and installing new loading ramps.

The works to be performed by the Contractor include the provision of all labour, supervision, materials, equipment, designs, overheads, administration, taxes, wages, accommodation, transport, allowances, consumables, testing services and any other incidental costs, to construct the works in accordance with this Contract.

ON-SITE BRIEFING:

A pre-tender briefing will be held on Tuesday 1st September 2026 at 11AM. The meeting is to be held on-site at the Livestock Marketing Centre, Webb Street, Bomen. Registration to attend the briefing can be made via email procurement@wagga.nsw.gov.au.

Whilst this briefing is not compulsory, consultants are encouraged to attend to obtain a firsthand understanding of the works required.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI 1 - Pile Section dimensions, Wharves 5 and 6

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 5.5; Figure 6 Pile Repair Detail; Appendix E reference drawings 403-003, 403-007, 403-017

The Technical Specification and the Pile Repair Detail at Figure 6 specify a retained core of not less than 250mm x 250mm and reference existing 40mm reinforcing bars, but do not state the overall pile section dimensions.

Of the reference drawings at Appendix E, drawing 303-001 relates to Wharf No. 1 and notes columns of 17" x 19½". Drawing 403-003 is annotated as not proceeded with. Drawing 403-017, which covers the Wharf 5 and Wharf 6 works area, carries the note "WHARF GEOMETRY NOT VERIFIED".

Would the Principal please confirm the pile section dimensions, including corner chamfer, applicable to the piles nominated for repair on Wharves 5 and 6; or confirm that no verified dimensional information is held by the Principal.

Further notes that clause 1.6 states a precise scope of work has not been defined and that the exact extent of repairs will be determined during the Works. Confirmation of the pile section is nonetheless required at tender, as it governs the design and fabrication of reinstatement formwork.

RFI 2 - Release of existing condition survey and investigation reports

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 1.4, 1.5, 7.14; FY26 Works Layout Plan (KBR annotation)

Clause 1.4 of the Scope of Works states that the Priority 1A and 1B defects were identified during a detailed inspection undertaken by KBR in February 2023, that further deterioration has likely occurred since, and that some areas have been repaired since the 2023 condition survey. Clause 7.14 of the Technical Specification quotes concrete cover data attributed to a 1993 report by Beal.

Elouera observed at the Site Inspection that elements beneath the wharf carry survey markings, and that previously executed repairs are visible, consistent with the 2023 rectification works identified on drawing 300-085.

Would the Principal please make available to all Tenderers the KBR February 2023 detailed inspection report, the 1993 Beal report, and any supporting data relied upon in preparing the FY26 Works Layout Plan, including measured element dimensions, chloride profiles, cover meter surveys, delamination survey results and photographic records.

Would the Principal also please advise which elements have been repaired since the 2023 condition survey, and confirm whether those elements are excluded from the present scope.

RFI 3 - Annexure to the General Conditions of Contract

Reference: Conditions of Contract cl. 18, 20, 26; definitions of LD Cap and Operational Delay Allowance

The General Conditions repeatedly refer to particulars stated in the Annexure, including the Date for Practical Completion, the rate of liquidated damages, the LD Cap, the Operational Delay Allowance, the Defects Liability Period, Security and retention, and required insurance limits.

The Annexure does not appear within Parts A to E of the RFT package. Would the Principal please issue the completed Annexure to all Tenderers.

RFI 4 - Quantities for slab soffit and beam repairs

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 4.4(c), cl. 6.1; Part G Prices and Rates Schedule Items 3.00 and 4.00

Clause 6.1 states that precise locations and defined areas for slab soffit and beam repairs have not been defined on the drawings. The FY26 Works Layout Plan identifies 100 soffit panels, 65 primary beams and 15 secondary beams by element count.

Part G requires banded rates per square metre, and clause 4.4(c) provides for payment against the final measured area of each individual patch.

Would the Principal please advise the indicative total repair area, in square metres, anticipated for slab soffit repairs and for beam repairs respectively; and the anticipated distribution of individual patch repairs across the area bands set out at clause 4.4(f). If no such estimate is held, would the Principal please confirm this.

RFI 5 - Split of pile repairs between Type A and Type B

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 5.5; Part G Prices and Rates Schedule Item 2.00

Clause 5.5 requires two types of pile repair to be priced. The FY26 Works Layout Plan identifies 54 piles for repair but does not indicate which are anticipated to be Type A and which Type B.

The two repair types differ materially in extent, Type A being one full face over a 2000mm height and Type B extending from 1.700m Chart Datum to the underside of the slab.

Would the Principal please advise the anticipated number of Type A and Type B pile repairs, or confirm that this allocation is to be determined at the joint inspection under clause 5.2.

RFI 6 - Tenderer access for measurement prior to close of Tender

Reference: Part A — Site Inspection / RFT Briefing; Conditions of Tender cl. 6.2, 6.3

Access at the mandatory Site Inspection on 19 August 2026 was limited to visual observation from the wharf deck. The elements to be repaired are located beneath the wharf deck and were not accessible for inspection or measurement.

Clause 6.2 deems the Tenderer to have inspected the Site and satisfied itself of conditions. In order to discharge that obligation in a meaningful way, would the Principal please confirm in writing whether Tenderers may arrange a further inspection prior to close of Tender with access beneath the wharf deck, including by small vessel, and advise the conditions, notice period, induction and security requirements applicable to such access.

If such access cannot be made available, would the Principal please confirm this in writing.

RFI 7 - Basis of the Principal's estimate of repair extent

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 4.4(d) and Figure 3; cl. 7.9; Conditions of Contract cl. 26

Clause 4.4(d) sets expected repair depths of 150mm for piles, 120mm for slab soffits and 140mm for beams, each with a tolerance of plus or minus 20mm, and provides for rate adjustment where measured depths fall outside that tolerance. Clause 7.9 provides that excessive removal beyond the specified extent is at the Contractor's cost.

Would the Principal please advise the basis on which the expected repair depths at Figure 3 were derived, and confirm whether the Principal anticipates that the actual extent and depth of deterioration may differ materially from those expected values.

Would the Principal further confirm that where measured extents exceed those anticipated to a degree that affects the Contractor's ability to reach Practical Completion by the Date for Practical Completion, the Contractor's entitlement to an extension of time under clause 18 is preserved.

Reference: Part A — RFT Package Details; Technical Specification cl. 4.4

RFI 9 - Approved Budget and its relationship to the scope of works

Reference: Scope of Works cl. 1.6, 1.7, 1.8; Conditions of Contract — Date for Practical Completion

Clause 1.7 provides that tendered Fixed Costs and Rates, combined with on-site measurement, will be used to track and forecast project costs up to an approved budget to be advised by the Principal at contract formation. Clause 1.8 provides that the approved budget must not be exceeded by the Contractor unless approved in writing.

The approved budget is therefore not disclosed to Tenderers at the time of pricing, yet governs the volume of work that may be executed under the Contract.

(a) the approved budget, or an indicative range, to enable Tenderers to assess the likely volume of work and resource it accordingly;

(b) the mechanism by which the Works will proceed if the approved budget is reached before all nominated elements have been repaired — specifically whether the Contractor is to cease work, whether Practical Completion is achieved at that point, and how Preliminaries are treated for the balance of the Contract period; and

(c) whether the quantities shown on the FY26 Works Layout Plan, being 54 piles, 100 soffit panels, 65 primary beams and 15 secondary beams, are within the approved budget at the Principal's own estimate of rates.

RFI 10 - Pile head haunching and termination of Type B repairs

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 5.5(d); Figure 6 Pile Repair Detail; observed conditions at Site Inspection

Clause 5.5(d) provides that Type B pile repairs shall extend from 1.700m Chart Datum to the underside of the slab. Figure 6 depicts the pile as a prismatic section of constant dimension.

Would the Principal please advise:

(a) whether Type B repairs are required to extend through the haunched pile head to the underside of the slab, or are to terminate below the commencement of the haunch;

(b) if the haunch is included, whether reinstatement of the haunch profile is deemed included in the Type B pile repair rate or is to be measured separately; and

(c) whether any dimensional information for the haunch geometry is held by the Principal.

RFI 11 - Removal of marine growth

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 9.10 Surface Preparation; cl. 14.4 Silane Application; Part G Prices and Rates Schedule

Elouera observed dense marine growth, including oyster and barnacle encrustation, extending a substantial height up the piles from the bed. Removal of this growth is a necessary precursor to hydro-demolition, to reinstatement, and to silane application on any surface within the affected zone.

The Technical Specification addresses surface preparation at clause 9.10 but does not identify removal of marine growth, and no corresponding item is evident in the payment mechanism at clause 4.4.

Would the Principal please confirm whether removal and disposal of marine growth is deemed included within the tendered pile repair rates, or is to be measured and paid separately; and confirm any environmental controls required for its capture and disposal under the Environmental Management Plan.

RFI 12 - Heritage General Exemption Certificate

Reference: Scope of Works cl. 2.1, 2.2

Clause 2.2 provides that work shall not commence until the Principal has confirmed that the General Exemption Certificate — Queensland Heritage Places will apply to this project.

Would the Principal please confirm whether that certificate has been obtained or confirmed as applicable as at the date of tender; and if not, advise the anticipated timing and confirm that any delay to commencement arising from it will be treated as an act or omission of the Principal for the purposes of extension of time under clause 18.

RFI 13 - Hydro-demolition working hours and tidal working windows

Reference: Scope of Works cl. 8.3(a), 8.3(b); cl. 8.5(b)

Clause 8.3(a) permits working hours between 6.00am and 6.30pm, Monday to Sunday. Clause 8.3(b) provides that there shall be no excessively noisy activities such as hydro-demolition before 8.00am or after 5.00pm, giving an effective nine-hour window for concrete removal.

The elements to be repaired are tidal. Type B pile repairs commence at 1.700m Chart Datum, which the Specification identifies as Mean Sea Level, and are accessible only during low-water windows. Those windows advance by approximately 50 minutes each day and will regularly fall wholly or partly outside the 8.00am to 5.00pm period.

Would the Principal please confirm:

(a) whether the Superintendent will consider approval under clause 8.3(a) for hydro-demolition to be undertaken outside 8.00am to 5.00pm where a low-water working window falls outside those hours, and the basis on which such approval would be assessed; and

(b) whether any noise limits, monitoring requirements or conditions apply, having regard to nearby residential receivers.

RFI 14 - Maritime Security Identification Cards

Reference: Scope of Works cl. 8.2(g); General Conditions of Contract cl. 7.3

Clause 8.2(g) of the Scope of Works states that it is expected Maritime Security Identification Cards will not be required, as the works are being undertaken around vessel operations.

Clause 7.3(a) of the General Conditions provides that if the work is required to be performed in maritime security zones, at least two employees of the Contractor must hold an MSIC, with all associated costs borne by the Contractor.

Would the Principal please confirm which position applies to these works, and whether any part of the Wharf 5 and Wharf 6 works area is designated a maritime security zone.

The Mackay Regional Council area is one of the fastest growing regions in Queensland. Covering the areas of the former Sarina and Mirani shires and Mackay city, it extends 7261 square kilometres.

With a population of around 110,000 as at June 2008 and a projected annual growth rate of 2.1 per cent, the region’s estimated population in 2031 is about 173,000 people.

Its coastal location is complemented by its spectacular natural environment. This includes 31 beautiful beaches, a picturesque blue river and a pristine rainforest hinterland.

Only an hour’s flight from Brisbane, the Mackay region boasts an enviable lifestyle and a buoyant economy with the benefits of a fastgrowing coastal city. It is the gateway to the rich coal deposits in the Bowen basin.

title: Mental Health Wellbeing Investment Package ITO
description:
The Package is being delivered through a partnership-based approach, working across Queensland Government, with up to six government partner agencies, to implement strategic funding partnerships. The Commission has established a group with representatives from each partner agency, to support coordination, collective impact measurement, shared learning and governance oversight across the package.

The partnerships fund a range of initiatives including, a mix of place-based activities, community and local council grant programs, cross-sector collaboration, and activities that strengthen workforce capability, service integration, and policy and practice across systems. Activities are delivered across metropolitan, regional, and remote Queensland. Timing of initiatives will be staggered across financial years FY2025/2026 to mid FY2028/2029.

The Commission requires an external Supplier to undertake an independent evaluation of the previous Grants and the Package, including development of an evaluation framework, to assess mental health and wellbeing outcomes and broader system impacts. The Supplier will be expected to design practical data collection and reporting approaches that partners can reasonably implement within existing operational environments.

The evaluation will also examine the collaborative approach between the Commission and government partners to inform future policy and reform directions. The Supplier will be expected to take a collaborative and developmental evaluation approach, working alongside the Commission and government partners over the life of the Package to support learning, adaptation, and continuous improvement, rather than undertaking a single end-point evaluation.

The evaluation is intended to inform future cross-government investment approaches, strengthen the evidence base for mental health promotion and prevention, and provide practical insights to inform ongoing mental health and wellbeing system reform and policy development in Queensland.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
The Queensland Mental Health Commission (the Commission) is a statutory body established under the Queensland Mental Health Commission Act 2013 to drive systemic reform across Queensland’s mental health, alcohol and other drugs, and suicide prevention systems. A core function of the Commission is to develop and facilitate implementation of a whole-of-government strategic plan to improve mental health and wellbeing outcomes for Queenslanders. The current plans, Shifting minds: The Queensland Mental Health, Alcohol and Other Drugs, and Suicide Prevention Strategic Plan 2023-2028 (Shifting minds) and its associated sub-plans; The Queensland Trauma Strategy 2024-2029, Achieving balance: The Queensland Alcohol and Other Drugs Plan 2022-2027 and Every life: The Queensland Suicide Prevention Plan 2019-2029 Phase Two, provides the overarching framework for this work.

In addition, in response to Recommendation 19 of the 2022 Queensland Parliament Mental Health Select Committee Inquiry into opportunities to improve mental health outcomes for Queenslanders, Thriving Lives, Connected Communities – Queensland’s Commitment to Mental Health and Wellbeing (Thriving Lives, Connected Communities) was developed to provide a focused direction for improving community mental health and wellbeing.

Recommendation 19 – Develop Mental Health and Wellbeing Strategy

The committee recommends the Queensland Government considers the development of a population based Mental Health and Wellbeing Strategy that works across human services portfolios and is aimed at improving community mental health and wellbeing.

Time-limited, non-recurrent funding has been provided to the Commission to progress priorities identified in Thriving Lives, Connected Communities.

In 2025, the Commission delivered the Mental Health and Wellbeing Grants program, (the Grants) distributing $2.8 million across 22 projects to strengthen community mental health and wellbeing through mental health promotion, prevention and early intervention initiatives.

Building on the Grants, the Commission established the Mental Health and Wellbeing Investment Package (the Package), a targeted, time-limited investment of $9 million that adopts a strategic and coordinated approach. The Package supports initiatives that strengthen population-based mental health and wellbeing through mental health promotion and prevention, while leveraging existing systems, infrastructure and partnerships to maximise impact, reduce duplication and support sustainability beyond the funding period.

publicQuestions.question: For engagement of people with lived and living experience (LLE) in the design and delivery of the evaluation (e.g. contributing to the evaluation plan, methods and other project deliverables, rather than participating as research participants in data collection activities), does the Commission have existing LLE advisory groups, networks, panels or engagement mechanisms that the successful supplier will be able to access, or will the supplier be responsible for recruiting LLE contributors for this purpose in addition to participant recruitment for data collection activities?
publicQuestions.answer:
Hi Sophie,

The Commission may have existing networks and engagement mechanisms that could be drawn upon to support Lived-Living Expertise involvement. However, suppliers should propose an approach to engaging people with Lived-Living Expertise, in line with the ITO requirements, that aligns with their proposed methodology and approach to the evaluation.

Suppliers are encouraged to consider how they would identify and engage appropriate Lived-Living Expertise contributors, including where their own networks or recruitment approaches may be required.

Kind regards,

Jasmine Repia

Queensland Mental Health Commission

publicQuestions.question: The Commission requires remuneration of engaged LLE participants. Should these costs be included within the supplier's proposed budget, or will the Commission manage these costs separately? If suppliers are expected to budget for participation, can the Commission provide guidance regarding the anticipated number and frequency of LLE engagement activities over the course of the evaluation?
publicQuestions.answer:
Hi Sophie,

As outlined in Part A (Section 1.2) of the ITO, the Supplier is required to provide remuneration to people with Lived-Living Expertise engaged in consultation, collaboration or co-design, at a minimum, in line with the Commission’s paid participation rates.

In addition, the Selection Criteria (refer to Parts A and C of the ITO) specify that “the Supplier’s budget must reflect appropriate allocation to personnel, engagement (including paid participation for people with Lived-Living Expertise) and reporting.” Suppliers should therefore include costs associated with paid participation within their proposed budget.

The Selection Criteria also require suppliers to demonstrate “how people with Lived-Living Expertise will be involved throughout all stages of the evaluation, including its design, delivery, interpretation of findings and knowledge translation.”

The ITO has not prescribed a specific number or frequency of engagement activities. Suppliers should propose an approach to Lived-Living Expertise involvement in line with the ITO requirements, that is appropriate to their proposed project and evaluation methodology.

Kind regards,

Jasmine Repia

Queensland Mental Health Commissions

changes.to:
The Package is being delivered through a partnership-based approach, working across Queensland Government, with up to six government partner agencies, to implement strategic funding partnerships. The Commission has established a group with representatives from each partner agency, to support coordination, collective impact measurement, shared learning and governance oversight across the package.

The partnerships fund a range of initiatives including, a mix of place-based activities, community and local council grant programs, cross-sector collaboration, and activities that strengthen workforce capability, service integration, and policy and practice across systems. Activities are delivered across metropolitan, regional, and remote Queensland. Timing of initiatives will be staggered across financial years FY2025/2026 to mid FY2028/2029.

The Commission requires an external Supplier to undertake an independent evaluation of the previous Grants and the Package, including development of an evaluation framework, to assess mental health and wellbeing outcomes and broader system impacts. The Supplier will be expected to design practical data collection and reporting approaches that partners can reasonably implement within existing operational environments.

The evaluation will also examine the collaborative approach between the Commission and government partners to inform future policy and reform directions. The Supplier will be expected to take a collaborative and developmental evaluation approach, working alongside the Commission and government partners over the life of the Package to support learning, adaptation, and continuous improvement, rather than undertaking a single end-point evaluation.

The evaluation is intended to inform future cross-government investment approaches, strengthen the evidence base for mental health promotion and prevention, and provide practical insights to inform ongoing mental health and wellbeing system reform and policy development in Queensland.

title: New England Highway Chalk Drive Cycleway Upgrades

publicQuestions.question:
Good Morning,

For clarification please:

ISO 27001 - Mandatory Criteria

Where a Respondents use Microsoft 365 environments for its information and record management but does not itself hold ISO 27001 certification, please confirm whether Council will accept providing Microsoft’s current ISO/IEC 27001 certification as evidence of compliance with this mandatory criterion?

Data Transfer / System Access – Scope

Please confirm how Council intends to provide debtor account data to the successful Contractor, for example via Excel/CSV files, secure file transfer, access to Council systems, or another method? Please also confirm whether any direct system integration is required?

Pricing - Tender Form Price

Council does not guarantee referral volumes or committed work, however the Tender Form requests a single total Price. Please confirm what Tenderers should enter as the total Price in the Tender Form?

Legal Recovery / Sale of Land - Subcontracting

Where a Respondent proposes to use subcontractors for legal recovery and Sale of Land activities, please confirm whether Council will accept an approved external law firm for these services.
publicQuestions.answer:
1 - Whilst desirable, ISO 27001 compliance/certification is not mandatory. We will issue an amendment to the scope.

2 - Council can provide the information via Excel/CSV Files either via email or secure file transfer depending on the Contractors systems and requirements.

Direct system integration is not required.

3 - As per the page 23 of the T-MSC2026-05_Response_Schedule.docx - please provide a detailed outline of all costs associated with the provision of this service, including any applicable fees, charges and other costs.

4 - Council confirms that it is acceptable for a Respondent to engage an approved external law firm to undertake legal recovery and Sale of Land activities, subject to the Respondent remaining responsible for the performance of the subcontracted services and ensuring compliance with all applicable legislation, Council policies and contractual requirements.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-001

Issue: Pricing Schedule Item 1.4.3 prices 40 m of groundwater "pipe type C", but Specification S13 defines only a Type A collection pipe (OD 250 PE100 PN20, cl.7.1.1) and a Type B panel drain (cl.7.1.2). "Type C" is not defined anywhere.

RFI-002

Issue: Pricing Schedule Item 1.4.4 prices "supply and install groundwater sump/pit" as 2 lump sums. S13 cl.7.1.4 and cl.7.4.2 describe a precast concrete manhole-type structure "as shown in the drawings", but no sump dimensions, precast size/class, depth/invert levels, base-slab or lid (load class), or pipe-inlet/grouting detail is provided.

Clarification: Provide the sump/pit design details (structure type and dimensions, precast size/class, depth and invert levels, base-slab and lid load class, pipe-inlet/grouting), or issue the relevant drawing/typical detail, so the 2 sumps can be priced.

RFI-003

Issue: S13 cl.12.4 requires precast Class 3 RCP culverts (MRTS03/MRTS24) with headwalls (SD1243), wingwalls (SD1304) and bedding (SD1359), and cl.12.5 states "culverts shall not be measured", all components deemed included in the work item. The Pricing Schedule contains no culvert/headwall pay item and no lump-sum line for the culvert work to be deemed into.

Clarification: Confirm whether culverts and headwalls are within this package and, if so, the pay item under which they are to be included.

RFI-004

Issue: Concrete barrier locations are identifiable on the drawings but are not referenced in the Council Specification, Specification S13 or the Pricing Schedule, and no barrier pay item exists in the BOQ.

Clarification: Confirm whether precast concrete barriers are included under this Contract and, if so, provide the design details (type, dimensions, quantity and footing/anchorage) and the pay item; if none are required, confirm they are excluded from scope.

RFI-005

Issue: Pricing Schedule Item 1.3.6 prices a provisional in-situ subgrade stabilisation (Type D) but nominates no binder (cement or lime), no binder content/application rate, and no treatment depth.

Clarification: For the in-situ stabilisation provisional item, nominate the binder type (e.g. GP cement or lime), the application rate (% by mass or kg/m²), and the treatment depth (confirm 150–300 mm).

RFI-006

Issue: The design set includes a Haul Road Layout Plan and Longitudinal Section (Drawings 015 and 016) and S13 cl.13 specifies roadworks (Type 2.1 pavement to MRTS05, guideposts), but the Pricing Schedule contains no pay item for the haul road.

Clarification: Confirm whether construction of the permanent haul road (Drawings 015 and 016) is included in the scope of this proposal. If so, issue the pay item, the pavement/subgrade-improvement standard and the quantity; if not, confirm it is excluded.

publicQuestions.question: We note that the geotech report provided indicates that TP01-TP07 identified suitable clay material for the Clay Fill, however it also states that all Test Pits failed the Emerson Class requirements. Can Council please specify what treatment is to be expected to modify the in-situ material to meet the required specification?
publicQuestions.answer:
The Principal confirms that the on-site clay material identified within TP01–TP07 is suitable for use as Clay Fill without modification or treatment specifically in response to the Emerson Class results.

Stabilisation, including lime treatment of the identifeid Clay Fill material, is not required or included in the design.

General preparation must be undertaken in accordance with Clause 5.5.1 of the Civil and Earthworks Specification (S13).

General Surface Preparation Types A, B, C and D remain provisional items within the Pricing Schedule and must be priced accordingly. The requirement for any of these provisional treatments will be determined based on the conditions encountered during the works and direction under the Contract.

Should imported Clay Fill material be required, the imported material must comply with the requirements of the Specification.

publicQuestions.question: We note proposed PC date of 7th of May, can council confirm if this date is negotiable? Constructing a landfill cell, especially utilising GCL is extremely risky in the wet season, ideally these works would be completed in the drier months.
publicQuestions.answer:
Council acknowledges the Tenderer's concerns regarding the proposed Practical Completion date and the risks associated with landfill cell construction, particularly GCL installation during the wet season.

Tenderers are required to submit a conforming offer based on the Practical Completion date and requirements specified in the Tender Documents.

Where a Tenderer considers that an alternative construction programme and/or Practical Completion date would provide an improved delivery outcome, this may be submitted as an alternative offer in addition to the required conforming offer.

Any alternative programme will be considered by Council as part of the tender evaluation process. Acceptance of an alternative programme or Practical Completion date is at Council's discretion and should not be assumed for the purposes of the conforming tender.

title: Development of Fleet Management System Using TechnologyOne Works & Asset Management
description:
Lithgow City Council invites quotations from suitably qualified vendors to design, configure, and implement a comprehensive Fleet Management System using TechnologyOne’s Works & Asset Management (WAM) modules.

Council manages a fleet of approximately 200 vehicles and plant items, including light vehicles, heavy plant, trucks, and specialised operational equipment. The new system must support the full lifecycle of these assets, from procurement and maintenance through to financial reporting and replacement forecasting.

This RFQ forms part of Council’s Fleet Management Project and aims to establish a modern, integrated, and sustainable fleet management capability.

See attached file for full details of RFQ.

Lithgow, New South Wales 2790
Australia

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Project Objectives

Council requires a solution that:

•	Establishes a complete and accurate Fleet Asset Register within TechnologyOne WAM.

•	Supports reactive and proactive maintenance, including scheduling, work orders, and cost tracking.

•	Integrates procurement workflows for fuel, registration, CTP, external servicing, and other fleet-related expenses.

•	Provides custodianship tracking for fleet assets.

•	Delivers robust financial reporting, including asset valuation, lifecycle costing, replacement forecasting, and fuel tax credit reporting.

•	Ensures high quality data migration, system configuration, and testing.

•	Includes training to build internal capability and system ownership.

•	Offers options for ongoing support and system health management.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi, May I please request clarifications on the below items:

1. Maintenance strategy — scope boundary

Section 3.2 refers to "development of maintenance schedules, worksheets

and allocation processes." Can Council confirm whether this means

configuring maintenance regimes Council has already defined, or

developing those regimes as part of this engagement?

Specifically, does Council currently hold documented service intervals

and task content by asset class (light vehicles, trucks, heavy plant,

specialised equipment), criticality ratings, and a componentisation and

useful life schedule for the fleet — or is establishing these within

scope? The distinction materially affects effort and price, and we

would prefer to price it explicitly rather than carry it as an

assumption.

Also the tender specifically requests two separate skillsets, the configuration of tech one, and the asset management component (Which falls out of most IT firm capability).

My firm has deep expertise in the asset management component and experience with various CMMC's, but not directly within TechOne (Although this can be done via user manuals)- Can council advise if it is possible to provide a proposal for the Asset Management section of work only? Or if council would hard-stop a proposal without direct TechOne experience?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council already maintains vehicle service schedules and maintenance intervals. Our intent is not to develop the maintenance regimes themselves, but rather to configure these schedules within TechnologyOne so that the system can automatically generate maintenance notifications, work orders, and related workflows. We also expect the successful respondent to configure checklist-style maintenance activities that can be completed through the TechnologyOne mobile inspection module.

We recognise that the requirement for TechnologyOne Works & Asset Management experience may reduce the number of potential respondents. However, the use of TechnologyOne is a mandatory project requirement, as Council already holds the relevant licensing and is seeking to maximise the value of its existing investment while avoiding the ongoing licensing costs associated with introducing an alternative platform.

publicQuestions.question: Is it possible to have a week extension. There is considerable collation of information required and the existing one-week timeline does not allow a thoughtful response.
publicQuestions.answer: Unfortunately an extension is not possible. We do understand that this is an extremely tight time frame.

title: RFQ260197 - Emerald Saleyards Dip Yards Redesign Construct
description:
Central Highlands Regional Council (Council) operates the Emerald Saleyards and has a clearing dip which services thousands of cattle each year. Council's current objective is to upgrade existing areas and utilise spaces that will overall improve operational use and provide a safer and more reliable working environment.

Council have provided draft/concept drawings for the addition of gates to the Emerald Saleyards dip area, currently it has 90-degree passages with pull down portable panels. Construction to the area will optimize cattle flow and accessibility, improving livestock welfare, driving higher processing volumes and increased sales.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
The Central Highlands region is in Central Queensland, Australia. The region encompasses an area of around 60 000 square kilometres, making it just short of the size of Tasmania.

It is home to around 30 000 people who live in the thirteen unique communities of Arcadia Valley, Bauhinia, Blackwater, Bluff, Capella, Comet, Dingo, Duaringa, Emerald, Rolleston, Sapphire Gemfields, Springsure and Tieri.

Our region is rich in minerals and agriculture, thriving on irrigation sourced from water storage on the Nogoa and Comet rivers. We claim the largest sapphire-producing fields in the Southern Hemisphere.

Major freight routes through the region include the north-south link between Charters Towers and northern New South Wales—identified as the inland transport alternative between Cairns and Melbourne.

description:

Fraser Coast Regional Council is inviting offers from suitably qualified and experienced Tenderers for CTDC003 - 26/27 - Provision for Mowing, Slashing and Streetscape Maintenance across FCRC LGA.

This invitation to offer is in separable portions. The Principal may only award any portion depending on funding availability. The Principal requires the tenderer to price all portions or part portions and also provide a discount if awarded more than one (1) portion in one process.

The Principal may award part or whole of the contract to a single Tenderer or to a panel of Tenderers.

The ITO comprises six (6) Separable Portions. Tenderers may submit for one, multiple or all Separable Portions. Council may award any combination of Separable Portions to one or more Contractors to achieve the best overall value for money, capability, service resilience and service outcomes.

Further details in the Tender documentation.

NON-MANDATORY TENDER BRIEFING

A Tender Briefing is not mandatory for this tender. The details are outlined below:

Date: Wednesday, 19 August 2026

Time 11:30am (AEST) (for approx. 30 minutes to 1 hour)

Location: TEAMS MEETING or you can attend in person with location being: Hervey Bay Neighbourhood Centre (Hall B) at 22 Charles Street, Pialba QLD 4655

Booking Required: YES - State: name, position, mobile number and email address of person/s attending and whether they are attending by TEAMS (so we can send a link to TEAMS meeting or in person.

Point of Contact for Booking: Email - procurement@frasercoast.qld.gov.au

Other Details (incl. Dress Code / PPE): N/A

SUBMISSION OF TENDER DOCUMENTS

Please be advised that tender response forms are to be submitted as two files only and in the following format:

 - Non-Price Response Form: PDF including all supporting documentation as one file. This PDF must not contain any price related criteria.

 - Price Response Form: Excel

Failure to comply with this requirement may result in a non-conforming offer.

title: RFT260086 - Long-Term Residual Waste Solution — Standardised Site Assessment
description:
Central Highlands Regional Council (CHRC) invites suitably qualified consultants to submit tenders for RFT260086 – Long-Term Residual Waste Solution – Standardised Site Assessment.

The engagement is for a strategic waste planning consultancy to undertake a comprehensive, evidence-based assessment of Council's long-term (30–50 year) residual waste disposal solution. The successful consultant will reconcile the remaining life of the existing Lochlees Resource Recovery and Landfill Facility, model long-term residual waste demand, develop a standardised assessment methodology, evaluate potential long-term disposal options against the Queensland Landfill Siting, Design, Operation and Rehabilitation Guideline (ESR/2015/1627), and prepare a defensible options report to inform future Council decision-making.

This is a desktop strategic planning and technical assessment. It does not include detailed engineering design, statutory approvals, land acquisition, or intrusive field investigations, which are outside the scope of this procurement.

The consultancy is expected to commence shortly following contract award and be completed over an approximately six-month period. Services may be undertaken remotely; however, attendance at key meetings and site inspections in Emerald, Queensland, will be required during the engagement.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerAddress:
65 Egerton St
Emerald, Queensland 4720
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
The Central Highlands region is in Central Queensland, Australia. The region encompasses an area of around 60 000 square kilometres, making it just short of the size of Tasmania.

It is home to around 30 000 people who live in the thirteen unique communities of Arcadia Valley, Bauhinia, Blackwater, Bluff, Capella, Comet, Dingo, Duaringa, Emerald, Rolleston, Sapphire Gemfields, Springsure and Tieri.

Our region is rich in minerals and agriculture, thriving on irrigation sourced from water storage on the Nogoa and Comet rivers. We claim the largest sapphire-producing fields in the Southern Hemisphere.

Major freight routes through the region include the north-south link between Charters Towers and northern New South Wales—identified as the inland transport alternative between Cairns and Melbourne.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Central Highlands Regional Council (CHRC) operates the Lochlees Resource Recovery and Landfill Facility at Emerald as its principal regional residual waste disposal facility. With the remaining capacity of the existing landfill being finite, Council is undertaking strategic planning to identify the most appropriate long-term (30–50 year) residual waste solution for the region. This procurement forms part of that strategic planning process and does not represent a decision to develop or acquire any particular site.

Tenderers should demonstrate experience in strategic landfill planning, waste infrastructure planning, environmental assessment, and multi-criteria options analysis within the Queensland regulatory environment. Experience applying the Queensland Landfill Siting, Design, Operation and Rehabilitation Guideline (ESR/2015/1627), landfill capacity modelling, life-cycle costing, GIS-based spatial assessment, and facilitation of strategic decision-making for local government or similar organisations will be highly regarded.

Council will provide relevant background information, including previous investigations, landfill survey information, airspace and stockpile data, waste generation information, existing planning studies and other reference material identified within the tender documentation. Tenderers are expected to validate and appropriately use this information while exercising independent professional judgement.

The successful consultant will be required to:

- Work collaboratively with Council's project team throughout the engagement.

- Attend key project meetings and undertake site inspections at Emerald where required.

- Provide all reports, models and supporting documentation in fully editable electronic formats.

- Develop a transparent, evidence-based and independently defensible assessment methodology.

- Cooperate with an independently appointed peer reviewer engaged separately by Council for review of the assessment methodology.

The engagement is a professional services consultancy only. Intrusive field investigations, statutory approvals, detailed engineering design, land acquisition activities and other downstream implementation works are expressly excluded from this procurement and, if required, will be commissioned under separate engagements.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
Council seeks a consultant that can deliver a transparent, evidence-based and independently defensible assessment of long-term residual waste disposal options that will support future strategic decision-making.

The successful consultant should:

- Deliver a robust, standardised assessment methodology capable of objectively comparing all reasonable long-term residual waste options on a consistent basis.

- Produce clear, high-quality technical reports and supporting models that are fully editable and suitable for future refinement and downstream planning.

- Demonstrate a sound understanding of Queensland landfill planning, environmental constraints, waste infrastructure planning and strategic options assessment.

- Apply recognised industry best practice and relevant Queensland regulatory guidance throughout the engagement.

- Provide practical, well-reasoned recommendations supported by documented assumptions, analysis and evidence.

- Maintain proactive communication, meet agreed project milestones, and work collaboratively with Council's project team throughout the engagement.

- Respond constructively to Council feedback and the independently commissioned methodology peer review within the agreed programme.

- Deliver all services within the agreed fixed lump-sum fee and project timeframe.

Council is seeking a consultant capable of becoming a trusted strategic advisor for this engagement by combining strong technical capability with practical understanding of local government decision-making, risk management and long-term infrastructure planning. The successful outcome will provide Council with a defensible evidence base to support future decisions regarding its long-term residual waste disposal strategy, while recognising that this engagement does not commit Council to any particular site, development or capital project.

title: Pick of the Crop 2027-28 expansion to Far North Queensland
description:
HWQld is Queensland’s dedicated prevention agency established to prevent chronic disease and improve health equity, with a focus on healthy eating, physical activity and obesity.

HWQld has committed to implementing a whole-school healthy eating program in all state primary schools across Queensland to increase children’s vegetable and fruit consumption. Pick of the Crop (POTC) is a whole school, multi-strategic, evidence-based healthy eating initiative developed by HWQld; it is flexible and designed by schools to focus on their unique community needs and school environment.

HWQld seeks to engage one or more Implementation partner/s in a two-year agreement to support delivery of POTC across Far North Queensland's Department of Education (DoE) regions.

Implementation Partner/s will be responsible for recruiting and managing a regional coordinator and supporting school engagement, implementation and stakeholder collaboration.

Key activities are expected to include:

 •	Recruitment, onboarding and support of a Regional Coordinator.

 •	School engagement, recruitment and relationship management activities to achieve school participation targets.

 •	Support at least 15 new schools per DoE region each year to develop and implement School Action Plans and approval processes.

 •	Support schools to apply for grants administered by HWQld and associated reporting requirements.

 •	Facilitate access to POTC resources, professional learning opportunities and implementation support.

 •	Coordinate stakeholder engagement and regional partnerships that strengthen POTC delivery.

 •	Ongoing support to participating schools to embed and sustain locally run activities.

 •	Collect required data and contribute to monitoring, evaluation and reporting activities.

 •	Prepare implementation insights and lessons learned to inform ongoing POTC development and continuous improvement.

 •	Networking with other POTC coordinators across the state, working in partnership and collaboration.

The Regional Coordinator is the primary point of contact for participating schools and stakeholders and will support the successful implementation, growth and sustainability of POTC across the region and state.

Key aims of POTC are:

 o	All Qld primary school students develop the knowledge, attitudes and skills to make healthy food choices through quality learning experiences, which are reinforced by supportive environments at school and at home.

 o	All Qld primary school educators have the capability and resources to deliver quality nutrition education learning experiences consistent with, and integrated across, the school curriculum.

 o	Build capacity and capability of communities to support schools increase student’s intake of vegetables and fruit.

Key Objectives for schools align with the World Health Organisation’s Health Promoting Schools framework. These are:

 1. Teaching and Learning: integrate food and nutrition education into the curriculum. Students will learn and gain knowledge, skills and experiences that will promote greater consumption of vegetables and fruit.

 2. Healthy School Environments: provide opportunities for students to access vegetables and fruit by incorporating them into the school tuckshop, breakfast clubs, brain breaks, tasting activities and establishing school gardens.

 3. Grower and Community Connections: strengthen connections with growers and producers (from Paddock to Plate), and implement engagement strategies with the community, families, parents and beyond.

Implementation of POTC regionally involves funding provided to local organisations (called Implementation Partners) under a negotiated Service Agreement with defined performance measures and contract deliverables.

For more detailed information please see the attached Request for Quote Information Document and supporting material.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
POTC is a tried and test model, demonstrated to be feasible for schools and teachers to implement and resulting in changes to students’ attitudes and beliefs towards vegetables and fruit consistent with project objectives.

Program need

Most Queensland (Qld) children do not meet the Australian Dietary Guideline recommendations:

 •	Only 3.2% of Queensland children aged 5 to 11 years are eating the recommended amount of 5 vegetables every day.

 •	80.7% of children eat the recommended 2 serves of fruit every day.

 •	39% of total energy intake of 4 to 8-year old males and 36% of females comes from unhealthy food and drinks.

 •	In 2022, research commissioned by HWQld found that children born in Queensland in 2023 could lose up to 4 years of life expectancy if obesity rates are not reversed, increasing up to 5 years for First Nations children.

Schools are ideal settings to reach large numbers of children, their families and communities and can shape their values and foster lifelong habits.

The overall goal of POTC is to achieve a sustained increase in vegetable and fruit consumption among primary school aged children in Queensland.

HWQld Strategic Alignment

POTC started with 35 state (primary) schools in three regional areas (Bowen, Bundaberg and Logan) as a pilot in 2021 to support HWQld’s commitment to increasing vegetable and fruit consumption for Queensland’s children, and since then has grown to reach 300 state schools with more than 70,000 student enrolments across Queensland. The vision for POTC is for all Queensland primary schools to have an opportunity to implement POTC by 2032.

changes.to:
HWQld is Queensland’s dedicated prevention agency established to prevent chronic disease and improve health equity, with a focus on healthy eating, physical activity and obesity.

HWQld has committed to implementing a whole-school healthy eating program in all state primary schools across Queensland to increase children’s vegetable and fruit consumption. Pick of the Crop (POTC) is a whole school, multi-strategic, evidence-based healthy eating initiative developed by HWQld; it is flexible and designed by schools to focus on their unique community needs and school environment.

HWQld seeks to engage one or more Implementation partner/s in a two-year agreement to support delivery of POTC across Far North Queensland's Department of Education (DoE) regions.

Implementation Partner/s will be responsible for recruiting and managing a regional coordinator and supporting school engagement, implementation and stakeholder collaboration.

Key activities are expected to include:

 •	Recruitment, onboarding and support of a Regional Coordinator.

 •	School engagement, recruitment and relationship management activities to achieve school participation targets.

 •	Support at least 15 new schools per DoE region each year to develop and implement School Action Plans and approval processes.

 •	Support schools to apply for grants administered by HWQld and associated reporting requirements.

 •	Facilitate access to POTC resources, professional learning opportunities and implementation support.

 •	Coordinate stakeholder engagement and regional partnerships that strengthen POTC delivery.

 •	Ongoing support to participating schools to embed and sustain locally run activities.

 •	Collect required data and contribute to monitoring, evaluation and reporting activities.

 •	Prepare implementation insights and lessons learned to inform ongoing POTC development and continuous improvement.

 •	Networking with other POTC coordinators across the state, working in partnership and collaboration.

The Regional Coordinator is the primary point of contact for participating schools and stakeholders and will support the successful implementation, growth and sustainability of POTC across the region and state.

Key aims of POTC are:

 o	All Qld primary school students develop the knowledge, attitudes and skills to make healthy food choices through quality learning experiences, which are reinforced by supportive environments at school and at home.

 o	All Qld primary school educators have the capability and resources to deliver quality nutrition education learning experiences consistent with, and integrated across, the school curriculum.

 o	Build capacity and capability of communities to support schools increase student’s intake of vegetables and fruit.

Key Objectives for schools align with the World Health Organisation’s Health Promoting Schools framework. These are:

 1. Teaching and Learning: integrate food and nutrition education into the curriculum. Students will learn and gain knowledge, skills and experiences that will promote greater consumption of vegetables and fruit.

 2. Healthy School Environments: provide opportunities for students to access vegetables and fruit by incorporating them into the school tuckshop, breakfast clubs, brain breaks, tasting activities and establishing school gardens.

 3. Grower and Community Connections: strengthen connections with growers and producers (from Paddock to Plate), and implement engagement strategies with the community, families, parents and beyond.

Implementation of POTC regionally involves funding provided to local organisations (called Implementation Partners) under a negotiated Service Agreement with defined performance measures and contract deliverables.

For more detailed information please see the attached Request for Quote Information Document and supporting material.
