title: Installation of Pergola Roofing Over Existing Cement Slabs - 6 Units – Capella
description:
Installation of Pergola Roofing over Existing Cement Slabs for 6 Units.

There will be a Mandatory Site Inspection:

Date: Wednesday, 9 September 2026

Time: 10.00am

Place: Meet at 13 Malvern Street, Capella Qld

**Please register your attendance by 7 September 5pm**

The Contractor is to provide all labour, materials, plant, equipment, supervision and associated works necessary for the supply and installation of pergola roofing over the

existing concrete slabs at six (6) units.

The works are to be completed in accordance with the relevant Australian Standards, manufacturer’s requirements and applicable Building Regulations.

Site Verification

• Verify the existing slab dimensions, levels, condition and suitability for the proposed pergola structure.

• Confirm all dimensions, locations and site conditions prior to fabrication and installation.

• Dimensions shown in the documentation are indicative only. The Contractor is responsible for confirming all actual dimensions on site.

• Identify and confirm the location of any existing services that may affect the works.

• Undertake a Site Inspection of all six (6) units prior to commencing works.

Pergola Structure

• Supply and install the complete pergola framing structure, including posts, beams, rafters, brackets, fixings and associated components.

• Provide suitable structural connections between the pergola structure and the existing slab/building, as required by the design.

• Ensure all structural members are appropriately sized and designed for the site conditions and applicable wind loads.

• Provide corrosion-resistant fixings and connections suitable for the location.

• Ensure the structure is adequately braced and securely fixed.

• Provide appropriate clearances from existing buildings, doors, windows and other structures.

Roof

• Supply and install roofing over the pergola structure.

• Roofing material is to be suitable for the location and comply with the approved design.

• Provide all required flashings, trims, closures, gutters and associated roofing accessories.

• Ensure roofing is securely fixed and weatherproof.

• Provide appropriate roof falls to ensure effective stormwater drainage.

• Ensure roof drainage does not discharge onto adjoining properties, access paths or areas where it may create a hazard.

Storm Water

• Provide gutters and downpipes where required.

• Connect downpipes to the existing stormwater system where suitable and approved.

• Where connection to the existing system is not practicable, provide an appropriate alternative discharge arrangement.

• Ensure all stormwater works comply with relevant requirements and do not adversely affect the existing property.

Existing Concrete Slabs

• Inspect the existing concrete slabs prior to installation.

• Confirm the slab is suitable to support the proposed structure and associated loads.

• Avoid damage to the existing slab during drilling, anchoring and installation.

• Make good any minor damage caused by the Contractor during the works.

• Any structural deficiencies identified in the existing slab are to be reported to the Principal prior to proceeding.

Finishes and Protection

• Provide appropriate protective coatings to all exposed steel/aluminium components as required.

• Touch up any damaged coatings resulting from transportation or installation.

• Ensure all exposed edges, fixings and connections are finished safely.

• Match existing finishes where reasonably practicable and as agreed with the Principal.

Building Interfaces

• Ensure the new pergola roofing integrates appropriately with the existing building.

• Provide flashing and weatherproofing at all interfaces with the existing building.

• Maintain access to existing doors, windows, services and maintenance areas.

• Ensure the works do not interfere with existing building drainage, electrical services or other infrastructure.

Safety and Compliance

• Comply with all applicable WHS requirements and site safety procedures.

• Provide appropriate fall protection and safe access for working at heights.

• Maintain safe access to each Unit throughout the works.

• Protect existing buildings, landscaping, finishes and property during construction.

• Remove all construction waste and surplus materials from site.

Completion

• Inspect the completed pergola roofing works for structural stability, alignment, drainage and workmanship.

• Rectify any defects identified during inspection.

• Clean the work area and leave the site in a neat and safe condition.

• Provide relevant warranties, product information and certification upon completion.

• Provide as-built information where required.

Contractor’s Responsibility

The Contractor is responsible for confirming all dimensions, site conditions, quantities and interfaces prior to ordering materials or commencing fabrication. All dimensions shown or provided are indicative only and must be verified on site by the Contractor.

The Contractor is to allow for all incidental works necessary to provide a complete, functional and weatherproof pergola roofing installation for all six (6) Units.

Mandatory Site Visit

• A mandatory site inspection is required prior to submission of a quotation.

• The Contractor is to attend the site and inspect all Six (6) Units and the existing concrete slabs.

• The Contractor is responsible for verifying all existing site conditions, dimensions, levels, access requirements, services and interfaces relevant to the proposed works.

• All dimensions provided in the RFQ documentation are indicative only and must be verified on site by the Contractor.

• The Contractor is to satisfy themselves as to the full extent and nature of the works prior to submitting their response.

• No additional costs arising from a failure to attend the mandatory site inspection or verify site conditions will be considered, unless otherwise approved by the Principal.

• Respondents are to confirm attendance at the mandatory site inspection as part of their submission.

Estimated Start Contract Date 21/09/2026

End Contract Date 4/12/2026

The Central Highlands region is in Central Queensland, Australia. The region encompasses an area of around 60 000 square kilometres, making it just short of the size of Tasmania.

It is home to around 30 000 people who live in the thirteen unique communities of Arcadia Valley, Bauhinia, Blackwater, Bluff, Capella, Comet, Dingo, Duaringa, Emerald, Rolleston, Sapphire Gemfields, Springsure and Tieri.

Our region is rich in minerals and agriculture, thriving on irrigation sourced from water storage on the Nogoa and Comet rivers. We claim the largest sapphire-producing fields in the Southern Hemisphere.

Major freight routes through the region include the north-south link between Charters Towers and northern New South Wales—identified as the inland transport alternative between Cairns and Melbourne.

changes.to:
Installation of Pergola Roofing over Existing Cement Slabs for 6 Units.

There will be a Mandatory Site Inspection:

Date: Wednesday, 9 September 2026

Time: 10.00am

Place: Meet at 13 Malvern Street, Capella Qld

**Please register your attendance by 7 September 5pm**

The Contractor is to provide all labour, materials, plant, equipment, supervision and associated works necessary for the supply and installation of pergola roofing over the

existing concrete slabs at six (6) units.

The works are to be completed in accordance with the relevant Australian Standards, manufacturer’s requirements and applicable Building Regulations.

Site Verification

• Verify the existing slab dimensions, levels, condition and suitability for the proposed pergola structure.

• Confirm all dimensions, locations and site conditions prior to fabrication and installation.

• Dimensions shown in the documentation are indicative only. The Contractor is responsible for confirming all actual dimensions on site.

• Identify and confirm the location of any existing services that may affect the works.

• Undertake a Site Inspection of all six (6) units prior to commencing works.

Pergola Structure

• Supply and install the complete pergola framing structure, including posts, beams, rafters, brackets, fixings and associated components.

• Provide suitable structural connections between the pergola structure and the existing slab/building, as required by the design.

• Ensure all structural members are appropriately sized and designed for the site conditions and applicable wind loads.

• Provide corrosion-resistant fixings and connections suitable for the location.

• Ensure the structure is adequately braced and securely fixed.

• Provide appropriate clearances from existing buildings, doors, windows and other structures.

Roof

• Supply and install roofing over the pergola structure.

• Roofing material is to be suitable for the location and comply with the approved design.

• Provide all required flashings, trims, closures, gutters and associated roofing accessories.

• Ensure roofing is securely fixed and weatherproof.

• Provide appropriate roof falls to ensure effective stormwater drainage.

• Ensure roof drainage does not discharge onto adjoining properties, access paths or areas where it may create a hazard.

Storm Water

• Provide gutters and downpipes where required.

• Connect downpipes to the existing stormwater system where suitable and approved.

• Where connection to the existing system is not practicable, provide an appropriate alternative discharge arrangement.

• Ensure all stormwater works comply with relevant requirements and do not adversely affect the existing property.

Existing Concrete Slabs

• Inspect the existing concrete slabs prior to installation.

• Confirm the slab is suitable to support the proposed structure and associated loads.

• Avoid damage to the existing slab during drilling, anchoring and installation.

• Make good any minor damage caused by the Contractor during the works.

• Any structural deficiencies identified in the existing slab are to be reported to the Principal prior to proceeding.

Finishes and Protection

• Provide appropriate protective coatings to all exposed steel/aluminium components as required.

• Touch up any damaged coatings resulting from transportation or installation.

• Ensure all exposed edges, fixings and connections are finished safely.

• Match existing finishes where reasonably practicable and as agreed with the Principal.

Building Interfaces

• Ensure the new pergola roofing integrates appropriately with the existing building.

• Provide flashing and weatherproofing at all interfaces with the existing building.

• Maintain access to existing doors, windows, services and maintenance areas.

• Ensure the works do not interfere with existing building drainage, electrical services or other infrastructure.

Safety and Compliance

• Comply with all applicable WHS requirements and site safety procedures.

• Provide appropriate fall protection and safe access for working at heights.

• Maintain safe access to each Unit throughout the works.

• Protect existing buildings, landscaping, finishes and property during construction.

• Remove all construction waste and surplus materials from site.

Completion

• Inspect the completed pergola roofing works for structural stability, alignment, drainage and workmanship.

• Rectify any defects identified during inspection.

• Clean the work area and leave the site in a neat and safe condition.

• Provide relevant warranties, product information and certification upon completion.

• Provide as-built information where required.

Contractor’s Responsibility

The Contractor is responsible for confirming all dimensions, site conditions, quantities and interfaces prior to ordering materials or commencing fabrication. All dimensions shown or provided are indicative only and must be verified on site by the Contractor.

The Contractor is to allow for all incidental works necessary to provide a complete, functional and weatherproof pergola roofing installation for all six (6) Units.

Mandatory Site Visit

• A mandatory site inspection is required prior to submission of a quotation.

• The Contractor is to attend the site and inspect all Six (6) Units and the existing concrete slabs.

• The Contractor is responsible for verifying all existing site conditions, dimensions, levels, access requirements, services and interfaces relevant to the proposed works.

• All dimensions provided in the RFQ documentation are indicative only and must be verified on site by the Contractor.

• The Contractor is to satisfy themselves as to the full extent and nature of the works prior to submitting their response.

• No additional costs arising from a failure to attend the mandatory site inspection or verify site conditions will be considered, unless otherwise approved by the Principal.

• Respondents are to confirm attendance at the mandatory site inspection as part of their submission.

Estimated Start Contract Date 21/09/2026

End Contract Date 4/12/2026

publicQuestions.question:
Good morning,

We are considering applying for inclusion on this Register, however the listed insurance requirements are vastly in excess of the norm for our profession and the scope of work that we undertake.

We are a drafting consultancy and our only deliverables are drawings for steel fabrication, provided on paper or electronically. Consequently our Public Liability risk amounts to little more than an occasional paper cut. Therefore the $20m PL requirement is vastly in excess of the norm for our profession and the cost of increasing ours to that amount would be too onerous to entertain given that there is no assurance of any particular volume of work.

Similarly, although our successfully completed projects have included several major and renowned high-rise buildings, an offshore naval facility, ferry terminals, port and harbour restructuring, shopping centres and similar, our worst-case Professional Indemnity liability is unlikely to ever rise above perhaps $100k, due to the nature of independent checks during the process. All of our output is Checked and Reviewed prior to the fabrication of the steel, by the Architect and Engineer responsible for the project, so any major discrepancies would be corrected at that stage.

A drafting consultancy that engages in projects of the size and scope that we do, would not normally carry PL insurance of more than $5m and PI insurance of $1m, if at all. More than that is excessive for the extent of risk that might ever be encountered, and is also too costly to be viable.

Therefore the question is - can Council vary the insurance requirement on a case-by-case basis, or should we not unnecessary spend our, and Council's, time making and processing this Application?

If the insurance is not variable it would be very unfortunate because over the last 25 years we have built a reputation for providing meticulous product at a price that is more than competitive in our industry

Thank you and kind regards.
publicQuestions.answer:
Good Morning,

Thank you for your enquiry and for providing further information regarding your business.

Council advises that the requirement for Public Liability and Professional Indemnity Insurance is not able to be varied on a case-by-case basis and is outlined at sections 2.3 and 6.3 of Part 2. Scope.

Section 6.3 states:

“The supplier must effect and maintain the following insurances in accordance with the requirements listed for each category at section 2.3:

1.	Public liability insurance in the amount of at least $20,000,000 in respect of any one occurrence and for an unlimited number of claims;

2.	Professional indemnity insurance in the amount of at least $5,000,000 in respect of any one occurrence and for an unlimited number of claims;”

Please refer to section 2.3 to confirm the minimum requirement for insurances at each category.

We appreciate your comments and interest in our procurement and look forward to reviewing your submission should you choose to submit.

Kind regards,

Procurement Team

publicQuestions.question:
--- Q1 - Liability Limit stated in Supplier Engagement Orders ---

Clause 22.1(a) of the Standard Terms and Conditions - Goods and Services limits the aggregate liability of each party to that party's Liability Limit, and clause 1.1(ee)(ii) defines the Supplier's Liability Limit as the amount stated in the SEO. Could Council please confirm what amount, if any, it intends to state as the Liability Limit in Supplier Engagement Orders issued under this register, and whether a standard figure will apply across the register or whether it will be set for each engagement?

--- Q2 - Documents against which departures are recorded ---

Part 3, Schedule F1 asks respondents to provide details of any proposed amendments, qualifications or departures "to the Contract contained in Part 4 - Contract or the scope contained in Part 5 - Scope of the Request for Tender". In this Request for Tender, Part 2 is the Scope and Part 4 is the Schedule of Rates. Could Council please confirm that departures should be recorded against the Standard Terms and Conditions - Goods and Services (Issue LGT2.4, October 2025) and Part 2. Scope?

--- Q3 - GST treatment of the Schedule of Rates ---

Section 5.3 of Part 2 - Scope requires hourly rates to be charged inclusive of GST, and the Part 4 column headings read "GST Inc". Clause 5.3 of the Procurement Process Conditions requires the Price to be submitted exclusive of GST, and clause 16.10 of the Standard Terms and Conditions provides that the amount payable for a supply is to be increased by the amount of any GST imposed. Council has previously confirmed that rates are to be submitted GST inclusive. Could Council please also confirm that no further GST will be added to those rates on invoice under clause 16.10?
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your enquiry.

--- Q1 - Liability Limit stated in Supplier Engagement Orders ---

This Arrangement does not, in itself, constitute a contract for the provision of Goods and/or Services, and therefore a liability limit is not predetermined for future procurements.

Clause 1.1(ee) Liability Limit and Clause 1.1(xx) SEO (from ‘Supplier Engagement Order’) provide the mechanism for the applicable liability limit to be established for each future procurement, with the Supplier’s liability determined in accordance with Clause 1.1(ee) and the relevant SEO.

--- Q2 - Documents against which departures are recorded ---

The references to Part 4 – Contract and Part 5 – Scope are to the respective Parts identified in the Request for Tender documentation. Respondents are to record any proposed amendments, qualifications or departures against the relevant Contract and Scope documents identified in the Request for Tender.

--- Q3 - GST treatment of the Schedule of Rates ---

Council advises that, for the purposes of completing the Schedule of Rates, all rates are to be submitted inclusive of GST, as indicated in Part 4 – Schedule of Rates, where the relevant rate columns are identified as “Rate (Inc GST)”.

Accordingly, Respondents should ensure that their tendered rates are inclusive of GST. For clarity, the Schedule of Rates is to be relied upon in determining the required GST treatment of the tendered rates, and the rates submitted are not to have GST added again on invoicing.

Kind regards,

Procurement Team

title: Supply and Delivery of One Articulated Motor Grader
description:
Central Goldfields Shire Council invites tenders for the supply and delivery of one (1) new articulated diesel-powered Motor Grader for use in municipal road construction, renewal and maintenance throughout the Central Goldfields Shire municipality.

The Grader will primarily operate on unsealed rural roads and, to a lesser extent, urban streets. title: Operation and Management of Bay Pavilions Aquatic Centre, Moruya War Memorial Swimming Pool and Nar
description:
Eurobodalla Shire Council (‘Council’) is issuing this open Request for Tender (RFT) for the provision of the

following scope of work:

1. The management and operation of Bay Pavilions aquatic and fitness (gym) facilities.

2. The provision of food and beverage services for the Bay Pavilions, including the café, poolside canteen

and meeting room catering.

3. The management and operation of Moruya War Memorial Swimming Pool, Narooma Swimming Pool

and facilitation of access to other on-site facilities (meeting room and kiosk).

Council has identified three separable packages, as identified above, with Tenderers able to submit a Tender to

provide singular package(s) and/or bundle of packages. Further details on the bundles of packages are included

within the scope.

What’s important to us?

Council is looking for a suitably experienced contractor(s) to undertake the management and operation of its

aquatic facilities and associated services. The key objectives for Council are to ensure that it is achieving best

value for money from its aquatic facilities contract(s) and to ensure that more specialist and/or locally based

providers are able to submit viable tender offers. It is also a key requirement for the procurement process that

the Bay Pavilions Aquatic Centre attracts a provider that will ensure the facility retains its premier, five-star

status. Council has therefore elected to offer separable packages so that tenderers may submit for one or more

individual packages or bundles, aiming to balance simplicity and operational efficiency. The details on the

separable packages are included within the Scope.

Why should you bid?

This is an opportunity to partner with Eurobodalla Shire Council on a long-term contract (four years, with two

three-year extension options) to manage and operate a partial or full portfolio of high-profile aquatic facilities,

including the Bay Pavilions Aquatic Centre, Moruya War Memorial Swimming Pool and Narooma Swimming

Pool. The separable packaging approach enables Tenderers to bid for a single package or propose an efficient

bundled offer, creating a genuine pathway for specialist and locally based operators as well as larger providers.

The successful provider(s) will have the ability to drive service quality, customer experience and participation

outcomes for residents and visitors, with scope to propose innovations and improvements to enhance the

facility offering and grow revenue within a supportive Council partnership.

Dear Procurement officer,

We have the following questions. If you could please provide clarification on the queries below, it would be greatly appreciated, as this information will assist us in preparing and submitting our tender response.

1. RFID driver sign-on and start inhibit on the existing system

Section 1.2 lists RFID driver sign-on with asset start inhibit as a minimum requirement. Is that capability currently wired and enabled across the existing fitted assets, or is it a capability of the installed system that has not been commissioned? If it is not currently enabled, should a proposal to support the existing system include pricing to retrofit it?

2. Existing employee card technology

Council has advised that the existing RFID readers encode Wiegand 26 with parity 4, and that the same employee cards are used for building access. Wiegand 26 describes the reader to panel wire format rather than the card technology, so it does not identify the card itself. Could Council confirm the operating frequency and card technology of the existing employee cards, for example 125 kHz proximity such as HID Prox or EM4102, or 13.56 MHz such as MIFARE Classic or DESFire. The answer determines the method for adding an individually identifiable credential to the existing cards without disturbing building access.

3. The twelve month history requirement

Section 1.2 requires that the system can historically track assets up to 12 months. Does Council intend this as a forward-looking data retention capability from the commencement of the contract, or does it require migration of the existing 12 months of historical telematics data into the new system? If migration is required, will Council provide an export of the existing data or arrange for the incumbent to do so?

4. Removal of the existing hardware

Where a proposal involves migration to a new system, does Council require the existing telematics hardware to be removed and returned to Council, and where should the cost of that removal be shown in Schedule B2, which does not include a removal line item?
publicQuestions.answer:
Good afternoon and thank you for your questions

1. RFID driver sign-on and start inhibit on the existing system

Section 1.2 lists RFID driver sign-on with asset start inhibit as a minimum requirement. Is that capability currently wired and enabled across the existing fitted assets, or is it a capability of the installed system that has not been commissioned? If it is not currently enabled, should a proposal to support the existing system include pricing to retrofit it? This system is fitted and operation on all existing units

2. Existing employee card technology

Council has advised that the existing RFID readers encode Wiegand 26 with parity 4, and that the same employee cards are used for building access. Wiegand 26 describes the reader to panel wire format rather than the card technology, so it does not identify the card itself. Could Council confirm the operating frequency and card technology of the existing employee cards, for example 125 kHz proximity such as HID Prox or EM4102, or 13.56 MHz such as MIFARE Classic or DESFire. The answer determines the method for adding an individually identifiable credential to the existing cards without disturbing building access. Our existing cards are HID Prox. Our existing Mix Telematics system and all other systems that utilise our employee RFID cards can use all 3 of these credential types

3. The twelve month history requirement

Section 1.2 requires that the system can historically track assets up to 12 months. Does Council intend this as a forward-looking data retention capability from the commencement of the contract, or does it require migration of the existing 12 months of historical telematics data into the new system? If migration is required, will Council provide an export of the existing data or arrange for the incumbent to do so? New suppliers are not required to provision for the existing historical 12 months of data. New suppliers are required to maintain a minimum rolling 12 months historical tracking data from implementation date moving forward.

4. Removal of the existing hardware

Where a proposal involves migration to a new system, does Council require the existing telematics hardware to be removed and returned to Council, and where should the cost of that removal be shown in Schedule B2, which does not include a removal line item? For a migration proposal, the implantation plan should include removal of the existing system. The proposal should include a labour time per unit removal. This would then be applied using the rate “Labour - Repair and Rectification work” on schedule B2

description:
Livingstone Shire Council (Council) invites suitably qualified and experienced contractors to submit a Tender for the Construction of Rosslyn Street Sewage Pump Station (SPS42) Wet Well Renewal, Rosslyn QLD 4703.

The Works comprise the construction and commissioning of a new sewage pump station facility to replace the existing SPS42 infrastructure. The project is intended to improve the operational reliability, emergency storage capacity, maintainability, monitoring capability and long-term performance of this critical asset within Council's wastewater network.

The successful Tenderer will be responsible for providing all labour, materials, plant, equipment, supervision, temporary works and associated activities necessary to complete the Works, including maintaining continuity of sewer services throughout construction, testing, commissioning and handover, in accordance with the Contract, Technical Specification and Tender Documents.

The Contract will be administered under contract – AS2124 - Construct Only and may be delivered in staged components, as detailed in the Tender Documents.

publicQuestions.question:
Good afternoon

Item 1, Control and SCADA Scope

Reference: Technical Specification (Part 2, Appendix A) Sections 15.1.1 and 15.1.2; Site Meeting Minutes dated 20/08/2026, "SCADA and PLC".

The tender documents appear to conflict on responsibility for the control and SCADA scope:

•	The Technical Specification (Sections 15.1.1 and 15.1.2) requires the Contractor to perform all SCADA configuration, RTU and control programming, program the PLC and RTU, integrate the station into Council's SCADA system, produce a Functional Specification, and fully commission the telemetry system.

•	The Site Meeting Minutes (20/08/2026) state the Contractor supplies the unprogrammed MIRI and PLC, Council returns them programmed, and the Contractor will not program or integrate the switchboard.

Please confirm who is responsible for the control and SCADA scope, specifically the PLC and MIRI programming, SCADA integration, and the Functional Specification deliverable (Section 15.1.2).

If any of these remain the Contractor's responsibility, please advise Council's preferred SCADA integrator.

Item 2, Groundwater Level for Dewatering

Reference: Geotechnical Report (Part 2, Appendix E, GE_2510.1180) Sections 5 and 6.2.3; PPR Section 2.6; Site Meeting Minutes dated 20/08/2026, "Geotechnical Conditions and Dewatering".

The tender documents give conflicting groundwater levels:

•	The Geotechnical Report states groundwater was encountered at 8.0m in BH1, records this as the groundwater table in Table 5.1, and adopts 8.0m as the basis for its trench stability assessment in Section 6.2.3.

•	The Site Meeting Minutes (20/08/2026) state groundwater may be encountered approximately 1 to 2 metres below ground level.

The 1 to 2 metre figure does not appear in the Geotechnical Report or elsewhere in the tender documents. Given the deep excavations in the scope, this difference has a significant impact on dewatering design, methodology and price.

Please confirm the groundwater level tenderers are to adopt as the basis for pricing dewatering and excavation.

If the 1 to 2 metre level is to be adopted, please provide the supporting investigation data, confirm whether the Geotechnical Report's trench stability and excavation recommendations remain valid, and advise how dewatering is to be allowed for this condition.

Regards
publicQuestions.answer:
RFI Response – Control and SCADA Scope

The Contractor shall:

* Supply the unprogrammed MIRI and HMI to Council.

Council shall:

* Provide a programmed MIRI and HMI to the Contractor.

The Contractor shall:

* Install the programmed MIRI and HMI into the switchboard.

* Test and install the switchboard into position on site and connect all site equipment as per the design.

* Not be required to produce a Functional Specification

This above scope will alleviate the contractor from having to perform SCADA integration because the equipment will come pre-programmed.

RFI Response – Groundwater Level for Dewatering

The geotechnical investigation recorded free groundwater in BH1 at approximately 8.0 m below ground level at the time of investigation.

The reference in the Site Meeting Minutes to groundwater potentially being encountered at approximately 1-2 m below ground level, as the Liquid Limit of soil is around 44%-50%, indicates the moist soil may encounter water at shallow depth. The groundwater conditions may fluctuate due to seasonal and rainfall influences and may differ from those observed during the geotechnical investigation.

Tenderers shall make their own assessment of the information provided and allow for all dewatering, groundwater management, excavation support and temporary works necessary to undertake the Works. In accordance with the PPR, all associated costs and risks are the responsibility of the Contractor and shall be deemed included in the Contract Sum. No additional groundwater investigation data is available

title: RFT 2669 - Design and Construction – North Bronte Beach Rockfall Remediation
description:

The final Phase of Stage 1 focuses on undertaking the design, documentation, planning and costing frameworks to inform future procurement and project delivery related to public domain works.

publicQuestions.answer:
Good morning,

Which access route(s) will be available for construction traffic? - Only one route is available into the valley, via the Donkey Steps access road. The damaged section of Wolgan Road into the Wolgan Valley is closed to all vehicles.

What GVM, axle load, vehicle/trailer dimensions, operating hours and movement restrictions apply? - The current day-to-day limit for vehicles into the Wolgan Valley is 6t GVM, with a maximum length of 8m. Can tenderers assume project-specific exemptions will be approved for quarry trucks, concrete agitators, low loaders, drilling/piling plant and large armour rock deliveries? - Yes, as per above.

Are pilot/escort, convoy or wet-weather restrictions applicable? - Council may consider temporary closure of the road to residents whilst heavy plant is traversing the Donkey Steps. Wet weather restrictions are generally not applicable. However, Council may, at its discretion, close the access road in extreme weather events.

Must tenderers allow for material transfer/staging and/or access-road maintenance, upgrading or reinstatement? - There is no mandated requirement for material staging. title: Penrith City Library Smart Device Application
description:
The contractor is required to deliver a comprehensive mobile library application (iOS and Android) with the following key capabilities:

• Core Features:

User account access, catalogue search across physical and digital collections, real-time item availability and location and item renewals synced with the Library Management System (LMS).

• Integration:

Seamless integration with LMS and RFID systems, with LMS-agnostic functionality. The app must connect to a wide range of existing digital platforms (e.g., Libby, BorrowBox, Freegal, Beamafilm, StoryBox, Humanitix) and support future integrations.

• Digital Access:

Ability to download and access eBooks and eAudiobooks directly within the app.

• User Experience:

Intuitive, user-friendly design that meets accessibility standards (e.g., WCAG), and allows in-library borrowing via mobile devices.

• Administration:

A staff-facing CMS for content management, plus flexible branding and content customisation.

• Events & Information:

Event booking/ticketing functionality and integration with Council website content.

• Reporting & Support:

Analytics and reporting tools, along with 24/7 technical support.

Overall, the solution should provide a fully integrated, accessible and user-centred mobile library experience with strong backend management and support.

publicQuestions.question:
Commencement versus go-live

Does the service commencement date of 21 December 2026 represent the required production go-live date for the replacement application, or the commencement of an implementation and transition period? If an implementation period is anticipated, what is Council's target production go-live date?

Catalogue data access

What interfaces does Council's Spydus environment make available to authorised third-party applications for catalogue search and data extraction, including any API, LCF service, MARC export, OAI-PMH or Z39.50/SRU endpoint and do these cover digital collections as well as physical holdings?

Digital content delivery model

For third-party digital content platforms subject to provider DRM restrictions, does Council require digital content to be rendered natively within the application, or is authenticated access with handoff to the provider's platform acceptable?

RFID and self-check integration

Can Council provide details of the FE Technologies RFID and security environment at its branches, including gate models, the RFID tag standard and data encoding in use (for example ISO 15693 / ISO 28560)?
publicQuestions.answer:
Commencement versus go-live

Yes, the service commencement date of 21 December 2026 represents the required production go-live date for the replacement application.

Catalogue data access

We have paid for access to the Spydus API and third-party APIs are also permitted. Spydus still has SIP2 connection available, though it is not a preferred option. Spydus has the ability to export MARC records, we have OAI-PMH set up to harvest records into TROVE and I think Sharon’s team use Z39.50 to import MARC records for cataloguing purposes. We certainly use eContent harvesting to import catalogue records from Libby, BorrowBox and Indyreads. Spydus pricing has increased, so it is possible that we won’t be extending our eContent harvesting to cover any of our other providers.

Digital content delivery model

Our eContent providers handle the DRM requirements. We authenticate patron logins via Spydus API or a SIP2 process and loans are then accessed via the provider’s platform.

RFID and self-check integration

We have Designer Clear 2 Column security gates at all branches. Penrith and St Marys have Return Shelves and all branches have V5 Loan Stations. We are currently running with SIP2 integration but are in the process of converting to LCF via API. title: Request for Quote – Tim Fischer Bridge & Heavy Vehicle Monitoring
description:
The Department of Transport and Main Roads (TMR) invites suitably qualified suppliers to submit a quotation for CN-27671 – STR26749 Tim Fischer Bridge & Heavy Vehicle Monitoring.

Location: Wide Bay Burnett Region, Queensland

Key Details

RFQ Closing Date: 5:00 pm, Wednesday, 9 September 2026

Submission Requirements

Suppliers are required to complete Section 2 – Supplier Response of the CN-27671 – STR26749 Request for Quote document and submit a quotation addressing the evaluation criteria outlined in the RFQ and engagement brief. Responses must demonstrate the supplier’s capability to deliver the services in accordance with the specifications and scope of work provided.

Scope of Services

Engineering and Technology Branch is seeking to engage a specialist contractor (the Offeror) with demonstrated expertise in structural monitoring and data collection services to support the Tim Fischer Bridge & Heavy Vehicle Monitoring Project within the Wide Bay Burnett Region.

The services will involve the collection, retrieval and reporting of bridge monitoring data to support project objectives. Further details of the requirements are provided in the Request for Quote and Engagement Brief.

publicQuestions.question:
Of the 1600 heavy vehicles per day, is there an estimate for the number of threshold 1 and 2 exceedances? This is for data storage and 4G transmission requirements.

Can TMR confirm the expected award date for the contract? Given the 3-week notice periods for site access and end of October delivery date, sensor selection will need to consider lead times.

Confirm if a certain level of accuracy is required for the temperature sensors.

Can nominal distances and expected (or max/min) measurement ranges for the displacement sensors be provided, and their required accuracy.

For the optional number plate detection, is a camera with combined ANPR and suitable optics acceptable? Or is the footage to capture number plates for human review?
publicQuestions.answer:
Q. Of the 1600 heavy vehicles per day, is there an estimate for the number of threshold 1 and 2 exceedances? This is for data storage and 4G transmission requirements.

A. The number of Threshold 1 and Threshold 2 exceedances will depend on the final trigger levels adopted. As a guide, TMR aims to capture waveform data for responses exceeding those typically generated by a heavy vehicle of approximately 20 tonnes. For video capture, a lower trigger frequency may be appropriate. Suppliers may assume that approximately the largest 1% of responses would be captured, equating to around 16 events per day based on the expected traffic volume of 1600 heavy vehicles per day.

Q. Can TMR confirm the expected award date for the contract? Given the 3-week notice periods for site access and end of October delivery date, sensor selection will need to consider lead times.

A. The anticipated contract award date is approximately two weeks after the RFQ closing date, subject to evaluation outcomes and internal approvals.

Q Confirm if a certain level of accuracy is required for the temperature sensors.

A. A temperature sensor resolution of 0.01°C is required. No specific accuracy requirement has been mandated; however, suppliers should provide details of proposed temperature sensors including the accuracy

Q. Can nominal distances and expected (or max/min) measurement ranges for the displacement sensors be provided, and their required accuracy.

A. Pier 5 has a 375mm slotted hole in the expansion joint restraint angle. A longitudinal displacement sensor measurement range of approximately 400 mm, and transverse and vertical displacement sensor measurement ranges of approximately 50 mm are recommended. Suppliers may propose alternative ranges with justification.

Q. For the optional number plate detection, is a camera with combined ANPR and suitable optics acceptable? Or is the footage to capture number plates for human review?

A. Both approaches are acceptable. A camera with integrated ANPR capability is preferred where available; however, the system does not mandate ANPR functionality. The camera should provide image/video footage of sufficient quality to allow manual number plate identification and verification when required.

publicQuestions.question: Would the Principal consider an extension to the RFQ closing date from 9 September 2026 to 18 September 2026?
publicQuestions.answer: Due to the desired project delivery schedule we are unable to extend the RFQ closing date.

publicQuestions.question:
1 - Can you please provide drawings of the bridge? Specifically looking for drawing around the piers, expansion joints, and bearings where sensors are located to determine suitable mounting brackets and associated ancillaries.

2 - Can you please provide close up photos of the bearings, piers, and expansion joints around where sensors are to be located?

3 - Page 8 of the brief lists the specifications for the tilt sensors as 0.001m/m resolution required, while page 10 lists 0.0001m/m resolution required. The latter seems unnecessarily high. Can you please confirm required tilt sensor accuracy?

4 - Time Synchronisation requirements - Do you require all instruments to be time synchronized together (to within the 100Hz tolerance), and trigger together? For example, a vehicle that exceeds the threshold for a sensor at span 1 and begins data capture, will also cause simultaneous capture of data from sensors at span 5 at the same instant.

Or is it acceptable for a span 5 sensor to only capture data if its local threshold is exceeded, irrespective of whether readings are occurring on other spans?

5 - The brief mentions a buried battery (Wom-Bat) with solar panels on the pole near Abut A. Is a buried battery and solar panel off the bridge required, or are we free to propose an alternative with solar panels mounted to the bridge pier headstock?

6 - Site working hours are listed as 7pm to 5am (night works). Will TMR/RoadTek be providing temporary site lighting and site facilities (i.e. laydown area, toilet) during this period, or are we to include these in our scope?
publicQuestions.answer: Refer to attachments uploaded 04/09/2026.

publicQuestions.question:
Q1. Engagement Brief, The uni-axial tilt sensor resolution is stated as 0.001 m/m in the Figure 5 legend and as 0.0001 m/m in the Instrumentation details table.

Q2. Strain sensor resolution is specified as 0.1 microstrain. The Scope table refers throughout to strains "relative to unloaded background strains", which indicates a dynamic (event-relative) measurement. Please confirm that 0.1 microstrain is a dynamic resolution requirement rather than an absolute accuracy requirement sustained over the monitoring period.

Q3. No measurement ranges are specified for the displacement sensors. Please confirm the expected movement ranges, or confirm that the Offeror may nominate them, for (a) girder to restraint angle vertical, longitudinal and transverse movements, and (b) longitudinal movement across the Pier 5 expansion joint under the full seasonal thermal range.

Q4. The location of the four provisional piezo sensors is stated as Span 5 in the Scope and in the Instrumentation details table, and as Span 4 in the Fee structure table. Please confirm the correct span.

Q5. The Figure 4 legend reads "Camera 25fps + Scene camera + Illumination", which may indicate two separate camera units, whereas the Instrumentation details table states a quantity of one. Please confirm the required number of camera units.

Q6. The provisional piezo sensors require a saw-cut slot in the deck running surface. Please confirm that TMR accepts this intervention to the wearing surface, confirm the reinstatement standard required, and confirm that TMR will provide and pay for the lane closure and traffic management required for deck-level works. The Excluded section addresses traffic control associated with access by UBIU or EWP, which is a different operation.

Q7. The deck top temperature sensors are to be located 30 mm below the top surface of the deck. Please confirm that coring of the running surface and any waterproofing membrane is permitted, confirm the reinstatement detail required, and confirm that TMR will provide the lane closure and traffic management for this work, which cannot be undertaken from beneath the bridge.

Q8. Please clarify the extent of Provisional item 7. In particular whether it comprises transfer of title in the installed hardware, confirm what is intended by "monitoring logic" whether a perpetual licence to the configured logger programs and processing logic, delivery of source, or both — and whether any continuing access to the data platform is required.

Q9. The reference system describes a buried battery adjacent to the pole. Please confirm which party is responsible for excavation approvals, service location (Before You Dig Australia), and any environmental or cultural heritage clearances required for excavation within the road reserve.

Q10. Please confirm that TMR will provide the calibration vehicle, its driver, traffic management and a certified weighbridge docket for the vehicle mass, and confirm the expected duration of the calibration exercise so that a consistent allowance can be made across offers.

Q11. The reference system specifies three days of battery autonomy without charge. In this locality the summer wet season can produce longer periods of heavy overcast. Would TMR wish a five-day or seven-day autonomy options to be priced separately?
publicQuestions.answer: Refer to attachments uploaded 04/09/2026.

title: Bamaga Football Oval Lighting
description:
The Northern Peninsular Area Council is looking to upgrade the lighting at the Bamaga Football Oval to Queensland Rugby League Seniors standards (200 Lux).

There are existing lighting poles at the ground, but it would be preferable to replace these with poles that can be lowered for maintenance. NPARC will consider multiple options from suppliers to achieve the 200 Lux standard for the lowest lifecycle cost.

Automatic and remote control of the lights is desirable.

The lights must be installed prior to the start of the 2027 football season - say 1 June 2027. Remembering that the wet season makes travel and construction works difficult from December to April each year.

This is a design and construct project. NPARC would be willing to evaluate a number of proposals from each supplier.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
The Northern Peninsular area is a proud Rugby League Area and competition in the area is strong for men's, women's and children's competitions.

The Bamaga Oval has undergone a number of upgrades over the past year, and the new lights will make this a first-class facility.

I have been getting multiple enquiries about downloading the documents for this tender. There are no documents to download.

I could not find any historical information on the current lighting system at the oval.

This should not be relevant to this proposal as we are looking for a completely new system, not using any of the current lighting system, other than the electrical conduits and pits may be of use for the new system. Again, I have no drawings to show where those pits and conduits are.

The existing lights will be moved by NPARC to the Injinoo Oval (if feasible).

Photos of existing lights and p[oles have been added, along with photos of the control panel. Top fuses run the lights control panel. Bottom fuses are for each light pole.

publicQuestions.question:
We are currently reviewing the requirements with the intention of submitting a response and would appreciate it if Council could provide, or direct us to, a current list of the plant, trucks and equipment typically required under this register.

Where available, could you please include the preferred makes, models, sizes/capacities and specifications for the equipment Council may require. This will assist us in identifying suitable equipment within our existing fleet and through our supply network that meets Council's operational requirements.

KFI Group has access to a broad range of heavy plant, trucks and support equipment, and we are keen to understand Council's requirements so we can put forward the most suitable equipment and competitive rates as part of our submission.
publicQuestions.answer:

Council operates a decentralised procurement model, with individual departments and officers responsible for procuring plant, trucks and equipment based on their operational requirements. As such, Council is unable to provide a definitive list of preferred makes, models, sizes, capacities or specifications.

Suppliers are encouraged to nominate any plant, trucks and equipment they consider suitable for inclusion on the Register, provided the equipment meets the requirements and categories outlined in Part 2. Scope.

You may include equipment from your existing fleet and/or equipment available through your supply network. Council will consider the equipment and rates submitted in accordance with the requirements of the Register.

Kind regards,

Procurement Team

publicQuestions.question:
RFI – COW000100 – GST Treatment of Tendered Rates

Ref: Scope cl 5.3; Procurement Process Conditions cl 5.3; Part 4 – Schedule of Rates

The RFT documents conflict on GST treatment: Scope cl 5.3 says rates are to be inclusive of GST; Procurement Process Conditions cl 5.3 says the Price must be exclusive of GST; and the Schedule of Rates columns are headed "Rate (Inc GST)."

Please confirm whether rates should be submitted GST-inclusive or GST-exclusive, and whether an addendum will issue.
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your enquiry.

Council advises that, for the purposes of completing the Schedule of Rates, all rates are to be submitted inclusive of GST, as indicated in Part 4 – Schedule of Rates, where the relevant rate columns are identified as “Rate (Inc GST)”.

Accordingly, Respondents should ensure that their tendered rates are inclusive of GST. For clarity, the Schedule of Rates is to be relied upon in determining the required GST treatment of the tendered rates.

Kind regards

Procurement Team

title: Cooktown Multi-Purpose Health Service (MPHS) Redevelopment – Enabling Works - Civil Contractor
description:
The State of Queensland through Queensland Health (the Principal), invites you to submit a Tender for the provision of a suitably qualified civil contractor to construct the Enabling Works for the Cooktown MPHS Redevelopment in accordance with the Invitation documents.

The Queensland Government is investing $200 million to redevelop the Cooktown Multipurpose Health Service (CMPHS), improving access to care for Cooktown and surrounding communities.

Health Infrastructure Queensland in partnership with Torres and Cape Hospital and Health Service are responsible for delivery of the project as part of the Hospital Rescue Plan. The project will deliver a range of essential healthcare facilities and services to meet the needs of the community and reduce the need for patients to travel outside the region.

The scope of this request is for an enabling works package the Project team have identified to mitigate risks to the main construction which is planned in 2027.

title: RFT2526-30 - Childcare Centre Expansion
description:
The Town of Port Hedland invites submissions from qualified Contractors for the construction of the Childcare Centre Expansion.

The project involves the construction of extensions and upgrading of the existing facility to increase the childcare capacity, improve functionality.

Port Hedland Rd
Port Hedland, Western Australia 6721
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription: Port Hedland is transforming into a vibrant attractive regional city with a community that are proud to live, work and play in the heart of the Pilbara.
vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Wednesday 16 September 2026 10:00 PM (W. Australia Standard Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background:
The Town of Port Hedland is seeking to engage a suitably qualified contractor for the construction of the Childcare Centre Expansion. The project involves the extension and upgrade of the existing facility to increase childcare capacity, improve functionality, and ensure compliance with current regulatory and operational requirements.

Due to the ongoing operation of the childcare centre, the works are required to be delivered in a staged manner. The project will be undertaken in stages to enable the continued operation of the facility as a childcare centre, with the Contractor responsible for appropriately sequencing works, managing site separation, and maintaining safe access for staff, children, and visitors at all times.

The works are to be completed by December 2027, with the contractor required to plan and resource the delivery accordingly to meet this timeframe.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi

Can you provide further information for the following?

1. Is design and RPEQ certification required for separable portions 1 and 3 or only required for SP 2 as per the tender price schedule?

2. Can you please provide the long section drawing for the HDD crossing at Lagoon creek to understand the depths and levels?

3. For Separable portion 2 can you please provide a drawing clarifying the length of pipe installed by the council and length of pipe to be installed by the contractor?

4. Can you please provide the cross section of the trench for the watermain indicating the type of bedding and backfill/trenchfill material required?

5. Can you please provide a cross section of the road pavement to understand the pavement restoration works required post construction of the watermain?

6. Are property service connections required? If yes, please provide details of the number of connections, type of pipe material. Please further confirm if the new connections are required from main to meter or just connect the existing property service to the new watermain?

publicQuestions.answer:
(edited on 31/Aug/2026 11:29 AM)

PLease find the answers to your questions.

1. Design and RPEQ certification – Separable Portions 1, 2 and 3

or the HDD works and Northridge Road works, where the Contractor is required to develop the final alignment, bore profile, methodology or other design elements, those elements are to be designed and certified by an appropriately qualified RPEQ.

For conventional pipeline construction, the Contractor may adopt applicable MICC, WSAA and recognised standard drawings/details for trenching, bedding, embedment, backfill, thrust restraint and associated pipeline construction without preparing a separate project-specific RPEQ design, unless site conditions require departure from those standards.

RPEQ-certified As-Constructed documentation will be required for all Separable Portions, confirming that the completed works have been constructed in accordance with the approved design, applicable standards and any approved design changes.

Where the Contractor proposes an alternative methodology or departure from the nominated standards or drawings, the Contractor shall provide RPEQ design and certification for that alternative prior to construction.

2. Lagoon Creek HDD long section

A detailed long section has not presently been issued.

The HDD Contractor is required to develop and confirm the proposed bore alignment, entry/exit locations and bore profile as part of its methodology. The current scope nominates an approximate minimum cover of 1.5 m beneath the Lagoon Creek bed, subject to the Contractor's proposed bore profile and Council approval.

Council will review whether any additional survey/design information is available and issue this to all tenderers if applicable.

3. SP2 – Council-installed versus Contractor-installed pipework

Council will provide an annotated plan identifying:

existing/Council-installed water main;

limits of Contractor-installed pipework;

This will be issued to all tenderers as an addendum/clarification.

4. Water main trench section – bedding and backfill

Unless specifically detailed otherwise within the Contract documents, conventional water main construction shall be undertaken in accordance with the applicable SEQ Water Supply Code and associated standard drawings, including requirements for trenching, bedding, embedment, backfill, compaction, fittings, thrust restraint and other typical water main construction details.

Where site conditions or the proposed construction methodology require a departure from the applicable SEQ standard details, the Contractor shall develop the alternative detail and provide RPEQ-certified design documentation for MICC review prior to construction.

5. Road pavement restoration

As per item 4 response.

6. Property service connections

No property service connections are included within the Contractor’s scope of works.

The Contractor is required to install the new water main infrastructure only, in accordance with the issued scope, drawings and applicable standards.

All property service connections, including connections from the new water main to existing property services/meters, will be undertaken separately by Mount Isa City Council at a later stage.

Tenderers are therefore not to include any allowance for property service connections within their tendered price.

7. Road crossing carrier/enveloper pipe

The size, material and configuration of any required enveloper/casing pipe are to be determined through the Contractor’s RPEQ-certified design for the Duchess Road crossing.

Tenderers shall consider the requirements applicable to the crossing of the TMR-controlled road corridor, including applicable TMR standards, clearances, loading requirements and approval conditions.

The Contractor’s design shall nominate the proposed carrier pipe, enveloper/casing (where required), bore diameter, depth/cover, entry and exit locations and associated construction methodology.

The final design is to be RPEQ certified and submitted to MICC for review prior to construction. Any required TMR approval shall be obtained prior to commencement of the affected works.

title: Provision of a Signage Design Manual
description:
The City of Clarence is seeking an experienced environmental graphic designer or signage design specialist to develop a practical and contemporary Signage Design Manual that provides a consistent, accessible and durable approach to signage across Council-managed places and facilities. The Manual should provide clear design and technical guidance so Council can design, procure, install, maintain and progressively replace standard signage across Clarence.

It is desirable that the consultant has demonstrated experience in city-wide or local government signage systems, including design strategy, documentation and implementation guidance.

The purpose of this project is to develop and implement a comprehensive Signage Design Manual for the City of Clarence. The manual will ensure that future public signage across the city is consistent, clear, and effective, aligning with urban design best practice, accessibility standards, and the visual identity of City of Clarence.

This manual will serve as a key reference for the design, placement and maintenance of signage across all Council-managed assets and public spaces, supporting a cohesive and welcoming city experience for residents and visitors alike.

The public spaces, facilities, and assets within City of Clarence are currently signed using a wide range of designs, materials, and messaging approaches. This has resulted in an inconsistent visual identity and, at times, confusion for the community. The absence of clear, consolidated design standards impacts communication, accessibility and a consistent maintenance approach.

To address these challenges and plan proactively for a growing and evolving community, we want to develop a new Signage Design Manual that:

•	Establishes a clear and consistent visual style for all signage

I have a few questions relating to the electrical scope for the Mackay Turf Club tender.

What size are the proposed portable heated spas? What electrical specs are available to allow for correct sizing of cabling and outlets for connection.

On the proposed Jockey facilities electrical plans there are 2 x meter panels shown on the western wall. Is this correct or will one be sufficient?

Are the existing meter panels being reused? If not are there any specs on what meter board/s is required to be installed? What size board/s?

Do the exhaust fans require ducting/venting? Are there specific exhaust fans that need to be used?

What size, brand are the ceiling fans?

What wattage flood light is required?

Are the 2 x 20A 3 phase outlets on the eastern wall remaining in place and do they need to be replaced during the upgrades? If so is a specific brand required?

Is the solar system getting upgraded during works and will a solar contractor need to be included as part of the electrical scope?

Is the comms cabinet located on the eastern wall of the jockey facilities? Does the data cabling in the jockey facility go back to that point?

Are there any specifications for sizing of sub main cabling for the proposed Horse Drug Testing Building?

Will the sub main cabling for the Horse Drug Testing Facility nee to be installed underground or overhead?
publicQuestions.answer:
Please see below answers (A) to your questions (Q):

Q1: What size are the proposed portable heated spas? What electrical specs are available to allow for correct sizing of cabling and outlets for connection.

A1: As per designs supplied min 2m x 1.5m capable of heating to 40 degrees. Cabling to be sized according to selected unit.

Q2: On the proposed Jockey facilities electrical plans there are 2 x meter panels shown on the western wall. Is this correct or will one be sufficient?

A2: As per supplied design, meter panels to be relocated from existing position to proposed positions. Vendors may choose after suitable consultation with electrical specialist to replace western wall with a singular meter board.

Q3: Are the existing meter panels being reused? If not are there any specs on what meter board/s is required to be installed? What size board/s?

A3: As above and supplied design.

Q4: Do the exhaust fans require ducting/venting? Are there specific exhaust fans that need to be used?

A4: Standard exhaust fans vented to roof cavity.

Q5: What size, brand are the ceiling fans?

A5: Standard builders range fans 122cm.

Q6: What wattage flood light is required?

A6: Min 100w (LED version).

Q7: Are the 2 x 20A 3 phase outlets on the eastern wall remaining in place and do they need to be replaced during the upgrades? If so, is a specific brand required?

A7: To remain unless unserviceable upon inspection by electrician at which point replacement only. This is power supply for SKY TV Trucks.

Q8: Is the solar system getting upgraded during works and will a solar contractor need to be included as part of the electrical scope?

A8: As per supplied design and Scope, existing solar to be removed and reinstalled in position as required for new roof. Nil upgrades unless required under electrical code.

Q9: Is the comms cabinet located on the eastern wall of the jockey facilities? Does the data cabling in the jockey facility go back to that point?

A9: Correct

Q10: Are there any specifications for sizing of sub main cabling for the proposed Horse Drug Testing Building?

A10: To be sized according to proposed load.

Q11: Will the sub main cabling for the Horse Drug Testing Facility need to be installed underground or overhead?

A11: Preferably underground.

description:
Gwydir Shire Council invites tenders from suitably qualified and experienced individuals, businesses, or organisations for the management and operation of the Bingara Riverside Caravan Park and/or the Warialda Caravan Park for the next 3 years.

Applicants may submit a tender for either facility individually or for both facilities.

Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
The Gwydir Shire is in the centre of the ‘Fossickers Way’, a route which offers the traveller a relaxing alternative to the New England or Newell Highways. The Shire encompasses a diverse landscape that is both picturesque and productive and is approximately 560 km north of Sydney, 160 km north of Tamworth along the Fossickers Way and 85 km north-west of Inverell. The shire is 9,122 square kilometres in size and is situated north of Tamworth Regional Council and continues almost to the Queensland border.

The southern boundary of the shire is the Nandewar Range where the Gwydir and Namoi Valleys meet. The Horton Valley and Cobbadah District are home to some Australia’s most highly regarded beef cattle studs. These enterprising farmers use the latest artificial breeding and agronomic technology to produce beef of exceptional quality. Meat Sheep and merinos that grow high quality wool are also grazed in this area.

The Gwydir River enters the Gwydir Shire where it spills from the Copeton Dam and meanders in a westerly direction through the towns of Bingara and Gravesend. The Gwydir valley is well know for irrigated and dry land cropping as well as livestock production. In addition to the traditional crops of wheat, barley, oats and sorghum, there are olive groves, pecan nut plantations and freshwater fish farms in the Gravesend district.

Heading northwest from the timbered surrounds of the town of Warialda and the close-knit community of Coolatai, the countryside opens into an undulating vista of basalt farmland. This part of the Shire which include the villages of Crooble, Croppa Creek and North Star, is known as the ‘Golden Triangle’. Farmers using advanced farming techniques, such as minimum tillage and satellite guidance systems, produce a variety of high yielding crops such as wheat, barley sorghum, maize, chick peas, canola and cotton to name just a few. This area also has several cattle feed lots which supply grain fed beef to the Australian domestic market and export markets throughout the world.

Both Warialda and Bingara have Hospitals, Aged Care Hostels, Medical Centres, Caravan Parks, Swimming Pools, Pre-schools, Libraries, Tourist Information Centres, and a Mobile Pre-school based at North Star. Warialda is the centre for the Council’s Technical Services functions. Bingara is the centre for the Administrative functions. The two centres are being linked through the use of sophisticated communications equipment to ensure that the amalgamations primary objective is achieved which is to save the existing employment numbers within each of the main urban centres of Warialda and Bingara.
Where is the Gwydir Shire?

Thank you for your questions regarding Request for Tender GWY_2027_T03 – Management of Bingara Riverside Caravan Park and Warialda Caravan Park.

Council provides the following clarification.

1. Warialda Manager Accommodation

As there is no caretaker residence at Warialda Caravan Park, Council will provide the successful contractor with one dedicated powered caravan site at no charge for the duration of the management agreement.

The site will include access to electricity, water and sewerage services where available to the site.

A suitable annex or temporary outdoor living area may be established, subject to compliance with normal park requirements and prior approval from Council.

Council is currently reviewing the availability of suitable storage space at the Warialda Caravan Park and will confirm any arrangements with the successful contractor.

Internet access required for the operation of the park office and Council systems will be provided by Council.

## 2. Grounds-Maintenance Equipment

Council-owned grounds-maintenance equipment currently located at each caravan park will remain available for use by the successful contractor in undertaking the required grounds-maintenance duties.

Currently there is no dedicated equipment available for the park however this will be discussed and plant equipment provided with the successful contractor.

The contractor will have access to fuel but will be responsible for ordinary consumables associated with day-to-day use of the equipment.

Council will remain responsible for routine servicing, major mechanical repairs and replacement of Council-owned equipment that becomes unserviceable through normal wear and tear.

The contractor will be responsible for damage caused through misuse, negligence or use outside the intended purpose of the equipment.

## 3. Definition of Minor Maintenance

For the purposes of the management agreement, minor maintenance generally refers to routine, low-cost maintenance and minor repairs that can reasonably be undertaken as part of normal day-to-day park operations.

Council proposes that minor maintenance will include repairs or materials up to a maximum value of $250 per individual repair or maintenance item, with an annual expenditure limit of $2,500 per park, unless otherwise approved by Council.

The contractor will be responsible for the labour and ordinary materials associated with minor maintenance within these limits.

Electrical, plumbing and other work requiring a licensed trade will generally be arranged and paid for by Council. Major repairs, replacement of significant assets and capital works will remain Council's responsibility.

Any maintenance issue exceeding the above limits should be reported to Council for assessment and approval prior to work being undertaken, except where immediate action is required to make an area safe.

## 4. Cleaning, Linen and Guest Consumables

The contractor will be responsible for the routine cleaning of cabins, amenities and other park facilities, including the purchase of cleaning chemicals and normal cleaning consumables.

The contractor will also be responsible for routine guest and facility consumables including:

* toilet paper;

* paper towel;

* hand soap;

* rubbish bags;

* guest toiletries and similar low-value cabin supplies; and

* routine laundering of cabin linen and towels.

Council will retain ownership of cabin linen, towels and bedding and will be responsible for replacement where items have reached the end of their useful life through normal wear and tear.

## 5. Waste Collection and Pest Control

Council will arrange and pay for the existing general waste and recycling collection services associated with each caravan park, including normal disposal and tipping charges.

Council will also meet the cost of existing sanitary-bin services.

The contractor will be responsible for routine cleanliness and basic pest-prevention measures associated with normal park operations.

Council will arrange and pay for specialist pest-control treatment where required for Council-owned cabins, amenities or other buildings, including significant infestations or treatment requiring a licensed contractor.

## 6. Collection of Park Income

All accommodation income and park takings will be retained by Council.

Council will provide the EFTPOS and payment-processing facilities required to operate the parks and will be responsible for associated merchant fees and online payment gateway charges.

Council will also be responsible for legitimate refunds and chargebacks processed in accordance with Council procedures.

The contractor will be responsible for the appropriate handling, reconciliation and banking of cash and other takings in accordance with Council procedures.

Where the contractor has complied with Council procedures and has not acted negligently, losses arising from fraudulent transactions or chargebacks will remain Council's responsibility.

## 7. Office and Information Technology Equipment

Council will provide the core equipment reasonably required to operate Council's booking, payment and administrative systems at each park.

This will include, where required:

* computers and monitors;

* printers/scanners;

* EFTPOS and point-of-sale equipment;

* internet access for the park office;

* access to GuestPoint; and

* technical support for Council-provided systems and equipment.

Council will also provide routine printer ink, paper and similar consumables required for Council administrative functions.

The contractor will be responsible for any additional equipment or systems they elect to use for their own business purposes.

## 8. Crown-Land Licence

Both caravan parks are located on Council-managed Crown land.

Council does not currently propose to charge the successful contractor a separate Crown-land licence fee, security deposit or bond associated with the licence required to operate the facility.

The contractor will, however, be required to comply with all conditions of the applicable Crown-land licence and maintain the insurance requirements specified in the RFT.

Any compliance costs arising directly from the contractor's activities or failure to comply with licence conditions will remain the contractor's responsibility.

## 9. Management-Fee Payments and Annual Adjustment

The agreed management fee will be paid monthly in arrears, subject to receipt of a valid tax invoice and satisfactory performance of the required services.

Respondents may propose a fixed annual management fee for the three-year term or nominate an alternative annual adjustment mechanism as part of their tender.

Council does not mandate a particular indexation method. Where indexation is proposed, respondents should clearly identify the method and index to be used. Council would consider a recognised measure such as the Consumer Price Index as an acceptable approach.

Any proposed annual adjustment will form part of the tender evaluation and, if accepted, will be incorporated into the final agreement.

## 10. Historical Operating Information

Council is unable to provide historical operating information as we have had no booking software implemented until recently.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
The Sunshine Coast Stadium (SCS) is a major regional sporting and events facility that supports community participation, high-performance sport and the delivery of large-scale events.

The SCS has been identified as a host venue for 2032 Brisbane Olympic and Paralympic Games, necessitating upgrades to meet Games requirements and support increased future demand.

The Sunshine Coast’s home of big events will be bigger and better with an upgrade to SCS, securing its position as the region’s premier venue for local, national and international sporting, leisure and entertainment events.

The stadium upgrade will boost permanent seating with a new eastern grandstand and a rebuilt western grandstand. Upgrades will include multi-purpose community spaces and amenities accessible to people of all abilities.

The early design vision by awarded Principal Consultant, Architectus, is inspired by the Sunshine Coast’s natural landscape and coastal lifestyle. Initial concepts explore light, open forms, shaded concourses and elevated seating to create a relaxed, immersive game-day experience.

The sports fields at SCS support a range of activities, from grassroots community sport to elite training camps and national-level football, rugby league, and rugby union games.

The planned upgrades will deliver modern, high-quality facilities for athletes, officials, and fans, ensuring the venue continues to serve the region for decades to come.

The SCS will be owned and operated by Sunshine Coast Council (SCC), delivering a lasting legacy for the region through enhanced tourism, economic development, and increased opportunities for community engagement and active recreation.
