title: RFT000040 Description: Electronic Document and Records Management System (EDRMS)
description: The Principal is seeking to procure an Electronic Document and Records Management System (EDRMS) solution and associated implementation services. The scope includes solution design, configuration, implementation, training, support, and migration of records and metadata from legacy systems, including TechnologyOne ECM and Objective. The procurement is vendor agnostic and is intended to identify the solution and delivery partner best able to support compliant, secure and sustainable records management across the Port’s Microsoft 365 and SharePoint environment.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerAddress:
1 Benwell Rd
South Townsville, Queensland 4810
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription: The Port of Townsville is Northern Australia’s largest container and automotive port, and the country's leading exporter of copper, zinc, lead, sugar, fertiliser and molasses. Located in the heart of Northern Australia's largest city, the Port handles more than 30 diverse commodities and is a strategic defence and cruise port.
vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Thursday 17 September 2026 10:00 AM (E. Australia Standard Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background: The Port’s current records management environment includes records held across TechnologyOne ECM, Objective, SharePoint, shared drives, OneDrive, Outlook and other business systems. The current environment presents risks relating to over-retention, inconsistent metadata, unclear information architecture, legacy access models, limited lifecycle management, and reduced ability to meet legislative and compliance obligations. The intended decommissioning of legacy platforms requires a structured approach to select and implement an EDRMS with capability to migrate records and metadata in a controlled manner. The successful Supplier will assist the Principal to establish the required records architecture, minimum metadata requirements, security model, migration approach, implementation plan and operating model for the new solution.

publicQuestions.question:
Software/Technology escrow

Greetings,

We are a software escrow services provider.

Software escrow helps manage the risk around implemented solutions (including in-development, bespoke applications and technologies, databases and interfaces) and the Supplier of those services. Whether the delivered solution is a standalone app or a SaaS deployment, the Licensee/User wants to know it has access to the application source code, and the relevant interfaces going forward. Software escrow helps to mitigate those risks.

As the documentation is silent on whether there will be a requirement for, or consideration of software escrow services, could you, if appropriate, let me know the following, …

1.
Has software escrow been considered as a risk mitigation strategy for this solution?

2.
If it has, has it been discarded?

3.
If software escrow is required, how will you go about selecting your software escrow agent, given the cost of software escrow services is typically modest?

Kind regards, Software Escrow Guardians
publicQuestions.answer: Thanks for your enquiry, we aren’t considering any escrow services as part of this tender.”

publicQuestions.question:
Good afternoon

We have reviewed the requirements and would like to know if you are interested in receiving guidance or advice from a vendor-independent Information Management Consulting practice. We specialise in providing record-keeping, information privacy, and information Security advice, and this often involves developing information architectures, security access models, and conducting in-depth assessments of systems and vendors.

We have delivered pre- and Post M365 Assessments including M365 Governance, selection of Third Party v Native controls, to ensure the M365 environment is aligned to legislative requirements.

In our experience, many MS Providers have the technical ability to deliver what you need. However, they often lack appropriate Information management knowledge, especially in a regulated environment.

We acknowledge your location, but for guidance, we would refer you to the NSW State Records and the Public Records Office of Victoria Guidelines on M365. These documents are similar because they are authored by the same person, but they can be helpful.

As we are a vendor-independent company, we would be pleased to have a discussion if this is felt helpful.

Regards

Mark
publicQuestions.answer: thanks for your query. We already have this capability in house and, as such, are only seeking services within the defined scope of the EDRMS procurement at this time.

"The following documents are incorporated by reference into this Scope:

Q5. If the preference is for Public Cloud, are you looking for a full Platform as a Service (PaaS) offering?

Q6. Are there workflows developed already for business activities and are you looking for automation capabilities in the new EDRMS solution?

To accurately estimate the effort, resources, and costs associated with the implementation of the proposed EDRMS solution, in particular the data migration element, we request clarification on the following technical matters. This information will help ensure our response is both comprehensive and reflective of the actual project scope.

publicQuestions.answer:
1. What versions of TechnologyOne ECM (T1) and Objective are currently implemented?

TechnologyOne ECM is currently operating on version 2022A. The Objective version is 8.1. Both systems are hosted on-premises, with application files and databases residing on Port-managed server infrastructure.

2. Is the Port operating standard vendor-supported deployments, or have there been any significant customisations or bespoke extensions?

Both systems are predominantly standard implementations. Some configuration changes and customisations have been applied over time to support business requirements; however, these are not considered extensive bespoke developments.

3. Are the systems currently under active vendor support and maintenance agreements?

TechnologyOne ECM is currently supported through a third-party support arrangement rather than directly by TechnologyOne. Objective is not currently covered by an active support or maintenance agreement.

4. Will the Port maintain vendor support agreements throughout the migration period and for an agreed post-migration warranty period?

TechnologyOne ECM support arrangements are expected to remain in place throughout the migration period. As Objective is not currently under support, no vendor support arrangement is planned for that platform during the migration.

5. Will the successful supplier be granted read access to the source repositories for migration and analysis purposes?

Yes. Subject to standard security, confidentiality and access approval processes.

6. Can the Port confirm whether T1 and Objective vendors have agreed to support extraction activities if required?

Neither vendor has been formally approached regarding extraction support at this stage. Given the age of the implementations, particularly Objective, vendor involvement may be limited. Tenderers should assume migration activities will need to be planned based on the information and access available to the Port at the time of implementation.

7. Have either vendor identified any restrictions relating to access, extraction, APIs, licensing or database connectivity?

No restrictions have been identified by the Port to date.

8. Are APIs available for both T1 and Objective?

This has not yet been confirmed.

9. If APIs are available, can the Port provide API documentation?

API documentation is not currently available. Any documentation identified by the Port during ongoing discovery activities will be made available to the successful supplier where possible.

10. Are vendor-supplied export utilities available for either platform?

This has not yet been confirmed. Tenderers should assume export methods and tooling will require assessment during migration planning and implementation.

11. Can the Port provide an indication of the number of metadata indexes, custom fields or metadata profiles configured within T1?

see attachment

Refer to the metadata inventory spreadsheet provided with the clarification response. The inventory represents the Port's current understanding of the environment and will continue to be refined through ongoing discovery activities.

12. Can the Port provide an indication of the number of metadata indexes, classifications or schemas configured within Objective?

Refer to the metadata inventory spreadsheet provided with the clarification response. The inventory represents the Port's current understanding of the environment and will continue to be refined through ongoing discovery activities.

13. Are QAPs, retention schedules, disposal classes and business classification schemes currently managed within T1, Objective, both systems, or externally?

No

14. Is event history, audit history and record activity history expected to be migrated?

Yes.

15. Does the current T1 implementation manage physical records, files, cartons or hybrid records?

No

16. If yes, approximately how many physical record entities and associated metadata records exist?

N/A

17. Can you provide the number of records currently held within Objective?

Objective currently contains approximately 918,778 records.

18. Can you provide the number of document versions held within Objective?

No

19. Can you provide the average and maximum document sizes within each repository?

No

20. Estimated number of records containing unsupported, legacy or proprietary file formats.

This information is currently unknown.

The Port has not yet completed a comprehensive file format assessment. Tenderers should assume that unsupported, legacy and proprietary file formats may exist given the age and diversity of the source repositories. Assessment of file formats, migration compatibility and remediation requirements should be considered as part of the migration planning approach.

title: REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL 19.26 CAR HIRE CONCESSION SERVICES: ONSLOW AIRPORT
description:
The Shire of Ashburton invites proposals from suitably qualified and experienced vehicle rental operators for the provision of car hire services at Onslow Airport.

The successful respondent(s) will be granted the right to operate a vehicle rental business from designated facilities within Onslow Airport under a Licence Agreement with the Shire of Ashburton.

Due to the limited availability of airport facilities and operational areas, the Shire intends to appoint no more than two (2) vehicle rental operators under this Request for Proposal. The Shire reserves the right to appoint one or two operators based on the outcome of the evaluation process and the best interests of the Shire.

The Shire is seeking a suitably experienced operator to provide vehicle rental services from Onslow Airport.

The successful respondent will have access to:

•	Dedicated car hire service counters within the terminal

•	Allocated vehicle parking areas

•	Branding opportunities within approved concession areas

•	Access to approximately 70,000 annual passenger movements

Respondents are encouraged to propose innovative service delivery models that best meet the needs of airport users.

title: T2026-023 Woorabinda Womens Sporting Hub - Netball Courts, Buildings Services and Associated Works
description:
Woorabinda Aboriginal Shire Council invites suitably qualified and experienced contractors for the delivery of Stage 2 of the Women’s Sporting Hub.

Stage 1 is the supply & installation of the modular clubhouse. (Works not within this tender)

Stage 2 comprises the establishment of the new Home of Women’s Sport in Woorabinda, featuring the construction of 2x multi-purpose sporting concrete courts, covered grandstand seating, concrete paths, design and installation of electrical, water, sewer and drainage to the clubhouse, playground and associated works as per the technical specification. The stage 2 scope along with the clubhouse will ensure the precinct provides the women of Woorabinda with a welcoming, family-friendly, safe community space.

Stage 3 works will follow, a time-frame TBC, comprising of a hardcover roof over the two courts with competition standard lighting.

As the 2nd stage of the Women’s Sporting Hub program, this package provides the key community infrastructure – 2 x courts, grandstand covered seating, fenced playground, concrete paths, building services and associated works that will contribute to a cohesive, high-quality sporting precinct for the Woorabinda community.

Works are to be completed in accordance with approved design documentation, applicable guidelines, and best-practice construction methods. Tender closing at 5.00 pm, Wednesday 9th September 2026.

publicQuestions.question:
Good morning,

In Part D – Schedule of Prices under “Termite Treatment”, it asks for confirmation that employee(s) hold a QBCC Termite Management – Chemical and a QBCC Termite Management – Physical licence. However, the services listed only require a QBCC Termite Management – Chemical licence.

Could you please confirm whether both licences are required, or only Chemical licensing for this tender?
publicQuestions.answer:
(edited on 13/Aug/2026 10:58 AM)

Thank you for your enquiry.

Tenderers are required to hold both a QBCC Termite Management – Chemical licence and a QBCC Termite Management – Physical licence.

While the termite treatment services currently listed in the Schedule of Rates primarily require a Termite Management – Chemical licence, the contract may include other termite management works that require a Termite Management – Physical licence. As subcontracting is not permitted under this arrangement, suppliers must be appropriately licensed to undertake the full range of potential termite-related services that may arise during the contract term.

Accordingly, the requirement for both licence types remains unchanged, and tenderers should ensure they can demonstrate compliance with both licensing requirements in their submission.

Please also note.

The QBCC Termite Management - Physical licence (along with the QBCC Termite Management – Chemical Licence) is only required if offering for the termite treatments, which is optional under this trade. The mandatory requirement for this SOA is the Pest Management Licence issued by Qld Health, which is required to undertake the basic and additional treatments etc.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Procurement

Can you please confirm that if we have no subcontractors to propose for the services, we do not have to submit the Appendix C - Schedule of Subcontractors and that our submission will still be conforming ie not alternative?

Thanks
publicQuestions.answer: Yes Correct if you are not subcontracting you do not need to submit appendix C - Schedule of Subcontractors

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Procurement

Can you please confirm - if we are a pest control business, we are not allowed to provide subcontactors for termite works ONLY? but we are able to nominate for other pest services ie snakes, native species removal, etc?

Thank you
publicQuestions.answer:
Good morning,

Yes, that is correct. Termite works must be performed by the contracted business and cannot be subcontracted.

For any items outside the termite scope, subcontractors can be nominated in Appendix C and engaged subject to QBuild approval.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Procurement

Can you confirm that the Annexure D Purchase Contract Conditions is for jobbing/ reactive services only? and that the contract for ongoing maintenance services will be created separately once the contractor is engaged under the SOA?
publicQuestions.answer:
Good morning,

This SOA covers reactive maintenance, planned maintenance, and housing vacant maintenance. A separate contract is required for ongoing regular servicing of certain sites, which is managed through our Service Maintenance team.

RFI-01: Please confirm which edition of the AFL Preferred Community Facility Guidelines the AP-001 minimum sizes are drawn from (2019 or 2024). RFI-08: Please confirm the minimum boundary setback/run-off distance applicable between the proposed building and the playing field boundary.

RFI-09: Please confirm the orientation requirement for the kiosk (Western side) - whether this is fixed relative to true north or relative to the oval/spectator side of the building.

RFI-11: Please confirm whether operable/movable walls between change rooms, to allow flexible combined use, are a preference or a requirement.

RFI-14: As the project is funded via a Commonwealth grant, please confirm whether there is a total project budget or cost cap tenderers should be designing to.

RFI-15: Please confirm the expected patronage/crowd size the facility should be sized for, relevant to the external covered viewing area, kiosk and public toilet sizing.
publicQuestions.answer:
The following responses are provided to clarify recent questions

RFI-01: Please confirm which edition of the AFL Preferred Community Facility Guidelines the AP-001 minimum sizes are drawn from (2019 or 2024). The two editions differ in several respects relevant to this design, including an additional Umpire Briefing Room requirement and the optional status of several rooms at regional level in the 2024 edition.

RESPONSE

The minimum sizes are drawn from the 2024 guidelines. Some building items have been excluded based on discussions with stake holders. The umpire briefing room is not required.

RFI-02: Please confirm whether First Aid/Medical Room (15 sqm), Doctors Room (10 sqm) and Gym/Fitness Area (25 sqm) are to be treated as mandatory inclusions, given the current AFL guideline lists these as optional at Regional level.

RESPONSE

Yes, these are mandatory items in the design

RFI-03: Please confirm the public toilet provision (male, female and accessible sizing) tenderers should design to, as this is not included within AP-001.

RESPONSE

Public toilets are not required in the new building only player amenities listed in the scope

RFI-04: Fig.3/DR-001 shows an indicative footprint of approximately 32m x 12m. Please confirm whether this is a fixed maximum building envelope or an indicative guide only, and whether tenderers may propose a larger footprint where necessary to meet AP-001 minimums.

RESPONSE

The building should be designed to the existing footprint; however, ramps/stairs can be accommodated outside of the footprint on the southwest side of the building. The transition to the field can be outside of this footprint but must be smooth. The Principal may, at its sole discretion, consider alternative tenders, provided the alternative tender meets the scope, functional intent and design concept expressed in the tender document. If an alternative tender is proposed, submit a detailed description of the alternative stating clearly the manner in which it differs from the detailed requirements of the RFT documents and including separate tender schedules applicable to the alternative.

Alternative tenders will not be considered unless the Tenderer has submitted a conforming tender.

RFI-05: Please confirm whether the amenity building must be a single connected structure, or whether a linked or separate two-pavilion arrangement (e.g. a detached change room block) would be acceptable on the site.

RESPONSE

Both options would be acceptable

RFI-06: Please confirm whether a partial second storey/mezzanine, as referenced in Section 4.1 for the timekeeper/scoring box, is acceptable in principle, and advise any fire, access and structural requirements that would apply.

RESPONSE

Partial second storey /mezzanine would be acceptable. Design requirements would have to be compliant with the NCC , however accessible access would not be required on the second floor.

RFI-07: Please provide the site survey and geotechnical information referenced in the Contract Documents list, to allow tenderers to confirm building setout, levels and footing design.

RESPONSE

The Site survey was provided in the original suit of documents , Ref S003-S-1, Geo Tec report was added 9 July Ref S-005H

RFI-08: Please confirm the minimum boundary setback/run-off distance applicable between the proposed building and the playing field boundary.

RESPONSE

Minimum Boundary run off is 4M to the player dugout/fences /gates. The building would need to accommodate these distances

RFI-09: Please confirm the orientation requirement for the kiosk (Western side) - whether this is fixed relative to true north or relative to the oval/spectator side of the building.

RESPONSE

The Kiosk is to be facing the oval/field of play

RFI-10: Please confirm any specific corrosion/durability standards Council expects for coastal-environment cladding, fixings and external hardware, beyond general NCC compliance.

RESPONSE

Nothing beyond general NCC requirements

RFI-11: Please confirm whether operable/movable walls between change rooms, to allow flexible combined use, are a preference or a requirement.

RESPONSE

Operable / movable walls are not a requirement but will be considered

RFI-12: Please clarify the expected timeframe and process for AFL design approval referenced in Section 4.2.1, and confirm whether this occurs prior to or following contract award.

RESPONSE

Concept design to be submitted with tender. Throughout the design process Council will be liaising with the AFL to ensure the building design meets the AFL minimal requirements

RFI-13: Please advise whether existing utility service records (Telstra, Essential Energy) for the site are available

RESPONSE

Not available

RFI-14: As the project is funded via a Commonwealth grant, please confirm whether there is a total project budget or cost cap tenderers should be designing to.

RESPONSE

Council will not be providing the project budget

RFI-15: Please confirm the expected patronage/crowd size the facility should be sized for, relevant to the external covered viewing area, kiosk and public toilet sizing.

RESPONSE

No public toilets required. Kiosk serving size to be a minimum of 30mtr Sq. No specific requirements for external covered viewing area

1.NCC lift requirement

Under NCC 2022, a two-storey Class 9b building is required to provide a means of access to the upper floor that complies with the accessibility provisions in NCC Section F. This typically requires a passenger lift or equivalent compliant access solution. This requirement was not contemplated in the original RFT scope and would represent a significant addition to the project cost and building footprint.

Please confirm whether council has considered this NCC requirement and whether a compliant accessible path of travel to the second floor is expected to be provided within the Contractor's scope. If so, please confirm whether a passenger lift is required or whether an alternative compliant access solution would be acceptable.

RESPONSE

Council has considered the accessibility requirements required for the second floor of the proposed building and is of the view that accessible access to the second floor is not required. This position is based on the anticipated limited patronage and use of the upper level and previous advice.

2. Floor-to-floor headroom

Based on the site levels available in S-005 and the current ground floor datum, a second floor FFL at 5RL to 5.5RL results in a floor-to-floor height that may not achieve a workable internal headroom at ground floor level. Please confirm the basis for the specified RL range, specifically whether it refers to the finished floor level of the second storey or another datum, and whether there is any flexibility in this specification to achieve a compliant and functional ground floor ceiling height.

RESPONSE

The specified RL range is based on the adjacent double storey building, with the intention that the proposed second storey floor level the new building aligns generally with the height and appearance of the existing building .There is an opportunity to excavate the current ground level to reach the acquired levels

3. Building footprint

The inclusion of a lift or equivalent accessible access solution, together with stair access, may require additional floor area within the 12m x 32m building footprint that was not allowed for in the original scope. Please confirm whether the footprint constraint remains fixed at 12m x 32m with these additional elements included, or whether any allowance for access infrastructure outside the primary footprint will be considered.

RESPONSE

The allowance for access infrastructure outside the primary footprint will be considered

RFI-

Please confirm whether a Development Application is genuinely not required given the development without consent classification stated in the RFT, or whether any conditions or notifications apply as a separate planning process (REF?)

RESPONSE

Council Can confirm no development application is required for this project

title: 2026.069 - Development of a Laratinga Trails and Boardwalks Masterplan
description:
Laratinga Wetland is a highly popular and well used community and environmental asset with over 8,000 people accessing the wetland via its trails each week. To ensure access to the wetland is safe, equitable and maximises community and environmental outcomes, a review of the trails and boardwalk infrastructure is proposed. To help with this task, the Mount Barker District Council (“Council”) is seeking to engage a suitably qualified consultant to review existing Laratinga wetland trails and boardwalk layout and infrastructure, associated access issues and opportunities and to develop a master plan to inform future development upgrades and renewals.

The existing Laratinga trail network and boardwalks was constructed when the wetlands were first developed in the late 1990’s. The boardwalks are now at end of life, with one section having been closed to public access for over 2 years. The boardwalks consist of 1 main section that crosses basin 3 and includes a viewing platform and 2 smaller sections in basins 1 and 2 (see Attachment 1 - Laratinga Wetlands Trails map).

Council has conducted a condition audit and commissioned a quote to replace the existing structures as they were originally designed but upgraded to comply with current standards. The quote to do this came in at close to $2M which prompted the need for a cost benefit analysis to ensure community funds are invested appropriately and community benefit is maximised.

In addition, the water regime in the wetland is changing to an ephemeral system, as part of a major upgrade to the Mount Barker Wastewater Treatment Plant. As well as broader management implications, this change will require lagoons to be dewatered for a period which would enable work on boardwalks and other infrastructure to occur, and before the ephemeral system is implemented. This is currently scheduled for 2028.

Therefore, before proceeding, it has been determined that a review of the layout and design of the whole Laratinga trail network and user needs should occur to ensure whatever is implemented is fit for purpose and identifies appropriate community use, access and safety as well as achieving environmental objectives, including the needs of birdlife and other fauna.

Any queries are to be submitted via VendorPanel and a response will be provided in the same manner.

Council's primary consideration will be artistic quality, audience experience, feasibility, and alignment with the event theme, rather than whether a proposed work is a premiere presentation.

title: 2026.039 - Treasury Consultant
description:
Mount Barker District Council (“Council”) is seeking to engage a suitably qualified and experienced treasury advisory consultant to provide both:

•	Strategic treasury advisory services, and

•	Ongoing monthly treasury and debt management advice in relation to Council’s treasury function.

This engagement will support Council (as the parent entity) while recognising that treasury positions are managed across:

•	The municipal operations of Council; and

•	The Council’s Wastewater Subsidiary (GMB Water), in accordance with Council’s Treasury Management Policy (Attachment 1).

Council is one of the fastest growing municipalities in South Australia and is experiencing significant infrastructure demand driven by population growth.

Council is forecasting a peak debt position of approximately $255 million by 2028/29, largely associated with the development of a wastewater network that is being delivered ahead of development demand.

Council currently operates under an approved borrowing facility from the Local Government Finance Authority (LGFA) of up to $255 million and manages its treasury activities in accordance with its Treasury Management Policy.

Council manages its treasury activities holistically, while also recognising that the treasury positions of the Municipal operations and the Wastewater Subsidiary are managed as distinct but interrelated portfolios in accordance with its Treasury Management Policy.

Given the scale, complexity, and forward profile of borrowings, Council is seeking external expert advice to:

•	Optimise its treasury management approach

•	Manage financial risks (particularly interest rate risk)

•	Ensure alignment with long-term financial sustainability objectives

•	Test current reliance on LGFA funding and explore alternative market options

•	Strengthen both strategic treasury planning and ongoing treasury decision-making

Engagement will be for a three (3) year term with the Strategy Development to be completed within six (6) weeks of Contract commencement.

All queries are to be submitted via VendorPanel and a response will be provided in the same manner.

Given that LAQ’s operations remain active at the subject property the successful agent will require thoughtful consideration for inspections to ensure limited interruption for business continuity during this period. The property must remain operational until the fit-out of LAQ’s new premises is completed and staff and operations are successfully relocated.

The Workplace Strategy Project (WPS) Team will be supported by ACCORP, acting as a property consultant, to assist in the sales process. We are also seeking for the Sales Agents to identify opportunities to mitigate risks, optimise the sales process, and expedite timelines where feasible, without compromising the outcome or compliance of the sales campaign.

title: Construction of Extensions and Studios - Capital Housing Program 2
description:
The Scope is described in the document(s) attached to or provided with this Request for Tender and identified as:

Scope of Works (Construct Only)

The Contractor shall undertake building approvals and complete the construction of Eight (8) new residential dwellings at the following locations as follows;

Current Addresses	Lot Number	Proposed Housing Type

- 5 Major Close	Lot 350 SP270846	2 Bedroom Studio

- 48 Workshop	Lot 48 SP265165	2 Bedroom Studio

- 37 Back Beach Road	Lot 356 SP270846	2 Bedroom Studio

- 39B Back Beach Road	Lot 357 SP265165	2 Bedroom Studio

- 16 Gribble Street	Lot 12 SP265165	2 Bedroom Extension

- 6 Major Close	Lot 346 SP270846	2 Bedroom Extension

- 98 Workshop Road	Lot 197 SP265165	2 Bedroom Extension

- 41 Back Beach Road	Lot 343 SP265165	2 Bedroom Extension

The Works include, but are not limited to, all labour, materials, plant, equipment, design, approvals and activities necessary to deliver a fully operational, compliant and complete housing development fit for purpose and ready for handover and occupation.

Reference Documents

2 Bedroom Studio Designs

o Lot 350 (5) Major Cl – Preliminary Issue C

o Lot 48 (48) Workshop Rd – Preliminary Issue C

o Lot 356 (37) Back Beach Rd – Preliminary Issue C

o Lot 357 (39B) Back Beach Rd – Preliminary Issue D

2 Bedroom Extension Designs

o Lot 12 (16) Gribble St – Preliminary Issue E

o Lot 346 (6) Major Cl – Preliminary Issue E

o Lot 197 (98) Workshop Rd – Preliminary Issue A

o Lot 343 (41) Back Beach Rd – Preliminary Issue C

.

Key Requirements

• The Contractor shall ensure the Works comply with all applicable legislation, codes, standards and authority requirements.

• The Works shall be delivered as a complete and functional development, notwithstanding any omissions or discrepancies in the reference documentation.

• A mandatory Indigenous Employment and Business Participation (IEBP) Plan shall be submitted with the Tender. Failure to submit an IEBP may result in the Tender being deemed non-conforming.

Building Approval

• Contractor must obtain relevant building approvals for each property for this work.

Site Establishment & Civil Works

• Site establishment, access, temporary services and controls

• Clearing, grubbing, demolition if required and site preparation.

• Bulk earthworks, cut and fill, trimming and compaction incl. testing if applicable

• Set out of all works in accordance with approved design and issued FFLs

• Stormwater drainage, overland flow management and lawful discharge

Residential Construction

• Construction of eight dwellings in accordance with the designs provided

• All works to be in accordance with Remote Housing Standards (RHS) or as otherwise nominated

• Complete construction of each dwelling including all structural, architectural and building elements necessary to achieve a fully functional and compliant dwelling

• Supply and installation of all fixtures, fittings and appliances

• Kitchens, bathrooms and laundries including joinery

Services & Utilities

• All hydraulic services including water, sewer and drainage

• Electrical reticulation, metering, switchboards and internal installations

• Communications and data provisions as typically required

• Coordination and connection to mains

External & Ancillary Works

• Driveways, pathways, hardstand areas and access ways

• Fencing, gates and boundary treatments

• Landscaping, reinstatement and making good of all disturbed areas

• Installation of external fixtures including T-Bar clotheslines, external sink and bins

Testing, Commissioning & Handover

• Testing and commissioning of all services and systems

• Rectification of defects and completion of outstanding works

• Provision of as-constructed documentation, manuals and warranties

• Final certification and approvals for occupancy

• Handover of a complete, operational and compliant development

Contractor Obligations

• The Contractor shall verify all site conditions, dimensions, levels and service locations prior to commencing Works.

• The Contractor shall be deemed to have allowed for all conditions that may reasonably be anticipated from available information and site inspection.

• No claim will be accepted for matters arising from failure to adequately investigate site conditions or coordinate the Works.

• The Contractor is responsible for all coordination, interfaces and integration of the Works, whether expressly stated or reasonably inferred.

Project Specification

• Design and Construction Standards for Remote Housing – August 2025

• National Construction Code (NCC)

Additional Council Specifications

Minimum specs in addition to the Remote Housing requirements; - 6mm FC sheets be nominated for soffit and patio ceiling

• Hinged doors for bedroom cupboards and linen cupboards be nominated in lieu of sliding doors

• Ensure correct rates tiles for kitchen floor area, laundry floor area, toilet floor area and bathrooms

• Exhaust fans to bathrooms, toilets and 1 in kitchen NOT directly over the stove. Exhaust fans to be 250-300mm low maintenance type. Ducted to external soffits per RHG

• Fixed ridge vents to roof where possible

• Door hold back stops to be fixed to top of all doors - Adoored 75mm white cushion clip door stop or similar

• 32mm s/s grab rails to be used as towel rails fit as many towel rails to bathrooms as reasonably possible.

• Rheem Solar HL 300ltr 3.6kw for Solar Hot Water System.

The Contractor shall comply with the current edition of the National Construction Code (NCC), all applicable Australian Standards (AS/NZS), and all relevant statutory and regulatory requirements.

It shall be the Contractor’s responsibility to identify and comply with all standards applicable to the Works, whether they are specifically listed in this document.

publicQuestions.question:

The houses are designed for Gold Standard minimum and will be built accordingly.

Axon cladding is to be allowed for external wall linings.

title: Design, Build and Implementation of the AFFIRMS Reporting System
description: AFAC is seeking a suitably qualified supplier to support the design and implementation of the Australasian Fire Fatality and Injury Reporting and Monitoring System (AFFIRMS). AFFIRMS is a national evidence and research utilisation initiative aimed at improving the consistency, quality and accessibility of fire fatality and injury data across Australia and New Zealand. The successful supplier will work with AFAC member agencies to review existing data sources and methodologies, develop a sustainable reporting framework, support data governance arrangements, and establish processes that enable meaningful analysis and reporting. While technology may form part of the solution, this is primarily a research, data and evidence-based project rather than a standalone software development procurement. Services may be delivered remotely, with project commencement anticipated in late 2026.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
AFAC is leading the development of the Australasian Fire Fatality and Injury Reporting and Monitoring System (AFFIRMS), a collaborative initiative involving fire and emergency service agencies across Australia and New Zealand.

A feasibility study has already been completed, identifying the need for a consistent, sustainable approach to collecting, analysing and reporting fire fatality and injury data. The project is intended to improve the evidence base available to support prevention, policy, research and operational decision-making across the sector. AFFIRMS is intended to establish a sustainable national approach to fire fatality and injury reporting, rather than develop a complex new technology platform.

The successful supplier will be expected to work with a range of jurisdictional stakeholders to build on existing project work, including outcomes from the feasibility study, stakeholder engagement activities and project governance arrangements. Experience in applied research, data governance, evaluation, evidence utilisation, public sector collaboration and multi-stakeholder projects will be highly regarded.

This Request is primarily seeking expertise in research, data governance, analysis and evidence utilisation. While technology may support the proposed approach, AFAC is not seeking a standalone software development or large-scale technology implementation project. Any proposed tools or platforms should be proportionate to the project objectives and capable of integrating with existing organisational processes and data sources where appropriate.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
Desired Outcomes

AFAC is seeking a supplier that can help establish a sustainable, nationally consistent approach to collecting, analysing and reporting fire fatality and injury data across Australia and New Zealand.

The successful proposal should demonstrate how it will:

Improve the consistency, quality and comparability of fire fatality and injury data across participating jurisdictions.

Support the development of practical governance arrangements, data standards and reporting processes that can be maintained over time.

Enable meaningful analysis and evidence generation to inform prevention, policy, research and operational decision-making.

Deliver recommendations that are practical, achievable and suitable for implementation across multiple agencies and jurisdictions.

Build stakeholder understanding, capability and ownership of the project outcomes.

Produce clear documentation and knowledge transfer materials to support long-term sustainability.

Highly Regarded

The following capabilities will be viewed favourably:

Experience working with government, emergency management, public safety, health or research sectors.

Expertise in data governance, evidence utilisation, program evaluation, applied research or national reporting frameworks.

Demonstrated experience facilitating collaboration across multiple organisations and stakeholders.

Understanding of injury surveillance, mortality reporting or other public sector data collections.

Ability to recommend proportionate technology or data management approaches that support, rather than drive, project outcomes.

Success Measures

Proposals will be assessed on their ability to:

Deliver practical and implementable outcomes.

Demonstrate a strong understanding of the project's strategic objectives.

Engage effectively with stakeholders.

Support long-term sustainability and sector adoption.

Provide value for money.

title: Expression of Interest - Mount Peter Sewer Rising Main
description:
The purpose of this EOI is to engage with industry prior to commencing the formal procurement process to better understand market capability, capacity, appetite and potential risks associated with the delivery of the Mount Peter Sewer Rising Main project.

The EOI will seek feedback on the proposed scope, delivery approach, packaging options, procurement strategy, risk allocation and social procurement requirements to ensure the project is structured in a manner that maximises competition, encourages innovation and delivers value for money. Information obtained through the EOI will be used to inform and refine the procurement strategy and tender documentation prior to release to market in FY27.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
Economic Development Queensland (EDQ) is the Queensland Government’s land use planning and property development agency. We embrace partnerships across government, industry and the community to deliver new residential communities, urban precincts and industrial ecosystems.

Backed by the Economic Development Act 2012, EDQ has unique planning and approval powers and a mandate to create private sector investment opportunities by de-risking and unlocking land for redevelopment. EDQ has planned and facilitated the delivery of some of the largest residential developments in Queensland, as well as some of the state’s most iconic urban renewal projects. We set benchmarks for the property industry through innovations and we’re creating jobs of the future in regional Queensland by unlocking land to promote priority industries, including clean energy and large-scale manufacturing.

We measure our success by the value we create in economic, social and environmental impacts. Over the last decade we have generated more than $3.7 billion in private sector investment and facilitated over $1 billion in trunk infrastructure for Queensland. EDQ focuses on achieving commercial outcomes for the state while delivering on government priorities.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
The Mount Peter Priority Development Area (PDA) was declared on 30 July 2025 and the Mount Peter PDA Interim Land Use Plan is now in effect.

The PDA covers approximately 2,650ha of land in the Southern Growth Corridor in the Cairns Regional Local Government Area. The area is bounded by the Wet Tropics World Heritage Area to the west, the Bruce Highway to the east and extends from the existing community of Edmonton in the north to Mackey Creek in the south.

The Mount Peter PDA was declared at the request of the Cairns Regional Council to provide a streamlined planning framework that accommodates the future housing needs of the Cairns region. The area is recognised as a future growth area in the Far North Queensland (FNQ) Regional Plan.

The Cairns South State Development Area (SDA) was declared in November 2018 as a special economic zone for regionally significant industrial development to support the long-term needs of the economy and create jobs in the Cairns region.

On 21 February 2020, the Cairns South SDA was varied to include an additional 303 hectares of land around the Mulgrave Mill to support the Mulgrave Mill’s future diversification plans, including industrial development opportunities that value-add to the sugar refining process.

The SDA is now a total of 1159 hectares over two separate areas at Wrights Creek and Gordonvale. The funding and building of infrastructure is key to facilitating development within PDA and SDA locations.

title: RFT2627-03 South Hedland Aquatics Facility Design Services
description:
The Town of Port Hedland is seeking a multidisciplinary design team to develop the Aquatic Centre and associated precinct through a traditional, linear design development process.

The proposed Aquatic Centre comprises approximately 1,250m² of internal accommodation and 4,390m² of external aquatic and recreation facilities, supported by a minimum of 420 car parking bays. The facility includes front-of-house functions such as reception and administration, flexible meeting and training spaces, a café, crèche, communications and cleaning facilities, and a comprehensive changing village incorporating family, accessible and Changing Places amenities. Operational areas include a pool office with oversight of all water bodies, a first aid room with direct pool and ambulance access, substantial internal and external storage, and dedicated wet and dry plant rooms. The external aquatic offering includes a 50m x 25m, 10-lane competition pool capable of supporting water polo, a 20m x 10m learn-to-swim warm water pool, a leisure water and splash play area, spectator facilities for approximately 200 people, extensive pool concourse areas, landscaped recreation space and associated parking infrastructure.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
Ipswich is centrally located in the booming south east Queensland region of Australia. To the east is the capital city Brisbane, and to the west are the rural and agricultural areas of the Brisbane, Lockyer and Fassifern Valleys. The city is ideally positioned on the national road network - 40 minutes drive from Brisbane, an hours drive from the Gold Coast and 60 minutes drive from domestic and international air and sea ports.
Ipswich comprises an area of 1090 square kms and has a population of 180,000 people. Ipswich enjoys a subtropical climate and is a safe, friendly and multicultural city. Residents come from 115 different ethnic backgrounds, speaking 84 languages.
As Queensland's oldest provincial city, Ipswich has a rich history. It is renowned for its architectural, natural and cultural heritage. Ipswich proudly preserves and still operates from many of its historical buildings and homes, with more than 6000 heritage-listed sites. Ipswich also has a range of charming townships within the western rural areas of the city, each with its own legitimate claims of historical significance.

publicQuestions.question:
Good afternoon,

1. We kindly ask for an extension of at least two weeks to the submission date.

2. Could the City please provide historical waste volumes for the ad hoc work for the (2025 calendar) year total volume, for: Ad Hoc Septic, Ad Hoc Oily Water and Hazardous Waste?

Thank you
publicQuestions.answer:
Council has received these questions and provides the following response:

Q1 - Council is unable to extend the closing date and time as it risks internal timelines to have a new contract commencement date aligned with the current contract expiry date.

Q2 - The requested historical volume information for Ad Hoc Septic, Ad Hoc Oily Water, and Hazardous Waste is not readily accessible in a consolidated format. To provide accurate annual volumes would require a detailed review of individual service records and invoices across multiple sites, which would be a significant exercise.

kind regards,

ICC

publicQuestions.question:
Clarification Request:

This relates to the Sewerage Pump Outs section (Tab #3) of Schedule 2 Appendix 2 – Asset Schedule & Price File.

Council's tender documentation refers to the services under Tab #3 as "Sewerage Pump Outs"; however, the asset schedule includes references to a mix of:

•	Holding tanks

•	Septic systems/septic to trench

•	Long drop toilets

•	Alarmed holding tanks

•	Various park and community facility wastewater systems

Could Council please clarify the following:

1.	Are the assets listed in Tab #3 classified as:

•	Sewerage waste;

•	Septic waste;

•	Grey water; or

•	A combination of these waste streams?

2.	For each listed asset, can Council confirm the expected waste composition and whether any solid components are anticipated within the waste stream?

3.	For alarmed services and holding tanks (e.g. College's Crossing and other alarmed assets), can Council provide any available historical pump-out volumes and servicing frequency data?

4.	Are there any assets within Tab #3 that receive waste from public amenities or facilities that may contain non-sewage materials or contaminants requiring special handling or disposal arrangements?

This information will assist tenderers in confirming the appropriate collection methodology, treatment/disposal pathway and pricing submission.
publicQuestions.answer:
Council has received these questions and provides the following response:

Q1 - the assets listed in Tab #3 classified as a combination of those waste streams (sewerage/septic/wastewater)

Q2 - As a guide, faecal matter 20%, urine and greywater 75%, paper and contaminants 5%

Q3 - Volume is stated as capacity in tab 3 - Colleges Crossing historically every 2-3 weeks - Henry Lawson Park – Scheduled Fortnightly, other services bi-annually.

Q4 - Yes, non-sewage including clothing, bottles, cans.

kind regards,

ICC

publicQuestions.question:
Good Morning,

Q1 - Can you please confirm the number of trained staff required or used historically to support the annual hazardous waste drop off day, including chemists?

Thank you
publicQuestions.answer:
Council has received this question and provides the following response:

Council advises that, currently, approximately five to six supplier personnel attend the Hazardous Waste Day, including at least one qualified chemist. This information is provided as a guide only and should not be interpreted as a requirement.

Tenderers are responsible for determining the appropriate resourcing of personnel necessary to safely and effectively deliver the services required for the event.

Should further information be required, please submit an additional clarification request through this portal.

kind regards,

ICC

publicQuestions.question: Site visits - Could we please have site visits to the sewerage pumpout sites in tab 3 of the RFT # 260316-000324 - Schedule 2 - Appendix 2 - Asset Schedule & Price File?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council has received this question and provides the following response:

Site visits - With the exception of the Willowbank listed sites and the Marburg SES site, all locations identified in the Request for Tender are publicly accessible and may be inspected by Tenderers without Council assistance.

Should access to Willowbank and/or Marburg SES be considered necessary for Tenderers to prepare and submit a tender, Council will consider arranging site visits to these locations only.

Kind regards,

ICC

kind regards,

ICC

publicQuestions.question:
Can a tenderer submit a response for only one scope of work. For example, can we tender for the GPT work, but not the household hazardous waste component?

Are the scopes separable?

Thanks
publicQuestions.answer:
Council has received this question and provides the following response:

Council will consider tenders for one or more separable portions of the works where the proposed solution represents value for money and meets Council's requirements.

Tenderers submitting for less than the full scope are still required to provide all information requested in the Request for Tender relevant to their proposed scope of works.

kind regards,

ICC

publicQuestions.question: Will the tender be awarded as a Panel for each separable portion or does council intend to only award each portion to one contractor?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council has received this question and provides the following response:

Council will consider tenders for one or more separable portions of the works where the proposed solution represents value for money and meets Council's requirements.

Tenderers submitting for less than the full scope are still required to provide all information requested in the Request for Tender relevant to their proposed scope of works.

kind regards,

ICC

publicQuestions.question: Are you able to clarify if multiple contractors will be awarded to each separable portion or will council only award one contractor per separable portion?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council will consider tenders for one or more separable portions of the works where the proposed solution represents value for money and meets Council's requirements.

Tenderers submitting for less than the full scope are still required to provide all information requested in the Request for Tender relevant to their proposed scope of works.

Per section 15 of the Request for tender document: Council may accept part or parts of a Tender or accept multiple Tenders and/or select multiple Tenderers as preferred Tenderers where the proposed solution represents value for money and meets Council's requirements.

Council is not in a position at this stage to advise how many tenders / contracts / suppliers will be awarded.

kind regards,

ICC
